areas.title: Blind re-derivation of the netlist

findings.title: Three supply pins have their decoupling capacitor 6 to 10 mm away
findings.refs: harmony-mark8-slab.kicad_pcb: U7 pin 10 (VSYS) nearest caps C16 100nF 6.30 mm, C15 1uF 6.37 mm, C10 7.51 mm; U3 pin 3 (VBAT) nearest C8 10uF 9.99 mm, C12 10.98 mm; J2 pin 10 (3V3_PERIPH) nearest C20 100nF 5.85 mm, C19 10uF 6.88 mm. Distances are pad centre to pad centre, computed from the board file (script: scratchpad/review-work/blind-netlist/pcbpads.py).
findings.evidence: The netlist has every capacitor I expected on these rails, but placement puts none of them next to the pin. For comparison, the other ICs have a capacitor at 1.2 to 3.7 mm: U2 V3 C2 1.75 mm, U4 VIN C10 1.72 mm, U6 VDD C13 1.49 mm, U1 3V3 C5 1.96 mm, J3 VDD C22 1.58 mm.
findings.requirement: DRV2605L SLOS854D sec 9 and 11.1: a 0.1 uF X5R/X7R bypass capacitor 'near the VDD supply pin', and the VDD decoupling capacitor 'placed close to the device pin'. MCP73831 DS20001984 p1 typical circuit: 4.7 uF on VBAT. SPEC 5.2: 10 uF and 100 nF on 3V3_PERIPH 'at the screen connector'.
findings.consequence: More supply ripple at the DRV2605L output stage when the optional motor runs, and less stability margin at the charger output with no battery fitted. The board will most likely still work.
findings.fix: For rev A, accept it. For rev B, move C15 or C16 next to U7 pins 10 and 8, move C8 (or add a 4.7 uF) next to U3 pin 3, and move C20 next to J2 pins 9 to 11.

findings.title: VBUS_SENSE puts about 3.0 V on GPIO36, above the ESP32 ADC accurate range
findings.refs: Net VBUS_SENSE: R29 100k (VBUS) / R30 150k (GND) to U1 pin 4 (I36). Firmware slab_analog.c line 15 uses ADC_ATTEN_DB_12. slab_analog.h: SLAB_VBUS_PRESENT_MV 4300, SLAB_D1_DROP_MV 350. slab_analog_math.c slab_vsys_estimate_mv() derives VSYS from the VBUS reading.
findings.evidence: At VBUS 5.0 to 5.25 V the pin sees 3.00 to 3.15 V. The 4.3 V presence threshold already puts 2.58 V on the pin.
findings.requirement: ESP32-PICO-MINI-02 datasheet v1.8 Table 10 note: with atten = 3, above about 2450 mV (raw 3000) the ADC accuracy is worse than specified.
findings.consequence: Presence detection still works. On USB the VBUS value, and so the VSYS estimate, can read low. The backlight duty and the R17 power cap are computed from that estimate, so on USB they are slightly off. The 80 percent USB duty cap limits the effect.
findings.fix: Firmware: on USB, use VBUS only as a yes/no and assume a nominal 5.0 V for the VSYS estimate. Rev B: change R30 to 68k (5.25 V gives 2.13 V at the pin) and update SLAB_VBUS_DIVIDER_X1000.

findings.title: Buzzer peak current can exceed the MLT-5020 100 mA maximum on USB
findings.refs: VSYS to R18 33R to BZ_P (BZ1 pin 1); BZ_N (BZ1 pin 2) to Q6 drain; D2 K=BZ_P, A=BZ_N.
findings.evidence: The coil is 12 ohm +-3 ohm. With VSYS about 4.7 V on USB: 4.7 / 45 ohm = 104 mA, and 112 mA with a 9 ohm coil. On battery at 4.2 V: 93 mA. The coil then sees only about 1.1 to 1.25 V.
findings.requirement: MLT-5020 spec (C94598) item 4: current max 100 mA; rated 3.0 Vo-p, operating 2 to 4 Vo-p.
findings.consequence: Short clicks at 50 percent duty will not damage the part. Sound output is below the rated SPL because the coil gets well under its rated drive.
findings.fix: No action for rev A. If the clicks are too quiet, lower R18 to about 22R, which keeps the peak under 100 mA on battery. If the USB peak is a concern, cap the firmware duty on USB.

findings.title: SPEC disagrees with itself about the MAX17048 supply; the netlist follows the datasheet version
findings.refs: U5 pin 3 VDD = /VBAT, pin 2 CELL = /VBAT, C12 1uF at 2.75 mm. SPEC 5.1 table U5: 'CELL and VDD on VBAT'. SPEC 5.2 bullet 4: '3V3 feeds U1, U5, U6'.
findings.evidence: The netlist puts VDD on VBAT. That matches SPEC 5.1 and the usual MAX17048 application, where VDD comes from the cell.
findings.requirement: MAX17048 VDD range is 2.5 to 4.5 V and is normally supplied from the cell. This is from memory: the LCSC file is a stub and the analog.com download timed out.
findings.consequence: No hardware effect. A later reader of SPEC 5.2 could 'fix' it the wrong way.
findings.fix: Correct SPEC 5.2 to say U5 is powered from VBAT.

findings.title: CH9102F VIO is on 3V3, not on VBUS as the SPEC wording says; this is the correct WCH scheme
findings.refs: U2 pin 5 VIO = /3V3 (C3 100nF at 2.56 mm); pin 7 VDD5 and pin 8 VBUS = /VBUS (C25 at 3.69 mm); pin 6 V3 = C2 only. SPEC 5.1: 'Power it from VBUS so it draws nothing on battery.'
findings.evidence: On battery, VDD5 and V3 are at 0 V while VIO stays at 3V3.
findings.requirement: CH9102 datasheet v1.4 sec 5.2: VIO should share the MCU supply (recommended dual-supply scheme). When V3 and VDD5 are at 0 V, VIO draws no current and does not back-feed them. Suspend VIO current is about 2 uA.
findings.consequence: This meets the SPEC intent of no battery draw and avoids back-powering the CH9102 through the 1k UART resistors. It is the better choice than VIO on V3.
findings.fix: None. Optionally reword SPEC 5.1 to 'VDD5 from VBUS, VIO from 3V3'.

findings.title: RTS may read as externally pulled down at CH9102 power-up, which disables its EEPROM settings
findings.refs: /RTS = U2 pin 19, Q1 pin 1 (Tr1 emitter) and Q1 pin 5 (Tr2 base through the internal 4.7k). Q1 pin 4 (Tr2 emitter) = /DTR = U2 pin 23.
findings.evidence: From RTS, the path through the 4.7k base resistor and the Tr2 base-emitter junction ends at DTR. If DTR is low or not yet driven when the chip samples RTS, that path looks like a pull-down.
findings.requirement: CH9102 datasheet v1.4 sec 4, RTS row: if an external pull-down is detected on RTS during power-up, the chip ignores the internal EEPROM configuration and uses its built-in defaults.
findings.consequence: At worst the chip enumerates with the default VID/PID and strings. Serial and auto-reset still work. This board does not program the EEPROM.
findings.fix: None needed. Worth knowing if the USB descriptor ever looks different from what is expected.

findings.title: Screen VCC and IOVCC run at the top of their operating range
findings.refs: J2 pins 9, 10, 11 = /3V3_PERIPH, switched by Q4 from the U4 RT9080-33 output.
findings.evidence: The RT9080 output is 3.3 V +-2 percent, so 3.23 to 3.37 V. The Q4 drop is a few mV.
findings.requirement: DLC-T2.7DDS#1 spec v1.0 p6: VCC 2.4 to 3.3 V max and IOVCC 1.65 to 3.3 V max (operating); p5 absolute maximum 4.6 V for both.
findings.consequence: Up to about 70 mV over the recommended maximum, but far inside the absolute maximum. This is usual practice for ST77xx-class panels and SPEC section 3 chose it.
findings.fix: None.

checked: Wrote the blind expected list before opening design.py, the schematic, netlist.xml or README.md: scratchpad/review-work/blind-netlist/expected.md. Inputs were SPEC.md, bom.csv, slab_pins.h, slab_power_seq.c and the datasheets.
netlist.xml is current: re-exported from a scratch copy of the schematic with kicad-cli 8.0.9. Both have 358 (ref, pin, net) triples, with no difference.

Board matches netlist: every pad net in harmony-mark8-slab.kicad_pcb equals the netlist (0 mismatches over 101 footprints). drc.json (2026-11-17 20:10, same time as the .kicad_pcb) has 0 unconnected items and 0 schematic-parity errors. erc.json has no violations.

No named net has only one connection. All 27 single-node nets are intentional no-connects: U1 pins 5, 19, 25, 32; U2 pins 1, 9-18, 22, 24; U4 pin 4; U5 ALRT; U6 ELE9-11; J1 SBU1/SBU2; J4 mounting tabs; BZ1 pad 3.

U1 ESP32-PICO-MINI-02, all 53 pins, against datasheet v1.8 Table 3. Every GPIO-to-net assignment matches SPEC 5.3 and slab_pins.h. GND on 1, 2, 11, 14, 36-53 (49 is the 3x3 EPAD). The footprint pad order (1-11 left, 12-24 bottom, 25-35 right, 36-48 top) matches Fig. 3.

U1 straps: GPIO0 R6 10k to 3V3 + SW2; GPIO2 has 100R + R20 100k to GND (stays low); GPIO12 unconnected (internal pull-down keeps the flash at 3.3 V); GPIO15 R25 100k pull-up + card-detect switch to GND; GPIO5 is SD_SCK and idles unloaded because the card is unpowered at boot. EN: R5 10k / C4 1uF per datasheet sec 9.
UART crossover: GPIO1 TXD0, R3 1k, U2 pin 20 RXD; U2 pin 21 TXD, R4 1k, GPIO3 RXD0. Test pads TP5 and TP6 are on the ESP32 side.
Q1 UMH3N pin functions match the CJ datasheet diagram (Tr1 E1/B2/C6, Tr2 E4/B5/C3). Tr1: B=DTR, E=RTS, C=ESP_EN. Tr2: B=RTS, E=DTR, C=BOOT. This is the standard esptool auto-reset.

U2 CH9102F QFN24 pin map against WCH datasheet v1.4 sec 4: UD+ pin 3 = USB_DP and UD- pin 4 = USB_DN with no series resistors; VDD5 and VBUS on VBUS; V3 C2 only; EPAD pad 25 and pin 2 to GND; RST floats on its internal pull-up; modem inputs float (internal pull-ups per sec 5.2).

J1 USB-C: CC1 (A5) to R1 5.1k and CC2 (B5) to R2 5.1k, separate resistors to GND; D+ A6/B6, D- A7/B7; VBUS on both pin pairs; GND and the shell to GND. Pad order matches the standard HRO TYPE-C-31-M-12 land.
U8 USBLC6-2SC6 against the ST datasheet p1: pins 1/6 = USB_DN, 3/4 = USB_DP, 5 = VBUS, 2 = GND.

U3 MCP73831 SOT-23-5 pins 1 STAT, 2 VSS, 3 VBAT, 4 VDD (VBUS, C7 4.7uF), 5 PROG. R7 2.7k gives IREG = 1000 V / 2.7k = 370 mA (DS20001984 electrical table, RPROG 2-67k). LED1 is on 1k from VBUS (about 3 mA) with its cathode on STAT.
U4 RT9080-33GJ5 TSOT-23-5 (DS9080-05 p1-2): 1 VIN = VSYS, 3 EN = VSYS (not floating), 2 GND, 4 NC (fixed version), 5 VOUT = 3V3. Cin C10 1uF at 1.7 mm, Cout C11 1uF at 3.7 mm plus C5 22uF.

Power path FET pins against AO3401A/AO3400A SOT-23 (1 G, 2 S, 3 D). Q2: D=BAT_P, S=VBAT, G=GND, correct reverse protection. Q3: D=VBAT, S=VSYS, G=VBUS with R9 100k to GND, correct load sharing (Vgs about +0.3 V on USB, body diode reverse-biased). D1: K=VSYS, A=VBUS (SOD-123 silk bar on pad 1).
Q4: S=3V3, D=3V3_PERIPH, gate has R13 100k to 3V3 and R14 10k from GPIO13. C18 100nF goes gate to source (3V3), so Q4 stays off at power-up. Turn-on time constant is 10k x 100nF = 1 ms.

Q5 backlight: D=LEDK (J2-1), S=GND, G has 100R from GPIO4 and R16 100k to GND. LEDA (J2-14/15) gets R17 10R 1206 from VSYS. The firmware power cap (slab_backlight.h, 231 mW, 80 percent on USB) handles the R17 0.25 W rating.
Q6, BZ1, D2: VSYS to 33R to BZ1 '+' (pad 1); BZ1 '-' to Q6 drain; flyback K on BZ_P. The footprint's NC pad 3 sits at the chamfered-corner pad position in the MLT-5020 bottom-view drawing.
U5 MAX17048 pin functions in the symbol agree with my independent pin list: CTG, QSTRT, GND and EP to GND; CELL and VDD to VBAT; ALRT open; SCL/SDA on the bus.

U6 MPR121 against Rev 4 Table 1: ADDR to 3V3 gives 0x5B, so no clash with DRV2605L 0x5A or MAX17048 0x36. VREG has its own C14 100nF (needed because VDD is 3.3 V, above 2.75 V). REXT is R10 75k to GND. VDD C13 at 1.5 mm. IRQ has R11 10k to 3V3 and goes to GPIO34. ELE9-11 float.

Touch wheel E1: ELE0 = centre; ELE1-ELE8 anchor pads map, through the SPEC 1 transform (device_x = -(kx - 150)), to 12, 1:30, 3, 4:30, 6, 7:30, 9 and 10:30 o'clock. That is clockwise from 12 o'clock as seen from the front, per SPEC 4.
U7 DRV2605L VSSOP-10 against SLOS854D p5: 1 REG C17 1uF; 4 IN/TRIG to GND; 5 EN through R12 10k to 3V3; 6 VDD/NC and 10 VDD on VSYS (max 5.2 V, above VSYS on USB); 7/9 to M1/M2 motor pads; 8 GND.

J2 FH35C, all 15 contacts match the DLC-T2.7DDS#1 spec pin table. TE to GPIO39, SDA to GPIO27, SCLK to GPIO14, RS to GPIO33, CS to GPIO26, RESET to GPIO32, IOVCC/VCC to 3V3_PERIPH, GND on 2/12/13, mounting tabs to GND.

J3 DM3AT: pads 1-8 match the Hirose catalog p3 contact order (DAT2, CD/DAT3, CMD, VDD, CLK, VSS, DAT0, DAT1). Detect switch B (pad 9, next to DAT1) goes to GND and A (pad 11, left side) to SD_CD, matching the drawing. DAT0/CS/DAT1/DAT2 pull-ups (R21-R24 10k) go to 3V3_PERIPH, not 3V3, so they do not back-power the card.

SW1 SKRTLAE010: per the Alps circuit diagram, terminals 1 and 3 are common and 2 is the moving contact. The netlist puts SIDE_BTN on centre pad 2 and GND on 1/3, which is correct; it is not shorted. SIDE_BTN has R26 100k to 3V3 and C23 100nF. SW2 is BOOT to GND and SW3 is EN to GND.
Footprint pad numbering for SOT-363, SOT-23-5, TSOT-23-5, SOT-23, SOT-23-6, TDFN-8, VSSOP-10, QFN-20, QFN-24 matches the datasheet pin-1 corner and counter-clockwise order.
BOM count against the expected budget: 6 x 1uF, 12 x 100nF, 9 x 10k, 7 x 100k, 3 x 1k and all single values match one-for-one with an expected function.
Test pads TP1-TP10 are on exactly the SPEC 6 nets (3V3, VSYS, VBAT, GND, U0TXD, U0RXD, GPIO7, GPIO8, I2C_SDA, I2C_SCL).
Panel SPI clock: the DLC spec gives TSCYCW min 66 ns (15 MHz). Firmware defaults to 40 MHz, but the Kconfig help already documents this and gives a fallback, so I did not raise it as new.
not_checked: MAX17048 datasheet: the LCSC file C2682616.pdf is an HTML stub. Downloads from analog.com (HTTP/2 errors and timeouts), maximintegrated, Adafruit and SparkFun mirrors and lcsc.com/datasheet all failed (scratchpad/review-datasheets/dl-max17048 holds only HTML). The pin map and the 0.1 uF VDD bypass are from memory; my list and the design agree.
