FH35C contact current rating: the Hirose PDF is drawings with no extractable text. LEDK carries up to about 170 mA through the single contact on pin 1, and I could not confirm that against the rating.

LED1 polarity on the JLC part: the EasyEDA 0603 silk (chamfer on the pad 2 side) suggests pad 2 is the cathode, which agrees with the netlist. I did not confirm it against the JLC library model or C2286 datasheet.
J4 battery polarity (pin 1 = -, pin 2 = +) against the specific battery Dave will buy: there is no universal JST PH convention.
Physical FPC pin order through the 180 degree fold, and the J2 pin 1 end of the slot: this is mechanical, not netlist.
ESP32 GPIO13 internal pull state during reset, and whether it fights R13 100k: the ESP32 series IO_MUX table is not in the provided module datasheet.
Land-pattern dimensions, paste, keep-outs, antenna clearance, trace widths, thermal relief and rotation/CPL correctness: outside the blind-netlist area. I checked only pad order and positions.
Unplug transient (VBUS decay through R9 while Q3 is still off, VSYS briefly on the Q3 body diode): reasoned about but not simulated. It is the same topology as the Feather V2.

verdicts.reasoning:
I measured this myself. I parsed harmony-mark8-slab.kicad_pcb (pad positions with rotation, then a shortest path along the routed segments and vias of each net, with T-junctions handled; scripts in scratchpad/review-work/blind-netlist-verify/pads.py and path.py). I could not refute any of the three points, but they are not equally strong.
(1) U7 DRV2605L: VDD pins 10 (174.2,106.35) and 6 (176.2,106.35) are joined by a 0.2 mm track at y 105.42. That track meets the VSYS trunk at a via at (171.09,106.39). C16 100nF and C15 1uF sit at the end of an 8.6 mm L3 stub beyond that junction (via at 173.42,113.33). The track from pin 10 to C16 is 13.2 mm, from pin 10 to C15 is 16.0 mm, and from pin 6 to C16 is 15.2 mm. The straight-line figures are right: 6.30 and 6.37 mm. The datasheet does require this: SLOS854D, pin table, pin 10 VDD, 'A 1-uF capacitor is required'; sec 9.2.2.2, the 0.1 uF bypass goes 'near the VDD supply pin' because the switching output stage draws transient current through VDD; sec 10 and 11.1 say to place it close to the device pin. The values are present but the placement is not. The motor is optional, so without one this costs nothing.
(2) U3 MCP73831: this is worse than reported. U3 pin 3 reaches Q2 pin 2 after 6.2 mm, then runs through two vias and L3 to Q3, and only then reaches C8 10uF, 28.7 mm of track in all. C12 is 31.4 mm away. DS20001984G sec 3.2 says to bypass VBAT to VSS with a minimum of 4.7 uF 'to ensure loop stability when the battery is disconnected', and sec 6.1.1.4 says the same. The capacitance is present but sits behind roughly 20 to 25 nH of track. This is still small next to the battery-lead inductance the datasheet says the capacitor must compensate for, so it is a margin issue, not a defect. It matters only with no battery fitted (USB-only bench use).
(3) J2: I do not support this part. The pin 10 figure (5.85 mm) is right, but pins 9 and 11 are on the same net, and C20 is 3.51 mm (4.4 mm of track) from pin 11 and 4.01 mm from pin 9. That meets SPEC 5.2 'at the screen connector', and the panel's FPC tail adds far more length than this anyway.
I also found a related point the reviewer did not raise: the U3 VDD (pin 4) bypass C7 4.7uF is 10.0 mm of track away (5.43 mm straight). It is a minor issue of the same kind (DS sec 3.1, 'Bypass to VSS with a minimum of 4.7 uF').
Checked and correct: the net membership of every capacitor named here (netlist.xml); C11 is 4.5 mm of track from U4 VOUT; C22 is 1.58 mm from J3 VDD; C12 is 2.75 mm from U5 VDD.
verdicts.fix: Rev A: order as is. On the first board, if the charge LED flickers or VBAT rings with no battery fitted, solder a 4.7 uF 0402 or 0603 across U3 pins 3 and 2. They are adjacent SOT-23-5 pins, 0.95 mm apart. If a motor is fitted and the DRV2605L resets or misbehaves, tack a 1 uF from the U7 VDD track (pin 10 or 6) to C17 pad 2 (GND, 172.6,107.92). Rev B: put C15 and C16 within 1 to 2 mm of U7 pins 10 and 6, on the pin side of the trunk junction. Put a 4.7 to 10 uF capacitor directly at U3 pin 3, and move C7 next to U3 pin 4. No change is needed at J2.

verdicts.reasoning:
netlist.xml: /VBUS_SENSE = R29 pin 2 (100k to VBUS), R30 pin 1 (150k to GND), U1 pin 4 (I36). The pin voltage is VBUS x 0.6, so 5.0 V gives 3.00 V, 5.25 V gives 3.15 V, and 4.3 V gives 2.58 V. Firmware slab_analog.c lines 15 and 19 use ADC_ATTEN_DB_12 with line-fitting calibration (default_vref 1100). The ESP32-PICO-MINI-02 datasheet v1.8 p25, Table 10 note, says that with atten = 3 and a result above 3000 (about 2450 mV), accuracy is worse than specified. Table 11 gives the calibrated range for atten 3 as 150 to 2450 mV (+-60 mV). So every USB reading lies outside the specified range. Pins near 3.1 V can also reach raw 4095 and clip.
I traced the effect: slab_vsys_estimate_mv() subtracts 350 mV from the VBUS reading. A low reading lowers full_ma in slab_bl_plan(), which raises the duty and also raises the R17 power cap. The error therefore makes the backlight brighter on USB, not dimmer. At 100 percent brightness the duty is about 46 to 53 percent (78 mA reference against about 150 to 170 mA full current), below the 800 permille USB cap and the 231 mW R17 cap. A 250 mV underestimate gives about 15 percent more brightness, and R17 stays near 150 mW. So the result is a small brightness mismatch, not overstress. Presence detection at 4300 mV (2.58 V at the pin) is reliable enough for a yes/no. The pin voltage stays under VDD3P3_RTC, so the pin is not at risk.
verdicts.fix: Firmware (rev A): on USB, treat VBUS_SENSE as presence only and use a fixed 5000 mV in slab_vsys_estimate_mv() (VSYS about 4650 mV). Rev B: R30 68k (0603 basic). Then 5.25 V gives 2.13 V and 4.3 V gives 1.74 V. Set SLAB_VBUS_DIVIDER_X1000 to 2471.

verdicts.reasoning: The netlist matches the topology: R18 33R from VSYS to BZ_P (BZ1 pin 1), BZ1 pin 2 and Q6 drain on BZ_N, D2 K = BZ_P, A = BZ_N. The firmware drives 4000 Hz at 50 percent duty (slab_buzzer.c, CONFIG_SLAB_CLICK_HZ and CONFIG_SLAB_CLICK_DUTY_PCT). The arithmetic is right: 4.7 V / 45 ohm is about 104 mA, but only as a DC steady state. The datasheet does not support reading 100 mA as a damage limit. In the MLT-5020 spec (C94598) section 1, item 4 'current Max 100mA' sits beside item 3 under the test condition 'Standard Drive Circuit, Rated voltage, Distance 0.1m': it is the consumption at rated drive (3.0 Vo-p, 1/2 duty square wave per section 2), not an absolute maximum. This circuit puts about 1.1 to 1.25 V on the coil, well under the rated 3.0 Vo-p. Coil dissipation is about (0.104 A)^2 x 12 ohm x 0.5, roughly 65 mW, which is less stress than the rated condition. Coil inductance at 4 kHz also keeps the peak below the DC figure. There is no overstress. The point about sound level is valid: the drive is below the 2 to 4 Vo-p operating range, so SPL will be below the 75 dB minimum. That is a loudness question, not a rating violation.
verdicts.fix: None for overstress. If clicks are too quiet on the first board, lower R18 to 22R or 15R (0805). Coil voltage then rises to about 1.6 to 2.0 V, still inside the rated drive.

verdicts.reasoning: netlist.xml: /VBAT includes U5 pin 2 (CELL) and pin 3 (VDD), plus C12 1uF (2.75 mm straight). SPEC.md line 99 (5.1 table, U5) says 'CELL and VDD on VBAT'. SPEC.md line 126 (5.2 bullet 4) says '3V3 feeds U1, U5, U6 and Q4', which contradicts it. I downloaded the MAX17048/MAX17049 datasheet (scratchpad/review-datasheets/dl-max17048/max17048.pdf, 1.1 MB, a full copy, extracted with pdftotext). It settles the question: pin 3 VDD is the 'voltage sense input. Connect to positive battery terminal', pin 2 CELL is 'not internally connected' on the MAX17048, and VDD is 2.5 to 4.5 V in the electrical characteristics. VBAT is at most 4.2 V, inside that range. The netlist is correct. README line 91 already words it as 'U5 logic side through the I2C pull-ups', so only the SPEC text is wrong.
verdicts.fix: Edit SPEC 5.2 bullet 4 to: '3V3 feeds U1, U6 and Q4 (and the I2C pull-ups). U5 is powered from VBAT.' No hardware change.

verdicts.reasoning: netlist.xml: U2 pin 5 VIO is on /3V3. Pins 7 (VDD5) and 8 (VBUS) are on /VBUS. C2 is on V3 and C3 100nF is on VIO, 2.56 mm straight. The CH9102 datasheet V1.4 sec 5.2 says VIO should share the MCU supply, and that VIO draws no current and does not back-feed VDD5 or V3 when they are at 0 V. It recommends the dual-supply scheme, with VIO at 2 uA in suspend. The VBUS pin abs max is 6.5 V (sec 6.1), so tying pin 8 directly to VBUS is fine. README.md line 93 and the deviations table at line 273 already document this as a deliberate departure from the SPEC 5.1 wording, with the same reasoning. The design is correct and the deviation is recorded.
verdicts.fix: None. Optionally reword SPEC 5.1 U2 to 'VDD5 and VBUS from USB VBUS, VIO from 3V3'.

verdicts.reasoning: The topology is as stated (netlist.xml). /RTS = U2 pin 19, Q1 pin 1 (E1) and Q1 pin 5 (B2). /DTR = U2 pin 23, Q1 pin 2 (B1) and Q1 pin 4 (E2). UMH3N R1 = 4.7k (C62892 datasheet, input resistance 3.29 to 6.11 k). Nothing else is on RTS, so there is no real pull-down resistor. CH9102 V1.4 pin table (QFN24 pin 19): if an external pull-down is detected on RTS during power-up, the chip ignores the EEPROM settings and uses its built-in defaults. The only path that could look like a pull-down is RTS through 4.7k and the Tr2 base-emitter junction to DTR, and only if DTR is low while RTS is sampled. On this board VIO (3V3) is already up when VBUS arrives. The datasheet gives 15 to 90 uA pull-ups to VIO on the serial pins (sec 6.2, IPUP) but does not say what DTR does during the sampling window. If DTR floats high or is held high, the path does not conduct and RTS reads high. I cannot settle this from the documents. It also does not matter on this board: the EEPROM is not programmed, so the default parameters and the EEPROM parameters give the same descriptor. Serial and auto-reset work either way. The SPEC copies the circuit from the Feather V2, which uses the same arrangement.
verdicts.fix: None. On the first board, check the enumerated VID/PID and strings (1A86:55D4 expected). Act only if the EEPROM is ever customised.

verdicts.reasoning: netlist.xml: J2 pin 9 (IOVCC) and pins 10 and 11 (VCC) are on /3V3_PERIPH, which is Q4 drain. Q4 source is /3V3, the output of U4 RT9080-33 (pin 5). C841192 datasheet: +-2 percent output accuracy, so 3.234 to 3.366 V. The DLC-T2.7DDS#1 spec v1.0 p6 'Electrical characteristics' gives VCC 2.4 / 2.75 / 3.3 V and IOVCC 1.65 / 1.8 / 3.3 V (min / typ / max). The p5 absolute maximum is 4.6 V for both. The Q4 AO3401A drop at about 15 mA panel current plus card current is a few mV. Worst case, the panel is about 66 mV over its recommended maximum and more than 1.2 V under its absolute maximum. SPEC.md line 46 chose this rail on purpose. The ESP32 drives the SPI lines at 3.3 V, so a lower IOVCC would create a VIH problem; 3.3 V is the right choice. This is harmless.
verdicts.fix: None.

areas.title: Power and charging circuits

findings.title: Q4 soft start does not slow the 3V3_PERIPH turn-on: about 0.1 ms rise with a 0.6 to 1.0 A inrush, not the 1 ms ramp the README states
findings.refs: design.py Q4 (AO3401A, S=3V3, D=3V3_PERIPH, G=PERIPH_GATE), R13 100k 3V3-gate, R14 10k PERIPH_EN_N-gate, C18 100 nF gate-3V3; README.md Power bullet 5 ('about a 1 ms turn-on ramp'); firmware slab_power_seq.h SLAB_PERIPH_RAMP_MS; 3V3_PERIPH load C19+C21 10 uF 0603 plus C20/C22, the screen and the card
findings.evidence: The gate RC time constant is (10k||100k) x 100 nF = 0.9 ms. But the FET goes from off to fully on across only about 0.3 V of gate swing near Vth (-0.5 to -1.3 V), and C18 sits gate-to-source, so it does not limit dV/dt at the drain the way a gate-drain (Miller) capacitor would. A square-law model (AO3401A Rds(on) 60 mOhm at -2.5 V, gFS 17 S, Vth -0.5/-0.9/-1.3 V, 18 uF effective load) gives a 3V3_PERIPH 10-90 % rise of 80 to 135 us and a peak current of 0.6 to 1.0 A (script: review-work/power-ics/q4_rise.py). With the RT9080 at its typical 1.1 A current limit, 3V3 dips only to about 3.17 to 3.26 V. With the guaranteed minimum limit of 610 mA and 250 mA of ESP32 load, the model gives 2.3 to 2.5 V, near the level-0 brownout (sdkconfig CONFIG_ESP_BROWNOUT_DET_LVL=0). Near Q4 only C11 (1 uF) is local: C5 22 uF is about 0.22 ohm of track away (computed U4.5 to U1.3 path, 108 mm, half on L3).
findings.requirement: RT9080 DS9080-05 p.4: ILIM 610 mA min / 1100 mA typ. ESP32-PICO-MINI-02 datasheet v1.8 Table 14: VDD33 3.0 V minimum. AO3401A datasheet p.1: Vth -0.5 to -1.3 V, Ciss 645 pF, Crss 55 pF.
findings.consequence: Each 3V3_PERIPH turn-on (boot and every wake) can pull the 3.3 V rail below the ESP32's 3.0 V minimum. On a low-limit RT9080 with Bluetooth running, it can cause a brownout reset. At boot (load about 80 mA) the model stays above brownout but goes below 3.0 V on a low-limit part.
findings.fix: Before ordering, change C18 from 100 nF to 1 uF. The 1 uF 0402 part C52923 is already on the BOM, so there is no new feeder. The model then gives a 0.36 to 0.47 ms rise, a 0.18 to 0.24 A peak and 3V3 above 3.29 V in all cases (q4_c18.py). Turn-off becomes about 10 ms, which does no harm. As an alternative, add 10 to 47 nF from gate to drain. Firmware workaround: turn 3V3_PERIPH on only while Bluetooth is off. Fix the README sentence either way.

findings.title: A reversed battery pack is not blocked while USB is connected: Q2 turns on and the pack drains at about 37 mA, and the charge LED shows 'charging'
findings.refs: design.py Q2 AO3401A {1 G: GND, 2 S: VBAT, 3 D: BAT_P}; J4 pin 1 GND, pin 2 BAT_P; U3 MCP73831 VBAT on VBAT; README 'Check before paying' 5 and ASSEMBLY.md step 11 ('The board blocks a reversed pack')
findings.evidence: Reversed pack with USB present: J4 pin 1 (board GND, 0 V) gets pack +, so BAT_P = -3.7 V. The charger output drives VBAT up from 0 V (6 uA detect current, then 10 % precondition current because VBAT < VPTH 2.79 V). Once VBAT is about 1 V, Q2's Vgs = 0 - VBAT reaches Vth and Q2 conducts from VBAT into BAT_P, which is the pack's negative terminal. That current runs through the cell in its discharge direction. VBAT then settles near 1 V with Q2 in linear mode, carrying the 37 mA precondition current. Q2 dissipates about (1 + 3.7) V x 37 mA = 0.17 W, and the cell supplies about 0.14 W. The MCP73831 has no safety timer, and STAT stays low, so LED1 is on. Without USB the README claim holds: VBAT is about 0, Vgs = 0, and the body diode is reverse-biased.
findings.requirement: MCP73831 DS20001984G section 4.4 (preconditioning at IPREG while VBAT < VPTH, option AC: 10 %, 66.5 %) and Fig. 4-1 flowchart (no timer). AO3401A Vth -0.5 to -1.3 V.
findings.consequence: A reversed pack left on USB is discharged until its protection circuit cuts off, about 30 h for a 1100 mAh pack, while the LED says it is charging. A protected pack (SPEC 10) survives. An unprotected pack would be over-discharged. The README and ASSEMBLY claim that the board blocks a reversed pack is true only without USB.
findings.fix: Keep the meter check in ASSEMBLY step 11, and correct the wording ('blocks a reversed pack on battery power only; with USB connected a reversed pack is slowly discharged'). Add a firmware check: if VBUS is present and VBAT_SENSE stays below about 2 V for more than 10 s, show 'battery reversed' and refuse to sleep. A hardware fix is not worth a re-spin for revision A.

findings.title: The VBUS path from J1 to U3 and D1 is about 0.31 to 0.35 ohm, not about 0.1 ohm, and carries more than the 500 mA that the accepted exception assumes
findings.refs: README 'Touch-wheel re-route' step C VBUS paragraph ('all the narrow track adds about 0.1 ohm... At the 500 mA USB limit'); design.py VBUS_PATH_ACCEPTED; jlcpcb/ORDER.md 'Inner copper weight 0.5 oz'; computed with review-work/power-ics/pathres2.py on harmony-mark8-slab.kicad_pcb
findings.evidence: Least-resistance track path, J1.A4B9 to U3.4: 140 mm in total. It is L1 0.4 mm 26.3 mm, L1 0.3 mm 27.2 mm, L1 0.2 mm 9.6 mm, L3 0.4 mm 63.2 mm and L3 0.3 mm 13.9 mm, with 8 vias, for R = 0.35 ohm at 35 um outer / 17.5 um inner. J1.B4A9 to D1.2 is 0.31 ohm. The README counts only the track narrower than 0.4 mm and does not count the 63 mm of 0.4 mm track on 0.5 oz L3, which alone is about 0.155 ohm. VBUS current is not capped at 500 mA. The charger takes 370 mA, and the system on D1 takes about 150 mA (3V3) plus up to 161 mA (backlight). That is about 0.65 A on average while charging and playing with the screen on, and about 1.1 A at peak with the buzzer and haptic. IPC-2221 (inner, conservative) puts 0.4 mm of 0.5 oz track at about 0.37 A for a 10 K rise.
findings.requirement: Exception reasoning in README step C. MCP73831 recommends VDD of at least VREG + 0.3 V = 4.5 V (DS20001984G section 3.1). USB 2.0 allows the device-side VBUS to fall to about 4.4 V after the cable.
findings.consequence: On USB, VBUS falls by about 0.2 V on average (0.35 V at peak). VSYS on USB is then about 4.3 to 4.4 V, not 4.6 to 4.7 V. With a weak source (4.75 V at the port, a long cable), U3 VDD can fall below 4.5 V. The charger still works but leaves less headroom in constant-voltage mode. The L3 VBUS run also heats the board under the wheel. The board works, but the accepted exception rests on numbers that are too low.
findings.fix: If JLC offers it for 4 layers at 0.8 mm, order 1 oz inner copper. That halves the L3 part, to about 0.23 ohm in total. Otherwise, accept the exception with the corrected numbers in the README, and on the first board measure VBUS at U3 pin 4 while charging with the screen at full brightness. Lowering the charge current (see PWR-4) also cuts the drop.

findings.title: MCP73831 in SOT-23-5 dissipates about 0.45 to 1.0 W at 370 mA, so it will run in thermal regulation inside the closed case, beside the PLA front skin
findings.refs: U3 MCP73831T-2ACI/OT at device (-24.6, -21.9), R7 2.7k; U4 RT9080, D1 and R17 in the same left column; board L4 against the PLA front skin (SPEC 6)
findings.evidence: Pd = (VDD - VBAT) x IREG. At VDD 4.8 V (after the PWR-3 drop) and VBAT 3.6 V: 1.2 x 0.37 = 0.44 W. The datasheet worst case (6.1.1.3: VDDmax - VPTHmin) is (5.25 - 2.67) x 0.41 = 1.0 W. Package theta-JA is 230 C/W on a JEDEC 4-layer board, about 130 C/W with large copper. That gives a junction rise of 57 to 100 K at 0.44 W, plus a case interior at about 35 to 45 C, with U4 (about 0.2 W on USB), D1 (about 0.15 W) and R17 (up to 0.23 W) next to it. Microchip states that the SOT-23-5 enters thermal regulation at these levels (section 6.1.1.3, Fig. 4-2) and suggests the DFN.
findings.requirement: MCP73831 DS20001984G: theta-JA 230 C/W (SOT-23-5, 4-layer JC51-7), TSD 150 C, section 6.1.1.3 and Fig. 4-2 thermal regulation.
findings.consequence: Charging slows (current folds back), and the top-left of the board runs hot, directly against the PLA front skin (glass transition about 55 to 60 C). There is no battery temperature sensing. The charger is safe (thermal regulation, TSD), but the enclosure and charge time are at risk.
findings.fix: Before ordering, consider lowering the charge current to about 210 mA (RPROG 4.7k 0603, check that it is a JLC basic part). That is still 0.16 to 0.19C, about 6 h to full, and it also reduces PWR-3 and PWR-10. Otherwise, on the first board measure the board temperature under U3 with a thermocouple while charging an empty pack with the screen on. Print the front shell in PETG if it exceeds about 50 C.

findings.title: On USB unplug, VSYS runs on the Q3 body diode until VBUS bleeds down through R9, so 3V3 falls below 3.0 V when the battery is below about 3.8 V
findings.refs: Q3 AO3401A {G: VBUS, S: VSYS, D: VBAT}, R9 100k VBUS-GND, R29+R30 250k VBUS-GND, C1 10 uF + C7 4.7 uF + C25 on VBUS, D1 B5819W
findings.evidence: After unplug, the loads pull VBUS down to about VSYS + 0.3 V, then D1 stops conducting. VSYS falls to VBAT - VSD(Q3 body diode, about 0.7 V). Q3's channel only turns on when its gate (VBUS) falls below VBAT - |Vth| (about VBAT - 0.9 V) and is fully on at about VBAT - 2.5 V. From then on, VBUS is discharged only by R9 || (R29+R30) = 71 kOhm, with U3 in UVLO drawing 1 to 5 uA and U2 drawing an unknown current. That is tau = 71k x about 11 uF effective = about 0.8 s, so the body-diode window can last tens to hundreds of ms. During it, 3V3 at U1 is about VBAT - 0.7 - LDO drop - 0.03 V of track, about VBAT - 0.8 V: 2.9 V at VBAT 3.7 V, and 2.5 V at 3.3 V (near the level-0 brownout). Plug-in has the same window, but only for the VBUS rise time (sub-ms).
findings.requirement: AO3401A VSD 0.7 V typ / 1 V max (p.2), Vth -0.5 to -1.3 V. ESP32-PICO-MINI-02 VDD33 3.0 V minimum (Table 14). The SD card needs 2.7 V or more.
findings.consequence: Pulling the cable during playback at mid-to-low charge can put the ESP32, PSRAM and card below their supply minimum for up to about 0.1 to 0.5 s. That can cause a brownout reset or a corrupted card or NVS write. The firmware has no guard.
findings.fix: Cheapest: R9 100k to 10k (0.5 mA from VBUS only while plugged in), which brings tau to about 0.1 s. Better: a Schottky in parallel with Q3 (anode VBAT, cathode VSYS) limits the dip to about 0.3 V. This needs a footprint, so it is for the next revision. On revision A, measure 3V3 on a scope while unplugging at VBAT 3.6 V.

findings.title: Firmware has no low-battery cutoff, and brownout stays at level 0, so the ESP32 runs below 3.0 V as the battery empties
findings.refs: firmware/mark-8/slab-player/main/player_power.c (reads MAX17048 every 30 s, no shutdown threshold); slab-player/sdkconfig CONFIG_ESP_BROWNOUT_DET_LVL=0; U5 ALRT unconnected
findings.evidence: Minimum VBAT (at J4) to keep U1 at 3.0 V or more. 3V3 path U4.5 to U1.3 is 0.224 ohm (computed). The battery path J4 to Q2, Q2 to Q3 and Q3 to U4 is 0.144 ohm of track plus Q2 and Q3 at 2 x 0.06 ohm. RT9080 dropout is 0.52 ohm typical / 0.88 ohm max (0.31/0.53 V at 600 mA). Average playback (3V3 150 mA, battery 250 mA): VBAT of 3.18 V typical / 3.25 V max. Peak (3V3 300 mA, battery 500 mA): 3.36 V typical / 3.46 V max. The firmware never acts on a low VCELL. The ESP32 keeps running until the level-0 brownout (about 2.4 V on the 3.3 V rail), well under the 3.0 V minimum, and writes NVS on sleep (player_prefs_flush).
findings.requirement: ESP32-PICO-MINI-02 Table 14 (VDD33 3.0 to 3.6 V). RT9080 dropout table (p.4). AO3401A Rds(on) of 85 mOhm max at -2.5 V.
findings.consequence: At the end of the battery, the player can brown out and reboot in a loop, or corrupt NVS or the card. The protected pack then trips its own cutoff.
findings.fix: Firmware: save state and enter deep sleep when VCELL under load is 3.45 V or less (or SOC is about 3 % or less), and refuse to wake from sleep below about 3.5 V without USB. Raise the brownout level to the highest that still sits below 3.0 V. Optionally use the MAX17048 VALRT.MIN alert in firmware.

findings.title: RT9080 output has only C11 (1 uF 0402, about 0.6 to 0.8 uF effective at 3.3 V) at the pin; the 22 uF bulk capacitor is 108 mm and 0.22 ohm away
findings.refs: U4 pin 5 to C11 (14 mOhm path); U4 pin 5 to C5 22 uF 221 mOhm path (L1 0.4 mm 50.5 mm + L3 0.4 mm 55.1 mm, 8 vias); C11 = CL05A105KA5NQNC 1 uF 25 V X5R 0402
findings.evidence: The datasheet asks for 'effective capacitance larger than 1 uF' at VOUT, placed close to VOUT and GND. A 1 uF 0402 X5R at a 3.3 V bias typically loses 20 to 40 % (from Samsung DC-bias curves, from memory). The other 3V3 capacitors are far away: C18 at Q4 (91 mOhm), C13 at U6, and C5/C6 at U1.
findings.requirement: RT9080 DS9080-05 'Application Information' (p.11): 1 uF or larger input capacitor close to VIN; output capacitor with effective capacitance > 1 uF and ESR of 1 mOhm or more, close to VOUT and GND.
findings.consequence: Less stability margin and worse load-step response at the LDO. It probably works, but it is below the datasheet minimum at the pin. It also makes the Q4 inrush (PWR-1) worse.
findings.fix: Before ordering, replace C11 with a 2.2 to 4.7 uF part that fits the 0402 pads (or keep 1 uF and add a second 1 uF there). Otherwise, check 3V3 ringing on the first board with a load step (backlight off/on, Bluetooth on).

findings.title: MCP73831 input and output capacitors are about 30 mm of track from the IC pins, and C7 is below 4.7 uF effective at 5 V
findings.refs: U3 pin 4 (VDD) to C7 4.7 uF CL10A475KO8NNNC 16 V 0603: 68.7 mOhm path, about 28 mm (L1 and L3); U3 pin 3 (VBAT) to C8 10 uF CL10A106KP8NNNC 10 V 0603: 58.9 mOhm path, 28.7 mm (via Q2); computed with pathres2.py
findings.evidence: The parts sit 3 to 9 mm from U3, but the routed copper between pin and capacitor is about 28 mm, about 25 to 30 nH. C7 at a 5 V bias is about 2.5 to 3 uF effective (Samsung curve, from memory). C1 10 uF sits at J1, 140 mm away.
findings.requirement: MCP73831 DS20001984G section 3.1: bypass VDD to VSS with at least 4.7 uF. Section 3.2 and 6.1.1.4: at least 4.7 uF on VBAT to keep the constant-voltage loop stable without a battery and to compensate the inductance of the battery and its leads.
findings.consequence: Possible constant-voltage oscillation or charge-state chatter, mainly with the battery unplugged or on long battery leads. Hot-plug transients reach U3 less filtered. Probably works.
findings.fix: No change required for revision A. On the first board, scope VBAT with no battery and with the battery in CV phase. In the next revision, put a 10 uF on each pin with a short loop to the VSS pin.

findings.title: With no battery, VBAT loading defeats the charger's battery-detect, so U3 cycles charge and complete, the LED flickers and the gauge reads full
findings.refs: VBAT net: R27+R28 2 MOhm divider, U5 MAX17048 VDD (23 uA active), C8, C12; U3 STAT to LED1
findings.evidence: The MCP73831 needs more than 2 MOhm on VBAT to see 'no battery': it sources 6 uA and looks for VREG + 100 mV. Here U5 alone draws 23 uA typ (about 180 kOhm at 4.2 V), in parallel with 2 MOhm. So the charger starts a cycle, charges C8 to 4.2 V, terminates, waits for VBAT to fall to VRTH 4.05 V (tens of ms at 25 uA into about 6 uF) and starts again.
findings.requirement: MCP73831 section 4.2 (no-battery detection: impedance seen by VBAT must be greater than 2 MOhm). MAX17048 IDD1 23 uA typ / 40 uA max.
findings.consequence: USB-only operation works: VSYS comes from D1. But LED1 flickers, and the MAX17048 and VBAT_SENSE report about 4.1 to 4.2 V, about 100 %, with no pack fitted. Bring-up tests on USB without a battery will show a 'battery' that is not there.
findings.fix: Document it in the bring-up notes. In firmware, treat 'VBUS present and VCELL sawtoothing about 4.05 to 4.2 V with no charge current trend' as 'no battery', or just accept it.

findings.title: USB input current exceeds the 500 mA default while charging and playing, and the board cannot read the source's current advertisement
findings.refs: J1 CC1/CC2 to R1/R2 5.1k only (no MCU sense); U3 370 mA plus VSYS loads through D1
findings.evidence: Estimated loads on USB: charger 370 mA, 3V3 about 150 mA on average and up to about 365 mA at peak (Bluetooth TX and CPU estimated at about 250 mA; screen ILCD 15 mA from the DLC spec; SD write up to about 100 mA), backlight up to 161 mA (firmware model (4.65 - 2.8)/11.5) at 80 % duty on USB, buzzer up to 104 mA (12 ohm coil + 33 ohm), and haptic about 100 mA. Average about 0.65 A, peak about 1.1 A. The MCP73831 has no input current limit.
findings.requirement: USB 2.0 / Type-C 'Default USB Power' is 500 mA for a sink that only presents Rd and does not read Rp.
findings.consequence: Fine on phone chargers. On a strict 500 mA laptop port, VBUS can sag or the port can trip. Then the system falls back to the battery through Q3's body diode, and charging stalls.
findings.fix: Accept it for revision A, or lower the charge current (PWR-4). The firmware could cap the backlight harder while VBUS is below about 4.6 V.

findings.title: The deep-sleep budget in the README leaves out D1 reverse leakage and the MPR121 run-mode current used by the default touch wake
findings.refs: README Power bullet 6 (deep-sleep estimate); D1 B5819W VSYS to VBUS; Kconfig SLAB_SLEEP_TOUCH_WAKE default y, ESI 64 ms; R25 100k SD_CD
findings.evidence: D1 is reverse-biased at about 4 V on battery. The B5819W reverse-characteristics graph (C8598 p.2) shows about 6 uA at 25 C, about 60 uA at 75 C (about 10 to 15 uA at pocket temperature). That current flows into R9 || (R29+R30) and lifts VBUS to about 0.4 to 0.8 V (VBUS_SENSE reads about 0.25 to 0.5 V; the 4.3 V threshold is unaffected). MPR121 at a 64 ms period draws 11 uA (C91322 Table 5), not the 3 uA stop mode. Revised typical total: ESP32 10 + U4 2 + U5 3 to 4 + U6 11 + U7 4.1 + U2 VIO 2 + divider 2.1 + D1 6 to 15 + U3 0.15, about 41 to 51 uA. With a card fitted add 33 uA (R25), about 74 to 84 uA. Datasheet maximums (U4 4, U5 5, U7 7, U2 VIO 50 uA, D1 at 45 C) can push it past 100 uA.
findings.requirement: SPEC 5.2 deep-sleep target below 100 uA.
findings.consequence: The target is still met in the typical case: about 1.5 to 2.5 years of standby on 1100 mAh. The margin is smaller than the README shows, and R25 is the largest single term.
findings.fix: Update the README budget. Optional: R25 100k to 1M (3.3 uA with a card in; the strap and the card-detect switch are both slow).

findings.title: VBUS_SENSE scales 5 V to 3.0 V, above the ESP32 ADC's calibrated range
findings.refs: R29 100k / R30 150k to GPIO36; slab_analog.c ADC_ATTEN_DB_12, line-fitting calibration; SLAB_VBUS_PRESENT_MV 4300
findings.evidence: 5.0 V gives 3.0 V at the pin, and 5.25 V gives 3.15 V. ESP-IDF documents the ESP32 12 dB range as accurate to about 2450 mV, with saturation near 3.1 V. The 4.3 V threshold is 2.58 V at the pin, just above the calibrated range. The VSYS estimate (VBUS - 350 mV) also ignores the 0.2 V or more of track drop to D1 (PWR-3), so the backlight compensation on USB runs slightly dim.
findings.requirement: ESP-IDF ADC documentation for ESP32 (12 dB: about 150 to 2450 mV recommended). This is not in the module datasheet, so it comes from memory.
findings.consequence: Presence detection works. Absolute VBUS readings near 5 V are compressed and inaccurate.
findings.fix: Optional: R30 150k to 68k (5.25 V gives 2.13 V). Or keep it and use the reading only as a present/absent flag.

checked: MCP73831 U3 pin map against datasheet table 3-1 (SOT-23-5: 1 STAT, 2 VSS, 3 VBAT, 4 VDD, 5 PROG) = netlist U3.1 CHG_STAT, U3.2 GND, U3.3 VBAT, U3.4 VBUS, U3.5 CHG_PROG; footprint pads 1-3 bottom row, 4-5 top row (standard CCW order)

MCP73831 PROG R7 2.7k: IREG = 1000 V / 2.7 kOhm = 370 mA (eq. 5-1), within the RPROG range of 2 to 67 kOhm; -2ACI option AC: VREG 4.20 V, precondition 10 % (37 mA) below 66.5 % (2.79 V), termination 7.5 % (28 mA), recharge at 96.5 % (4.05 V); 0.28 to 0.34C for the 1100 to 1300 mAh pack in SPEC 10 (0.37 to 0.5C for a 403450)

MCP73831 STAT: R8 1k from VBUS to the LED1 anode, cathode on STAT (netlist LED1.2 K): on while charging (STAT low), off when complete (STAT high = VDD) and when shut down (Hi-Z); about 2.6 mA, well under the 25 mA ISINK
MCP73831 VDD 3.75 to 6 V and abs max 7.0 V against VBUS; USBLC6-2SC6 U8 pin 5 on VBUS gives the input TVS that datasheet section 6.1.1.2 asks for (VBR of 6 V or more)
MCP73831 reverse discharge on battery (VDD < VSTOP): 0.15 uA typ / 2 uA max, matches the README
RT9080 U4 pin map against DS9080-05 (TSOT-23-5: 1 VIN, 2 GND, 3 EN, 4 NC, 5 VOUT) = netlist U4.1 VSYS, U4.3 VSYS, U4.5 3V3, U4.4 NC; EN tied to VIN is allowed (Application Information, Enable)

RT9080 VIN 1.2 to 5.5 V against VSYS of about 4.3 to 5.0 V on USB; IQ 2 uA typ / 4 uA max; ILIM 610 mA min / 1.1 A typ against the estimated 3V3 peak of about 365 mA with Bluetooth (about 480 mA if Wi-Fi TX at 368 mA were ever used); C10 1 uF at VIN with C9 22 uF 5 mm away
RT9080 thermal: on USB at 150 mA average, (4.4 - 3.3) x 0.15 = 0.17 W, about +40 K at 230.6 C/W, OK; sustained Wi-Fi-level load (about 0.5 A) would exceed the 0.43 W limit (datasheet Fig. 6)

Minimum battery voltage: VBAT at J4 of 3.18 V typ / 3.25 V max (average load) and 3.36 V typ / 3.46 V max (peak load) keeps U1 at 3.0 V or more, using RT9080 dropout 0.31/0.53 V at 600 mA, Q2+Q3 Rds(on) 2 x 60 mOhm and computed track resistances (J4 to U4 0.144 ohm, U4 to U1 0.224 ohm)

MAX17048 U5 against the datasheet (Adafruit-hosted copy, see not_checked): TDFN pin map 1 CTG to GND, 2 CELL to VBAT (not internally connected on the MAX17048, allowed), 3 VDD to VBAT (supply and voltage sense, 2.5 to 4.5 V), 4 GND, 5 ALRT open drain left open (optional), 6 QSTRT to GND ('connect to GND if not used'), 7 SCL, 8 SDA, EP to GND; I2C address 0110110 = 0x36; SDA/SCL abs max 5.5 V with 4.7k pull-ups to 3V3; VIH 1.4 V; C12 1 uF on VDD 2 mm away (datasheet asks for 0.1 uF or more); hibernate 3 uA typ / 5 uA max, active 23 uA typ / 40 uA max
MAX17048 measures between VDD and GND after Q2: Q2 adds about 20 to 30 mV at 400 mA, a small SOC error under load (note only)

Q2, Q3 and Q4 AO3401A pin map (1 G, 2 S, 3 D; datasheet p.1) against netlist Q2 {G GND, S VBAT, D BAT_P}, Q3 {G VBUS, S VSYS, D VBAT}, Q4 {G PERIPH_GATE, S 3V3, D 3V3_PERIPH}; SOT-23_AO3401A footprint pad geometry is a proper rotation of the standard SOT-23 (pin 1 bottom-left, pin 3 top), not a mirror
D1 B5819W cathode (pad 1) on VSYS, anode on VBUS; D2 cathode on BZ_P (flyback correct); B5819W 1 A rating, VF about 0.4 V at 0.7 A (C8598 p.2)
Power path, USB only: VSYS = VBUS - D1 (about 4.3 to 4.6 V with the track drop), Q3 off (Vgs about +0.3 to +0.5 V), the charger output is not loaded by the system
Power path, battery only: Q2 on (Vgs = -VBAT), Q3 on (Vgs = -VSYS, 60 to 85 mOhm), D1 reverse-biased

Power path, both: the system runs on D1, Q3 is off and its body diode is reverse-biased while VSYS > VBAT - 0.6 V (true down to VBUS of about 4.4 V at J1), the charger sees only U5 (23 uA) and the 2.1 uA divider, so termination at 28 mA works

Dead or protection-tripped pack with USB: the system boots from D1; the charger output raises VBAT, Q2 (gate on GND) turns on at VBAT of about 1 V and passes precondition current into the pack's protection circuit, so the pack recovers
Correct-polarity battery and no USB: Q2 protection logic correct (body diode, then channel); reversed pack without USB is blocked (VBAT about 0 V, Vgs = 0)

Q4 default state: R13 100k holds the gate at 3V3 (off) at reset and whenever GPIO13 floats; in deep sleep the firmware drives GPIO13 high through an RTC hold (slab_board_prepare_deep_sleep) with pulls disabled

3V3_PERIPH back-power: slab_power_seq.c drives LCD SCK/MOSI/CS/DC/RST and SD SCK/MOSI/CS low and makes SD_MISO and LCD_TE inputs before GPIO13 goes high; in deep sleep the RTC pads are isolated and GPIO5/19/21 are held low; SD pull-ups R21-R24 go to 3V3_PERIPH (no current while off); SD_CD R25 goes to the always-on 3V3 through a mechanical switch (no path into the card); Q4 body diode points 3V3_PERIPH to 3V3 (harmless)
Q4 on-state: Vgs = -3.3 x 100/110 = -3.0 V gives Rds of about 55 mOhm; R13+R14 draw 30 uA while the screen is on

VBAT_SENSE: R27/R28 1M/1M, 4.2 V gives 2.1 V (inside the 12 dB range), 2.1 uA drain, C24 100 nF gives a 50 ms time constant for sampling; GPIO35 is ADC1 (works with Bluetooth); firmware ratio 2000 and ADC_ATTEN_DB_12 match
VBUS_SENSE: R29/R30 100k/150k, ratio 1.667 matches SLAB_VBUS_DIVIDER_X1000 1667; GPIO36 is ADC1; injection current with 3V3 low is limited to microamps by 100 kOhm
CH9102F U2 on battery: VIO does not back-feed VDD5/V3 and draws 2 uA typ / 50 uA max (CH9102 datasheet section 5.2 and ISLP); its VBUS pin at the D1-leakage level of about 0.4 V is below VIHVBS 1.7 V

DRV2605L U7: VDD 2.0 to 5.2 V (abs max 5.5 V) against VSYS of 3.0 to 5.0 V; REG 1 uF (C17); IN/TRIG on GND as the datasheet asks for an unused pin; pin 6 VDD/NC tied to VDD; EN high through R12 gives standby at 4.1 uA typ / 7 uA max (same as shutdown 4 uA, so the always-high EN costs nothing)

Backlight: screen spec IF 200 mA typ at VF 2.7 to 3.3 V; at VSYS 4.2 V about 120 mA, on USB at most about 160 to 220 mA during the PWM on-time; the firmware caps average R17 power at 231 mW (under the 1206 0.25 W rating) and USB duty at 80 %
Buzzer: 12 ohm coil (C94598) + 33 ohm R18 gives 93 to 104 mA peak at VSYS 4.2 to 4.7 V, at the 100 mA rating; short clicks keep R18 (0805, 0.125 W) inside its rating

Peak current from the battery (Bluetooth playback, screen, card write, buzzer, haptic): about 0.6 A, 0.5C on 1100 mAh, well under typical pack over-current limits; average playback about 210 mA with the screen on (about 5 h on 1100 mAh) and about 150 mA with the screen off (estimates, see not_checked)

Track resistances of the power paths, computed from the routed board: J4 to Q2 37.5 mOhm, Q2 to Q3 39.7, Q3 to U4 66.1, U4 to U1 224, U4 to Q4 91, Q4 to J2 68, Q4 to J3 40, D1 to U4 171 mOhm; VBAT, VSYS and 3V3 trunks are 0.4 mm or wider
ESP32 MTDI (GPIO12) left unconnected keeps VDD_SDIO at 3.3 V for the PICO-V3-02's 3.3 V flash and PSRAM (module datasheet section 4.2), consistent with the 3V3 rail
not_checked: MAX17048: the LCSC file C2682616.pdf is an HTML stub, and analog.com and Mouser timed out or refused. I downloaded the manufacturer datasheet from an Adafruit CDN copy (cdn-learn.adafruit.com) to review-datasheets/dl-max17048/max17048.pdf, but I did not confirm its revision against analog.com

ESP32 GPIO13 (MTCK) reset pull state: the ESP32 series datasheet IO_MUX appendix is not in the folder. If GPIO13 had an internal pull-down at reset, Q4 would turn on during boot (45k against R13 100k + R14 10k). From memory it is input-only with no pull. Check on the first board that 3V3_PERIPH stays at 0 V while EN is held low and during the ROM boot

Bluetooth BR/EDR TX current, SD card currents and the LCM1027A motor current: no datasheets in the folder. The budget uses estimates (about 250 mA ESP32 with Bluetooth and CPU, about 100 mA for an SD write, about 100 mA for the motor)
Capacitor DC-bias derating (C7, C8, C11, C5, C9) is from memory of the Samsung curves, not from downloaded data

The Q4 inrush and 3V3 droop figures come from a simple square-law MOSFET and current-limited LDO model, not SPICE or a bench measurement. The RT9080 loop response and its real current limit were not modelled
Board thermal resistance of this 0.8 mm, 54 x 40 mm board inside the PLA case: not simulated. The MCP73831 and RT9080 temperatures are estimates from the JEDEC theta-JA
ESP32 deep-sleep current with ext0+ext1 wake, RTC GPIO holds and the PSRAM module: the module datasheet gives only 10 uA for the timer case
JLC CPL rotation and polarity of D1, Q2 to Q4, U3 to U5 and J4 in the placement preview, and the JST PH pack polarity convention: left to the placement reviewer and the assembly check
Actual JLC inner copper thickness (assumed 17.5 um for 0.5 oz) and whether 1 oz inner copper is offered for 4 layers at 0.8 mm
USB hot-plug overshoot on VBUS and VSYS (DRV2605L abs max 5.5 V behind D1 and C9): judged low risk, not simulated
The STEP and enclosure files were not used to confirm how close U3 sits to the front skin, beyond SPEC 6 (L4 against the skin)

verdicts.reasoning: Netlist: Q4 pin1 PERIPH_GATE, pin2 3V3 (source), pin3 3V3_PERIPH; R13 100k 3V3-gate, R14 10k PERIPH_EN_N-gate, C18 100 nF PERIPH_GATE-3V3, so C18 is gate-source. Load: C19, C21 10 uF 0603 (C19702) plus C20, C22. The 3V3 source side has only C5 22 uF 0603 (at U1, 221 mOhm of track from U4) and C11 1 uF (at U4); nothing to GND sits at Q4 (U4.5 to Q4.2 is 91 mOhm). A gate-source capacitor only sets the delay before Vth. It does not limit drain dV/dt, and Crss 55 pF (AO3401A p.2) is negligible against 100 nF. My own square-law simulation (review-work/power-verify/q4sim.py; K 5 to 18 A/V2 from Rds(on) 60 mOhm at -2.5 V and gFS 17 S; Vth -0.5/-0.9/-1.3 V; 14 uF load, 15 uF source) gives a 55 to 110 us 10-90 % rise after a 0.3 to 0.7 ms delay, and a 0.55 to 1.2 A peak. With RT9080 ILIM 610 mA min (DS9080-05 p.4) and an 80 mA load, 3V3 dips to 2.72 to 3.28 V. With a 250 mA load it dips to 2.46 to 3.01 V. With 1.1 A typical ILIM it stays at 3.23 V or more. The README 'about a 1 ms turn-on ramp' sentence and the slab_power_seq.h comment are wrong. One correction to the consequence: in the current firmware, slab-player main.c calls slab_board_periph_power(true) once per boot or wake, before esp_bt_controller_init, and turns it off only in player_power_sleep. So the 'Bluetooth running' case does not happen today. The real exposure is a 2.7 to 3.0 V dip at boot on a low-ILIM RT9080, below the ESP32-PICO-MINI-02 VDD33 3.0 V minimum (datasheet Table 14) but above the level-0 brownout.
verdicts.fix: Change C18 from 100 nF to 1 uF (C52923, already on the BOM in the same 0402 footprint). My simulation then gives a 0.14 to 0.28 A peak and no 3V3 dip. In the same change, raise SLAB_PERIPH_RAMP_MS in components/slab_board/include/slab_power_seq.h from 5 to about 20 ms. With 1 uF the gate time constant is 9.1 ms, and 3V3_PERIPH reaches 90 % only at 2.1 to 6.1 ms (Vth min to max). The current 5 ms wait would drive SD_CS high before the rail is up on a high-Vth part, which back-powers the card. Turn-off becomes about 9 ms (both resistors pull to 3.3 V), which is harmless. Correct the README Power bullet and the header comment. Keep the periph-on before Bluetooth init in firmware.

verdicts.reasoning: Netlist: Q2 pin1 G = GND, pin2 S = VBAT, pin3 D = BAT_P; J4 pin2 = BAT_P, pin1 = GND. With the pack reversed, BAT_P = -3.7 V and the body diode (anode BAT_P, cathode VBAT) is reverse-biased, so the board is safe without USB. With USB present, MCP73831 sources the 6 uA detect current, then (because VBAT < VPTH) the preconditioning current. Option AC is 10 % of IREG (DS20001984G p.4 and Product Identification table: AC = 10 / 66.5 / 7.5 / 96.5), about 37 mA at R7 2.7k. Once VBAT reaches |Vth| (0.5 to 1.3 V, AO3401A p.2), Q2 has Vgs = -VBAT and its channel conducts VBAT to BAT_P. VBAT clamps near 1 V, below VNO_BAT (VREG + 100 mV), so U3 'detects a battery' and stays in preconditioning with no timer (Fig. 4-1). STAT is low, so LED1 (R8 1k from VBUS) is on. The current runs through the cell in its discharge direction. Q2 dissipation is about 4.7 V x 37 mA = 0.17 W, which is safe. The README 'Check before paying' 5 and ASSEMBLY.md step 11 sentence 'The board blocks a reversed pack' is true only without USB.
verdicts.fix: No hardware change for revision A. Correct the README and ASSEMBLY step 11 wording ('blocks a reversed pack on battery power; with USB connected a reversed pack is slowly discharged and the charge LED stays on'). Keep the meter check. Optional firmware: if VBUS is present and VBAT_SENSE stays below about 2 V for 10 s, show 'battery reversed'.

verdicts.reasoning: I re-ran the path script on the PCB (copied to review-work/power-verify) and confirmed there is no VBUS zone: the only zones are GND and the electrodes. J1.A4B9 to U3.4 is 349 mOhm: L1 0.4 mm 26.3 mm, L1 0.3 mm 27.2, L1 0.2 mm 9.6, In2.Cu(L3) 0.4 mm 63.2, L3 0.3 mm 13.9, plus vias. J1.B4A9 to D1.2 is 315 mOhm. ORDER.md sets 1 oz outer and 0.5 oz inner copper. By hand, the narrow track alone is 0.024 + 0.037 + 0.046 = 0.106 ohm, so the README '0.1 ohm' is correct for the narrow track only. Its conclusion ('more than 4.6 V') leaves out the 63 mm of 0.4 mm track on 0.5 oz L3, about 0.155 ohm. The current is not capped at 500 mA. IREG = 1000 V / 2.7k = 370 mA, plus the VSYS load through D1 (Q3 is off on USB). IPC-2221 inner, 0.4 mm x 17.5 um (11 mil2): I = 0.024 x 10^0.44 x 11^0.725 = 0.37 A for a 10 K rise. MCP73831 specifies VDD of at least VREG + 0.3 V = 4.5 V (DS20001984G section 3.1 and the electrical-characteristics header). With about 0.2 V of track drop and a 4.75 V source, U3 runs slightly below that range. It still charges, with less CV headroom.
verdicts.fix: Ask JLC for 1 oz inner copper if the 4-layer 0.8 mm option allows it; I could not confirm it is offered. Otherwise accept it, and correct the README step C numbers to about 0.31 to 0.35 ohm total and 0.15 to 0.25 V of drop at 0.5 to 0.7 A. On the first board, measure VBUS at U3 pin 4 while charging with the backlight at full brightness.

verdicts.reasoning: U3 is the SOT-23-5 MCP73831T-2ACI/OT, theta-JA 230 C/W on a JEDEC 4-layer board (DS20001984G p.5). R7 2.7k gives IREG 370 mA. Pd = (VDD - VBAT) x IREG: at VDD 4.8 V it is 0.74 W at VBAT 2.8 V (start of fast charge) and 0.44 W at 3.6 V. That is a junction rise of about 100 to 170 K at 230 C/W. Fig. 4-2 (p.14) shows the current starting to fold back at about 80 C junction, down to about 300 mA at 95 C. So in a closed case U3 will run in thermal regulation for much of the fast-charge phase. Section 6.1.1.3 states this for the SOT-23 and suggests the DFN. This is the part's designed, safe behaviour (current foldback, TSD at 150 C). The real effect is a longer charge time and a hot spot of a few hundred mW at the top-left of the board, near the PLA front skin. Whether the PLA softens is not established: it depends on how far the board spreads the heat, which I could not model. The 1.0 W 'worst case' is overstated for this board, because VDD at U3 is about 4.6 to 4.8 V, not 5.25 V.
verdicts.fix: No change is required before ordering. Thermal regulation bounds the junction temperature. On the first board, measure the board surface temperature behind U3 (L4 side) while charging an empty pack with the screen on, inside the closed case. If it is above about 50 C, print the front shell in PETG (SPEC allows PLA or PETG), or raise R7 to 3.9k or 4.7k (about 256 or 213 mA). Check the JLC basic-part status of the new resistor before changing it.

verdicts.reasoning: Netlist: Q3 G = VBUS, S = VSYS, D = VBAT, so the body diode runs from VBAT to VSYS. R9 100k on VBUS; R29 + R30 = 250k; VBUS caps C1 10 uF 0805, C7 4.7 uF 0603, C25 100 nF. After unplug, U3 pulls VBUS down to about VBAT. D1 then clamps VBUS to about VSYS + 0.1 V while VSYS falls to VBAT - Vbody. AO3401A VSD is 0.7 V typ at 1 A (p.2), about 0.6 to 0.65 V at 0.2 A. Q3's channel turns on only when VBUS falls |Vth| (0.5 to 1.3 V) below VSYS. VBUS is discharged by 71k (about 42 uA), the CH9102F (datasheet section 6.2: operating 3 mA typ / 15 mA max, suspend 0.09 mA, VBUS pin pull-down 10 uA above 1.6 V) and U3 in power-down (1 to 5 uA, p.3). With about 12 uF effective on VBUS, the window is about 4 ms when a PC host was connected (U2 still operating until its 3 to 9 ms suspend detect) and about 50 to 120 ms on a wall charger (U2 suspended). The reviewer's 0.8 s time constant leaves out U2's current, so 'hundreds of ms' is an overestimate. During the window, 3V3 at U1 is about VBAT - 0.75 V: below the ESP32 3.0 V minimum (Table 14) for VBAT under about 3.75 V, and at the level-0 brownout (about 2.43 V) only for VBAT under about 3.2 V. The mechanism is real. Its impact is a short out-of-spec supply, and a reset is likely only at low charge.
verdicts.fix: Revision A, cheap: R9 100k to 10k (0.5 mA while plugged in), which shortens the wall-charger window to about 25 to 30 ms; 4.7k gives about 10 ms. It is the same footprint, but check the JLC basic part. Next revision: a Schottky from VBAT (anode) to VSYS (cathode) across Q3, or a load-switch ideal-diode part. On the first board, scope 3V3 at TP1 while unplugging from a wall charger at VBAT about 3.6 V with audio playing.

verdicts.reasoning: slab-player/main/player_power.c reads the MAX17048 every 30 s (GAUGE_PERIOD_MS) and stores percent and vcell_mv. Nothing compares them to a threshold, and a grep of slab-player/main and components/slab_board finds no low-battery cutoff. The U5 ALRT pin (5) is unconnected in design.py. sdkconfig has CONFIG_ESP_BROWNOUT_DET_LVL_SEL_0=y. Errata RES-3.4 affects only chip v0.0, so the brownout reset works on this part. Supply chain from my run of the path script: BAT_P 37.5 mOhm, VBAT Q2 to Q3 39.7 mOhm, VSYS Q3 to U4 66 mOhm, 3V3 U4 to U1 224 mOhm, plus Q2 and Q3 Rds(on) (AO3401A at most 85 mOhm at -2.5 V) and RT9080 dropout of 0.31 V typ / 0.53 V max at 600 mA (DS9080-05 p.4). This gives a minimum cell voltage of about 3.2 to 3.45 V to hold U1 at 3.0 V or more under playback or peak load, matching the reviewer. player_power_sleep calls player_prefs_flush (an NVS write) with no voltage check.
verdicts.fix: Firmware only. Save state and enter deep sleep when VCELL under load stays at or below about 3.45 V (or SOC at or below about 3 %) for several readings while VBUS is absent. Refuse to stay awake after a wake below about 3.5 V without USB. Raising the brownout level (level 7 is about 2.8 V) helps, but it also makes the PWR-1 and PWR-5 transients more likely to reset the chip, so fix PWR-1 first.

verdicts.reasoning: Netlist and BOM: C11 1 uF 0402 C52923 (CL05A105KA5NQNC, 25 V X5R) on 3V3, 14 mOhm of track from U4 pin 5. The next 3V3 capacitor to GND is C5 22 uF 0603 (C59461) at U1, 221 mOhm and about 106 mm away. RT9080 DS9080-05 p.10 and p.11 ask for an output capacitor with effective capacitance larger than 1 uF after voltage and temperature derating, placed close to VOUT and GND. A 1 uF 0402 X5R loses some capacitance at a 3.3 V bias. I could not check the Samsung DC-bias curve, so the 20 to 40 % figure is unverified, but the effective value is almost certainly below 1 uF. In practice the distant 22 uF behind about 0.22 ohm acts like a large capacitor with an ESR zero, which normally helps a PMOS LDO stay stable, so the real risk is low.
verdicts.fix: Before ordering, change C11 to a 2.2 uF (or larger) 10 V X5R 0402. Check that the LCSC part is a JLC basic part. If no basic part is available, leave it and check 3V3 at C11 for ringing on the first board during a backlight on/off step and Bluetooth start-up.

verdicts.reasoning: Placement: U3 at (-24.6, -21.9), C7 at (-25.4, -25.4), C8 at (-15.6, -21.4). Routed copper from my run: U3.4 to C7.1 is 68.7 mOhm, about 28 mm through 4 via transitions on L1 and L3; U3.3 to C8.1 is 58.9 mOhm, 28.7 mm. MCP73831 DS20001984G section 3.1 asks for VDD bypassed with at least 4.7 uF; sections 3.2 and 6.1.1.4 ask for at least 4.7 uF on VBAT for CV-loop stability without a battery. Section 6.2 asks for short connections. C7 is 4.7 uF 16 V 0603 (C19666), nominally at the minimum and below it at a 5 V bias; C8 is 10 uF 10 V 0603. The facts hold. The impact is small: the charger loop is slow, about 25 nH of track matters only at MHz, the 60 to 70 mOhm of track adds damping ESR, C1 10 uF also sits on VDD, and C12 1 uF and the battery sit on VBAT. 'Note' fits better than 'minor'.
verdicts.fix: No change for revision A. On the first board, scope VBAT with no battery fitted and during CV with a battery. In the next revision, put 10 uF directly at U3 pins 4 and 3 with a short return to pin 2.

verdicts.reasoning: VBAT net (netlist): C8, C12, Q2.2, Q3.3, R27 (1M + R28 1M to GND = 2 MOhm), U3.3, U5.2/3. MCP73831 section 4.2 and p.4: the 6 uA detect current must raise VBAT to VREG + 100 mV, and the load must be at least 2 MOhm for 'no battery'. MAX17048 IDD1 is 23 uA typ / 40 uA max in active mode (downloaded datasheet, review-work/power-ics/max17048.txt), so with no pack U3 'detects a battery'. It then charges C8 and C12 to 4.2 V, terminates at ITERM (7.5 %, option AC), and recharges when VBAT falls to VRTH (96.5 % = 4.05 V). At about 20 to 25 uA net drain into about 7 uF effective, one cycle takes about 40 to 50 ms. LED1 lights only during each short charge pulse, so it flickers faintly. The gauge and VBAT_SENSE read about 4.05 to 4.2 V.
verdicts.fix: Add a bring-up note: with no pack fitted, a faint LED flicker and a near-full gauge reading are expected. No hardware change.

verdicts.reasoning: J1 CC1 and CC2 go only to R1 and R2 5.1k Rd; no Rp sense reaches the MCU, so the sink must stay within Default USB Power (500 mA for USB 2.0). U3 takes IREG 370 mA (R7 2.7k) with no input current limit (the MCP73831 has none), and VSYS is fed through D1 on USB (Q3 off). With 3V3 at about 100 to 250 mA and the backlight on, the total is about 0.6 to 0.7 A, with peaks near 1 A. I did not re-derive each load figure, but charger plus system clearly exceeds 500 mA. It works on chargers and most laptop ports; strict ports may sag.
verdicts.fix: Accept it for revision A. Optional firmware: cap the backlight duty while USB is present. If PWR-4 leads to a larger R7, that also helps here.

verdicts.reasoning: B5819W reverse characteristic (C8598 p.2) reads about 5 to 6 uA at VR 4 V and 25 C, and about 60 uA at 75 C. On battery D1 is reverse-biased VSYS to VBUS, and that leakage flows into R9 || (R29 + R30) = 71k, lifting VBUS to about 0.4 V. The README Power bullet 6 budget does not list D1. MPR121 run mode at a 64 ms sample period is 11 uA (C91322 p. around line 625 of the extraction, average supply current table), not the 3 uA stop mode. Kconfig SLAB_SLEEP_TOUCH_WAKE defaults to y with SLAB_SLEEP_TOUCH_ESI_MS 64. This part is already acknowledged: README Power note 2 says the 100 uA budget assumes stop mode and that run-mode current must be measured. The D1 term is new. The revised typical totals (about 40 to 50 uA, about 75 to 85 uA with a card) still meet SPEC 5.2.
verdicts.fix: Update the README deep-sleep budget: add D1 leakage of 6 to 15 uA and the MPR121 at 11 uA with touch wake on. Optional: R25 100k to 1M to cut the card-detect term from 33 to 3.3 uA.

verdicts.reasoning: R29 100k (VBUS to VBUS_SENSE) and R30 150k (to GND): 5.0 V gives 3.0 V and 5.25 V gives 3.15 V at GPIO36. slab_analog.c uses ADC_ATTEN_DB_12 with line-fitting calibration. The ESP32 datasheet ADC calibration table (local esp32_datasheet_en.txt, line 2650; PICO-MINI-02 Table 11) gives the atten 3 effective range as 150 to 2450 mV, and says accuracy is worse above about 2450 mV. SLAB_VBUS_PRESENT_MV 4300 maps to 2.58 V, slightly above that range. Presence detection still works. Absolute VBUS (and slab_vsys_estimate_mv's VBUS - SLAB_D1_DROP_MV) is compressed near 5 V.
verdicts.fix: Optional: R30 150k to 68k (5.25 V gives 2.13 V), and scale SLAB_VBUS_DIVIDER_X1000 to match. Or keep it and use VBUS_SENSE only as a present/absent flag.

verdicts.reasoning: Coverage, verified correct from primary sources: MCP73831-2AC option = 4.20 V, 10 % precondition, VPTH 66.5 %, ITERM 7.5 %, VRTH 96.5 % (DS20001984G Product Identification); R7 2.7k gives IREG = 1000 V / 2.7k = 370 mA, within the 2k to 67k RPROG range. RT9080 ILIM 610 min / 1100 typ mA and dropout 0.31 / 0.53 V at 600 mA (DS9080-05 p.4). Q2 reverse-battery orientation (G GND, S VBAT, D BAT_P) is correct for battery-only operation. Q3 load sharing (G VBUS, S VSYS, D VBAT) is off on USB because VBUS - VSYS is about +0.35 V, and its body diode is reverse-biased while on USB. Q4 gate network values and pins. AO3401A Vth -0.5/-0.9/-1.3 V, Rds(on) 60/85 mOhm, VSD 0.7/1.0 V, Crss 55 pF (C15127). No copper zone on VBUS. Path resistances re-run on the PCB file (VBUS 315 to 349 mOhm, 3V3 U4 to U1 224 mOhm, U4 to C11 14 mOhm). CH9102F currents (operating 3/15 mA, suspend 0.09 mA, VBUS pull-down 10 uA). MAX17048 IDD1 23/40 uA. MPR121 run-mode currents. B5819W reverse curve. ESP32 brownout works on this chip revision (errata RES-3.4 affects v0.0 only). ESP32 ADC atten 3 range 150 to 2450 mV. Firmware switches 3V3_PERIPH on once per boot or wake, before Bluetooth starts (slab-player main.c), and has no low-battery cutoff.
verdicts.fix: None. This entry lists coverage.

verdicts.reasoning: Not checked: (1) Samsung DC-bias curves for CL05A105KA5NQNC, CL10A475KO8NNNC and CL10A106KP8NNNC: effective capacitances are estimates, so PWR-7 and PWR-8 keep low confidence. (2) Whether JLC offers 1 oz inner copper on a 4-layer 0.8 mm board (PWR-3 fix). (3) Real board theta-JA for U3 and the PLA surface temperature (PWR-4): only a measurement settles it. (4) The internal capacitance of the screen module, the SD card and the ESP32 module, which shifts the PWR-1 numbers. The model also treats the LDO as an instant current-limited source, which is optimistic. (5) The exact ESP32 brownout thresholds by level, quoted from ESP-IDF from memory (level 0 about 2.43 V, level 7 about 2.8 V). (6) JLC basic-part LCSC numbers for a 2.2 uF 0402 capacitor or a 10k/4.7k 0402 for R9: these must be checked in the JLC parts library before any change. (7) I did not re-derive the backlight, buzzer and haptic current figures in PWR-10.
verdicts.fix: Measure on the first assembled board: 3V3 dip at Q4 turn-on, 3V3 during a USB unplug, VBUS at U3 pin 4 while charging, U3 board temperature, and deep-sleep current with touch wake on.

areas.title: Peripheral and interface circuits

findings.title: LCD_LEDA is treated as a DC net under the wheel, but it swings 1.2 to 2.2 V at the backlight PWM rate
findings.refs: design.py DISC_L3_NETS (LCD_LEDA listed as DC/static); R17 10R VSYS->LCD_LEDA; Q5 AO3400A drain on LCD_LEDK; README 'Touch wheel' bullet 3 and Verification table (LCD_LEDA 11.91 mm of L3 inside r 16.6, 2 vias inside r 17.1); firmware slab_backlight.h header
findings.evidence: With Q5 off there is no LED current, so LEDA = VSYS. With Q5 on, LEDA = VSYS - 10 ohm x I_LED, which is 1.2 to 2.2 V lower for 120 to 224 mA. LEDA is therefore a square wave at the PWM frequency (20 kHz fallback, CONFIG_SLAB_BL_FALLBACK_HZ). My track sum from the .kicad_pcb gives LCD_LEDA 11.91 mm on In2.Cu (L3) and 2 vias, all inside the disc, about 0.1 mm behind the electrodes. That is the same scale as the accepted LCD_CS exception (11.85 mm). The README lists LEDA with 3V3/VBUS/VSYS as 'DC and static nets', and verify.py does not flag it. The firmware header (slab_backlight.h) says the opposite: 'LCD_LEDA ... swings at the PWM rate'. VSYS also steps by about 170 mA x source impedance (tens of mV) at each PWM edge, and VSYS has 23.6 mm of L3 under the wheel.
findings.requirement: README's own rule (NXP AN3863, as cited): inside r 17.1 only nets that do not switch while the MPR121 scans may run on L3. A 1 to 2 V edge on 12 mm of track (about 0.6 pF by README's 0.5 pF per 10 mm) puts more charge per edge than many of the accepted 3.3 V nets.
findings.consequence: Every PWM edge can couple into the electrodes above. Touch noise or false touches can depend on brightness and PWM frequency. The documented exception list does not show this net, so the bring-up noise budget may miss it.
findings.fix: Rev A, firmware: keep the bring-up noise table that picks the PWM frequency (already in slab-bringup). If no frequency is quiet, run the backlight at 0 or 1000 permille only, since both hold the pin and make no edges (slab_backlight_set_permille already does this), or PWM only while the MPR121 is stopped. Rev B: put R17 between LEDK and Q5 drain and tie LEDA straight to VSYS, so LEDA becomes truly static. Or keep LEDA off L3 inside r 17.1. Correct the README and DISC_L3_NETS to show LEDA as a switching net.

findings.title: Worst-case backlight current on USB is over 200 mA, the 0.25 W rating of R17 and the 0.2 A rating of the single LEDK pin
findings.refs: R17 10R 1206 (C17903 = 1206W4F100JT5E, 0.25 W); Q5; J2 pin 1 LCD_LEDK (single contact), pins 14/15 LCD_LEDA; SPEC.md line 47; firmware slab_backlight.h (VF0 2800 mV, 11.5 ohm model, P_MAX 231 mW, USB cap 800 permille)
findings.evidence: Screen spec DLC-T2.7DDS#1 p.6: IF 200 mA (typ column), VF 2.7 to 3.3 V. SPEC.md line 47: '200 mA maximum total'. On USB, VSYS = VBUS (5.0 to 5.25 V) minus about 0.3 V across D1, so 4.7 to 4.95 V. I = (4.7 - 3.0)/10 = 170 mA typical, but (4.95 - 2.7)/10 = about 224 mA at the VF minimum. That gives 0.50 W in R17 at 100 percent duty. The firmware duty cap uses a model (VF0 2.8 V plus 1.5 ohm of LED resistance). At VSYS 4.8 V the model gives a 765 permille cap, but the real dissipation with VF at 2.7 V is about 0.34 W, still over the 0.25 W rating. The README's own number (0.231 W) is already 92 percent of the rating, with no derating inside a closed case. LEDK returns the whole backlight current through J2 pin 1 alone. Hirose FH35C is rated 0.2 A per contact. I took that from distributor listings (Avnet FH35C series page, DigiKey FH series highlight), not from the Hirose drawing in the review folder.
findings.requirement: SPEC 200 mA maximum total; R17 rating 0.25 W (Uniroyal 1206W4); FH35C rated current 0.2 A per contact.
findings.consequence: On USB at high brightness, R17 can run above its rating and the LEDK contact runs at or above 0.2 A peak. That shortens R17 and contact life. Firmware can limit the average, but not the peak current.
findings.fix: Use a 0.5 W 1206 part (for example a Uniroyal 1206W2 series 10R anti-surge resistor) or a 2010 resistor, or raise R17 to 12 ohm, which costs some brightness on battery. Rev A without hardware change: lower SLAB_BL_USB_MAX_PERMILLE to about 500 and base the cap on VF 2.7 V, not 2.8 V.

findings.title: R18 (33R 0805, 0.125 W) has thin margin and is overloaded if the buzzer is driven steadily or at low frequency
findings.refs: R18 0805W8F330JT5E (C17634, 1/8 W), BZ1 MLT-5020, Q6, GPIO2 (BUZZER); firmware slab_buzzer.c (duty capped at 50 percent, tone() accepts any hz); slab-bringup bringup.c lines 379 and 499 (sustained tones)
findings.evidence: MLT-5020 spec (C94598 p.2): coil 12 +-3 ohm, rated 3.0 Vo-p, current max 100 mA. With Q6 held on: I = 4.8 V/(33 + 12) = 107 mA, which is over the buzzer's 100 mA, and P_R18 = 0.375 W, 3 times the 0.125 W rating. At 50 percent duty and low tone frequencies, where the coil inductance does not limit the current, P_R18 is about 0.19 W. At 4 kHz the coil inductance lowers this toward the README's about 0.1 W estimate, but the datasheet gives no inductance to confirm it. The 33 ohm also leaves the buzzer at about 1.2 V DC drive, well below its rated 3.0 Vo-p, so the loudness will be under the datasheet's 75 dB minimum. For clicks that is acceptable.
findings.requirement: Resistor power rating 0.125 W (Uniroyal 0805W8); MLT-5020 max current 100 mA.
findings.consequence: Short 4 kHz clicks are fine. A bug or feature that holds GPIO2 high, or plays long low-frequency tones, can overheat R18 and overdrive the buzzer.
findings.fix: Firmware: allow slab_buzzer_tone only near the 4 kHz resonance (for example 3 to 5 kHz) with a time limit. Rev B: put R18 in a 1206 (0.25 W) or a 0.25 W 0805.

findings.title: DRV2605L VDD decoupling caps sit about 13 mm and two vias from the VDD pins; the REG cap is about 4.6 mm and two vias away
findings.evidence: C15 and C16 sit beside the pin 1 to 5 row, not the VDD row. The VDD current reaches them through about 4 mm of L1, a via, about 5 mm of L3, a via and about 3 mm more. The nearest other VSYS capacitors (C10, C9) are 7 to 8 mm away. HAPTIC_REG reaches C17 through 1.9 mm of L1, 2.7 mm of L3 and 2 vias.
findings.requirement: DRV2605L datasheet SLOS854D: pin table 'A 1-uF capacitor is required' on VDD and REG; 9.2.2.2 and layout guidelines (lines 3401, 3417-3418 of the text extraction): place the VDD decoupling capacitor and the REG capacitor close to the device pins.
findings.consequence: The ERM drive pulls pulsed current, so expect more supply ripple at the pins than intended. It probably still works with a 10 mm ERM. There is a small risk of resets or brown-out flags in DRV2605L STATUS during strong effects.
findings.fix: Rev A: none needed unless bring-up shows problems. A 1 uF 0402 can be tacked from pin 10 to the GND via at (-25.2,-37.5). Rev B: put C15 next to pins 6 and 10, and C17 next to pin 1.

findings.title: DRV2605L VDD on VSYS sits at the top of its recommended range on USB
findings.refs: U7 pins 6, 10 = VSYS; D1 B5819W from VBUS
findings.evidence: VSYS on USB = VBUS minus the Schottky drop. At light load (deep sleep, screen off) the drop is about 0.2 to 0.3 V, so a 5.25 V source gives about 5.0 V, and a 5.5 V Type-C source (vSafe5V upper limit) gives about 5.2 to 5.3 V.
findings.requirement: DRV2605L 6.3 recommended VDD 2 to 5.2 V; 6.1 absolute maximum 5.5 V.
findings.consequence: No damage expected, but there is little margin with high-voltage chargers.
findings.fix: None for rev A. Note it if a 5.5 V supply is ever used for bench tests.

findings.title: CH9102F RTS and DTR state with VDD5 at 0 V and VIO at 3.3 V is not specified; Q1 could hold EN or IO0 on battery
findings.refs: U2 pins 19 (RTS), 23 (DTR); Q1 UMH3N (B1=DTR, E1=RTS, C1=ESP_EN; B2=RTS, E2=DTR, C2=BOOT); U2 pin 5 VIO = 3V3, pins 7/8 = VBUS
findings.evidence: CH9102 datasheet v1.4 5.2 says only that with V3 and VDD5 at 0 V, VIO draws no current and does not back-feed. It does not give the output state of DTR and RTS in that case. Q1 conducts only when one line is low and the other high. If both are high-Z or both high, nothing happens.
findings.requirement: For the auto-reset circuit to stay inactive on battery, DTR and RTS must not sit at opposite levels.
findings.consequence: If they did sit at opposite levels, the board would not boot, or would boot into download mode, on battery alone. That is unlikely, because WCH recommends this dual-supply scheme for MCU boards.
findings.fix: On the first board, check that ESP_EN is at 3.3 V and BOOT is at 3.3 V with USB unplugged. If either one is low, remove Q1.

checked: MPR121 U6 every pin against NXP MPR121 datasheet Table 1: 1 IRQ->TOUCH_IRQ, 2 SCL, 3 SDA, 4 ADDR->3V3, 5 VREG->C14 100 nF, 6 VSS->GND, 7 REXT->R10, 8-16 ELE0-ELE8, 17-19 ELE9-11 unconnected, 20 VDD->3V3 with C13 100 nF (netlist.xml and .kicad_pcb pad nets agree)
MPR121 address: ADDR to VDD gives 0x5B (datasheet Table 10); firmware slab_pins.h uses 0x5B
MPR121 REXT R10 = 75k 1 percent (0603WAF7502T5E), as the datasheet requires (75 kOhm 1 percent to VSS); trace 1.73 mm
MPR121 power configuration: VDD 3.3 V > 2.75 V, so it must use Figure 2 (VDD supply, separate 0.1 uF on VREG). The board does this. Caps C13 and C14 sit about 1.4 mm from pins 20 and 5
MPR121 IRQ is open collector (datasheet pin 1); R11 10k pull-up to 3V3 on GPIO34 (input only, no internal pull-up), so the external pull-up is required and present
MPR121 QFN-20 footprint numbering is counter-clockwise from pin 1, no exposed pad; ELE0 via between the pad rows is allowed

Electrode mapping: the L4 zone centroids in the .kicad_pcb give ELE1 89.7, ELE2 44.7, ELE3 -0.3, ELE4 -45.3, ELE5 -90.3, ELE6 -135.3, ELE7 179.7, ELE8 134.7 deg, ELE0 centre. That is clockwise from 12 o'clock seen from the front, and matches SPEC, design.py SECTOR_ANGLES and firmware wheel.h
Unused ELE9-ELE11 are left open. Firmware ECR 0x89/0x09 enables only ELE0-ELE8
Firmware MPR121 autoconfig limits for 3.3 V match AN3889: USL (3.3-0.7)/3.3*256 = 201 (0xC9), TL 0.9*USL = 181 (0xB5), LSL 0.65*USL = 130 (0x82)

DRV2605L U7 every pin against TI SLOS854D DGS pin table: 1 REG->C17 1 uF, 2 SCL, 3 SDA, 4 IN/TRIG->GND (required if unused), 5 EN->R12 10k to 3V3, 6 VDD/NC->VSYS (allowed: 'tied to VDD or left floating'), 7 OUT+->M1, 8 GND, 9 OUT- ->M2, 10 VDD->VSYS with C15 1 uF + C16 100 nF
DRV2605L address fixed 0x5A (datasheet 7-bit 1011010); unique against 0x36 and 0x5B
DRV2605L EN, SDA and SCL limits are VDD+0.3 (6.1). They are pulled to 3V3, which is always at or below VSYS because 3V3 comes from VSYS through the RT9080. VIH 1.3 V is met by 3.3 V logic
DRV2605L standby with EN high: 4.1 uA typ, 7 uA max (6.5), consistent with the README's 4 uA budget; MODE resets to standby 0x40; firmware waits 250 us after power-up
DRV2605L with no motor: datasheet 8.4.4.1 says the outputs just toggle, with no damage; firmware plays effects only with CONFIG_SLAB_MOTOR_FITTED
DRV2605L caps: C17 and C15 are CL05A105KA5NQNC 1 uF 25 V X5R, matching the datasheet's 1 uF X5R/X7R for REG and VDD

CH9102F U2 every pin against the WCH CH9102 datasheet v1.4 section 4 (QFN24): 7 VDD5 and 8 VBUS on USB VBUS, 5 VIO on 3V3 (dual-supply scheme recommended in 5.2), 6 V3 with C2 100 nF only (correct when VDD5 > 3.6 V), 2 and EP 25 to GND, 3 UD+ and 4 UD- straight to the USB lines with no series resistors (required), 19 RTS, 20 RXD, 21 TXD, 23 DTR, 9 RST open (internal pull-up), other modem and GPIO pins open

UART direction: U2 pin 21 TXD -> R4 1k -> U0RXD -> U1 module pin 30 (RXD0, GPIO3); U1 pin 31 (TXD0, GPIO1) -> U0TXD -> R3 1k -> U2 pin 20 RXD. Checked against the ESP32-PICO-MINI-02 datasheet v1.8 Table 3
CH9102F decoupling: C25 100 nF on VDD5/VBUS plus C1 10 uF at J1, C2 100 nF on V3 about 1.7 mm away, C3 100 nF on VIO about 2.8 mm away

UMH3N Q1 pinout against the CJ datasheet drawing: Tr1 E1 pin 1, B1 pin 2, C1 pin 6; Tr2 E2 pin 4, B2 pin 5, C2 pin 3; two DTC143T, R1 4.7k. Netlist: Tr1 B=DTR, E=RTS, C=EN; Tr2 B=RTS, E=DTR, C=IO0. That is the standard ESP32 circuit (RTS active with DTR inactive pulls EN low; DTR active with RTS inactive pulls IO0 low; both active or both inactive does nothing). Base drive 0.55 mA, hFE >= 100
EN RC: R5 10k and C4 1 uF give about 14 ms to reach the EN threshold, inside esptool's 50 ms reset-to-release delay
USBLC6-2SC6 U8 pinout: 1 and 6 I/O1 = D-, 3 and 4 I/O2 = D+, 2 GND, 5 VBUS. The layout is flow-through: connector side enters pins 6 and 4, chip side leaves pins 1 and 3 toward U2

Buzzer: BZ1 pad 1 '+' to BZ_P (VSYS side), pad 2 '-' to BZ_N (Q6 drain), pad 3 unconnected. Footprint pads match the MLT-5020 drawing (top view: + bottom-left, - bottom-right, chamfer top-right, third terminal top-left)
Flyback D2 B5819W: pad 1 is the cathode (EasyEDA SOD-123 silk triangle and bar on the pad 1 side; symbol pin 1 '-'), on BZ_P, anode on BZ_N. Correct orientation for a low-side switch
Q6 and Q5 AO3400A: SOT-23 pin 1 G, 2 S, 3 D matches netlist and footprint. Vgs(th) max 1.45 V, Rds(on) under 48 mOhm at 2.5 V, so it is fully on from 3.3 V GPIO
GPIO2 strap: R19 100R into the gate, R20 100k to GND plus the internal pull-down keep GPIO2 low at reset, so download mode works
Backlight: Q5 low-side on LEDK, R15 100R gate, R16 100k pull-down (backlight off during reset and deep sleep). GPIO4 is not a strapping pin. LEDC 40 kHz x 10 bit fits the 80 MHz APB clock
Backlight current on battery: 4.15 V gives at most about 145 mA, inside the screen spec's 200 mA

I2C: R31 and R32 4.7k to 3V3. Addresses 0x36 (MAX17048), 0x5A (DRV2605L), 0x5B (MPR121) are all different. SDA is 134 mm long with 8 vias, SCL 100 mm with 7 vias, about 40 to 50 pF in total, giving about 200 ns rise time with 4.7k. That is inside the 1000 ns standard-mode and 300 ns fast-mode limits. Pull-up sink current 0.7 mA. Firmware default 100 kHz
ESP32 pins for my blocks against the module datasheet: EN pin 8, IO0 pin 23, IO2 pin 22, IO4 pin 24, IO20 pin 26 (SCL), IO22 pin 34 (SDA), I34 pin 9 (TOUCH_IRQ)
Passive part numbers in jlcpcb/stock.json: R10 1 percent 75k, R17 0.25 W 1206, R18 0.125 W 0805, 100 nF X7R 16 V, 1 uF X5R 25 V
not_checked: MAX17048 pins and electrical limits: the local datasheet C2682616.pdf is a 14 KB stub and the part is outside my area. I only checked its I2C address 0x36 against the other two devices

KT-0603R (LED1) polarity against a manufacturer datasheet: no datasheet in the folder. Polarity is consistent with LCSC's own symbol and footprint, and the README already lists the LED1 cathode in the JLC preview checks

FH35C rated current per contact: the local Hirose drawing has no ratings table. The 0.2 A figure comes from distributor listings (https://my.avnet.com/abacus/manufacturers/m/hirose-electric/products/fh35c-series-flexible-printed-circuit-connectors/ , https://www.digikey.com/en-US/product-highlight/h/hirose/ffc-fpc)

Pin input capacitance of MPR121, MAX17048 and DRV2605L: not specified in the datasheets I read. The I2C capacitance total uses estimates of about 5 to 10 pF per pin

No kicad-cli runs; I parsed netlist.xml and the .kicad_pcb with python3 -I. Scratch files are in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-dave-projects-assistant/7e2488f2-c1f8-48ea-8311-4ecfb642e182/scratchpad/review-work/periph-ics/

verdicts.reasoning: I reproduced this from primary sources. Netlist: LCD_LEDA = R17 pin 2 + J2 pins 14 and 15 only. VSYS goes through R17 10R. LCD_LEDK = J2 pin 1 + Q5 drain. LEDA has no capacitor, so it sits at VSYS when Q5 is off and at VSYS - 10 ohm x I_LED when Q5 is on. That is a 1.2 to 2.2 V square wave at the PWM rate. My own parse of the .kicad_pcb (device transform X0 150, Y0 70; wheel centre (0,-27.75)) gives LCD_LEDA 11.91 mm on In2.Cu inside r 17.1. It also gives 4.61 mm on F.Cu and 2 vias, at (-8.60,-25.88) and (-5.89,-36.67). These match README Verification lines 255-256. Yet design.py DISC_L3_NETS (line 401) and README line 123 list LCD_LEDA under 'DC and static nets'. That classification is wrong. The charge per edge (about 0.6 pF x 2 V) is the same order as the accepted LCD_CS exception (11.85 mm, 3.3 V). The firmware already knows: slab_backlight.h lines 5-8 say LEDA 'swings at the PWM rate'. Kconfig SLAB_BL_PWM_HZ picks the frequency from the bring-up noise table. slab_backlight_set_permille holds the pin at 0 and 1000 permille. README line 293 asks to 'pick a backlight PWM frequency that does not show up as touch noise'. So the operational mitigation exists, and only the documented reasoning is wrong. One limit on the fallback: on USB the duty cap is 800 permille (SLAB_BL_USB_MAX_PERMILLE), so on USB the 'hold at 1000' option cannot be used and the backlight always PWMs. The VSYS ripple part of the claim (tens of mV with C9 22 uF nearby) is real but second order. My measurement: VSYS has 23.63 mm of L3 and 3 vias inside r 17.1.
verdicts.fix: Rev A: no hardware change. Keep the bring-up noise sweep across PWM frequencies, which already covers LEDA, and if no frequency is clean, synchronise PWM changes or pause PWM around MPR121 scans. Correct README line 123 and the DISC_L3_NETS comment to class LCD_LEDA as a switching net (an accepted exception with its 11.91 mm / 2-via cap in DISC_L3_ACCEPTED), so verify.py guards it. Rev B: move R17 to the cathode side (LEDA tied straight to VSYS, R17 between LEDK and Q5 drain) so LEDA is truly static, or keep LEDA off L3 inside r 17.1.

verdicts.reasoning: The corner math holds. The real risk is smaller than the finding says, and it lives in firmware. Screen spec DLC-T2.7DDS#1 p.6: IF 200 mA (TYP column, no MAX given); VF 2.7 to 3.3 V at 200 mA; note 2 says life drops above 200 mA. BOM: R17 = C17903 (1206W4, 0.25 W); D1 B5819W from VBUS to VSYS. With VBUS 5.25 V and about 0.35 V across D1, VSYS is about 4.9 V. With VF 2.7 V, I_peak is about 215 to 220 mA, so P(R17) at 100 percent duty is about 0.46 W. The firmware model (slab_backlight.h: VF0 2800 mV, 11.5 ohm) predicts 183 mA at VSYS 4.9 V, so its power cap (P_MAX 231 mW) allows 690 permille. Real average power at that duty is about 0.32 W, 1.27x the rating. So the claim that the cap underestimates in the VF-min corner is confirmed. In the shipped player config the corner is not reached: player_power.c calls slab_bl_plan(CONFIG_SLAB_BL_BRIGHTNESS_PCT=80, ...). That targets about 63 mA average, a duty of about 342 permille, so real R17 average is about 0.16 W at the worst corner. Real power passes 0.25 W only if brightness is set above about 127 percent (Kconfig allows up to 150). Bring-up runs 600 permille (bringup.c lines 280, 460, 682), which gives about 0.28 W only in the 5.25 V / VF-min corner. It also runs short 1000-permille noise cases (limited to 12 samples on USB, line 389). Both are short-time overloads that a thick-film 1206 tolerates. FH35C: web sources (Hirose product pages FH35C-25S/33S, Avnet series page) give 0.2 A rated current, 30 V. The local C2889267.pdf is a drawing with no rating, so I could not confirm this from the Hirose datasheet itself. Contact ratings are thermal. RMS through J2 pin 1 is about 215 mA x sqrt(0.342), about 126 mA, at default brightness. The panel's own FPC carries its rated 200 mA through its one LEDK finger by design, so the contact is a note, not a defect. Severity stays minor: R17 has less margin than the README claims, and the firmware cap is not conservative.
verdicts.fix: Rev A, firmware only. Compute the R17 power cap from a worst-case model, VF 2.7 V with R 10 ohm (I = (VSYS - 2700)/10), not from the brightness model. Also cap SLAB_BL_BRIGHTNESS_PCT at 100 in Kconfig. With that model, P_MAX 231 mW gives about 500 permille at VSYS 4.9 V, which still exceeds the default brightness duty. Optional BOM swap if desired: a 0.5 W 1206 10R (anti-surge/high-power series) or 12R. Not needed for rev A.

verdicts.reasoning: The numbers reproduce. Buzzer spec C94598 p.2: coil 12 +-3 ohm, rated 3.0 Vo-p, operating 2 to 4 Vo-p, current max 100 mA; drive is a 4000 Hz square wave at 1/2 duty. BOM: R18 = C17634 (0805W8, 1/8 W). Netlist: VSYS -> R18 -> BZ_P -> BZ1 -> BZ_N -> Q6 drain; D2 is across the buzzer. Steady-on at VSYS 4.8 to 4.9 V gives 107 to 117 mA (coil 12 or 9 ohm), so P(R18) is about 0.38 to 0.40 W. That is 3x the rating and slightly over the buzzer's 100 mA. At 50 percent duty, the resistive-only upper bound is about 0.19 W. The coil inductance is not in the datasheet, so the README's about 0.1 W at 4 kHz (line 270) can be neither confirmed nor refuted. No shipped firmware path reaches an overload, though. slab_buzzer.c set() clamps duty to 50 percent. Clicks last milliseconds. The bring-up noise case (bringup.c line 379) runs 4 kHz at 25 percent, about 0.1 W even resistive-only. The bring-up beeps (line 499) are 150 ms. CONFIG_SLAB_CLICK_HZ ranges 500 to 8000 Hz but is used only for short clicks. R20 100k holds Q6 off at reset and while GPIO2 is an input. The overload needs a firmware fault that drives GPIO2 high as GPIO, or a long low-frequency tone. On ESP-IDF's default panic-reboot this resets quickly. That makes it a note: the design works, and the margin matters only in a fault.
verdicts.fix: Firmware: in slab_buzzer_tone, allow only 3 to 5 kHz and keep the 50 percent clamp. Add a maximum continuous on-time, for example 500 ms, enforced by the existing esp_timer. Never drive GPIO2 as a plain GPIO output. Rev B: put R18 in a 0.25 W part (1206 or a 0.25 W 0805).

verdicts.reasoning: Pad positions from the .kicad_pcb (device coordinates): U7 pins 6 and 10 (VSYS) are at (-26.20,-36.35) and (-24.20,-36.35). C16 pin 1 (VSYS) is at (-23.42,-42.60) and C15 pin 1 at (-25.42,-42.60), both on the far side of the pin 1 to 5 row (y -41.05). Traced copper: the pins join on a 0.2 mm F.Cu track at y -35.42. A 0.4 mm F.Cu track then runs to the via at (-21.09,-36.39), about 4.7 mm of L1. In2.Cu continues (-21.09,-36.39)->(-21.09,-41.00)->(-23.42,-43.33), 7.9 mm of L3, to the via at (-23.42,-43.33). From there 0.73 mm of F.Cu reaches C16, and C15 hangs off a further L3/via branch at (-25.68,-43.33). That is about 13 mm and 2 vias, as claimed. The nearest other VSYS caps are C10 at (-22.3,-29.08), 7.5 mm from pin 10, and C9 at (-18.85,-28.6). HAPTIC_REG: pin 1 (-24.20,-41.05), about 1.1 mm of F.Cu, via (-24.06,-40.01), 2.7 mm of In2.Cu, via (-21.90,-38.71), 0.77 mm of F.Cu, C17 pin 1 at (-22.60,-38.88). That is about 4.6 mm and 2 vias, as claimed. DRV2605L SLOS854D pin table (pins 1 and 10): 'A 1-uF capacitor is required'. Section 11.1: VDD decoupling and the REG filter cap 'should be placed close to the device pin'. Both are violated. Impact is limited: CONFIG_SLAB_MOTOR_FITTED defaults to n, and with no motor U7 draws only standby or idle current. It matters only for the optional ERM upgrade, and probably still works then with C9 22 uF 7.5 mm away and solid GND planes. One correction to the reviewer's rework: the GND via at (-25.2,-37.5) lies under the U7 body (body about x -26.7 to -23.7, y -40.2 to -37.2), so a cap cannot be tacked there.
verdicts.fix: Rev A: none for the default build (no motor).
