If the motor is fitted and bring-up shows DRV2605L resets or faults during strong effects, tack a 1 uF 0402 across the exposed VSYS track near (-22.9,-35.25) and C17's GND pad or via at (-22.6,-37.92)/(-21.85,-37.92), scraping solder mask on the track as needed. Rev B: put C15 (1 uF) next to pins 6 and 10 on the same side, and C17 next to pin 1 with no vias.

verdicts.reasoning: Netlist: U7 pins 6 and 10 = VSYS; D1 B5819W anode on VBUS, cathode on VSYS. Q3 AO3401A (S=VSYS, D=VBAT, G=VBUS) gives no unclamped VBUS path to VSYS. DRV2605L SLOS854D 6.3: recommended VDD 2 to 5.2 V. 6.1 and 8.4.1.2: absolute maximum 5.5 V. USB 2.0 ports give at most 5.25 V and Type-C vSafe5V at most 5.5 V. B5819W drops roughly 0.15 to 0.3 V at light load, so VSYS can reach about 5.0 to 5.35 V. That is above the recommended maximum with a 5.5 V source, but below the absolute maximum. EN is held high by R12 10k to 3V3, so U7 sits in standby on VSYS whenever 3V3 is up. Reverse leakage and hot-plug overshoot are damped by C9 22 uF behind D1. No damage is expected.
verdicts.fix: None for rev A. Avoid bench supplies above 5.25 V on VBUS. For rev B, consider feeding U7 from a point that cannot exceed 5.2 V, or accept the condition as is.

verdicts.reasoning: Netlist: DTR = U2 pin 23 + Q1 pin 2 (B1) + Q1 pin 4 (E2). RTS = U2 pin 19 + Q1 pin 1 (E1) + Q1 pin 5 (B2). Q1 pin 6 (C1) = ESP_EN with R5 10k pull-up and C4 1 uF; Q1 pin 3 (C2) = BOOT with R6. That is the standard cross-coupled auto-reset. A transistor conducts only when its base is high and its emitter low, so EN or IO0 is pulled low only if DTR and RTS sit at opposite driven levels. CH9102 datasheet v1.4 section 5.2 (my read of the Chinese text) covers the case where V3 and VDD5 lose power (0 V). It says VIO draws current only as in suspend (no current when outputs are unloaded and inputs float or are high) and does not back-feed V3 or VDD5. It never states the DTR and RTS output levels in that state. The finding's premise is therefore accurate. Two things point to safe behaviour. WCH names this dual-supply scheme (VDD5 from USB, VIO shared with the MCU) as its recommended scheme. And 'no VIO current with unloaded outputs' implies the outputs are high or high-Z, either of which leaves Q1 off. README line 94 also assumes 'U2 unpowered' on battery. Only the first board can settle the question.
verdicts.fix: Bring-up check on the first board: with USB unplugged and the battery connected, measure ESP_EN (U1 pin 8) and BOOT/IO0 (U1 pin 23) at about 3.3 V, and confirm a normal boot from battery alone. If either is low, remove Q1 and keep using the BOOT and RESET buttons. COVERAGE (this verifier): I checked the LEDA L3 length and vias by parsing the PCB myself; LEDA, LEDK, BZ_P, BZ_N, HAPTIC_REG, VSYS, DTR, RTS, ESP_EN and BOOT pin assignments from netlist.xml; the backlight current and R17 power against the screen spec p.6 and the firmware model in slab_backlight_math.c and player_power.c; R18 and buzzer currents against MLT-5020 spec p.2; DRV2605L pad positions, VSYS and REG routing, and decoupling against SLOS854D pin table, 6.1, 6.3 and 11.1; and CH9102 section 5.2. NOT CHECKED: the Hirose FH35C current rating from a Hirose datasheet (the local PDF is a drawing; I used Hirose product pages and the Avnet series page via web search); MLT-5020 coil inductance (not in its spec); the B5819W VF curve at specific currents (I used typical values).

areas.title: Connectors, switches and pinouts

findings.title: Copper tracks and vias inside the DM3AT 'No conductive traces' areas under J3
findings.refs: J3 DM3AT-SF-PEJM5 at KiCad (164.05, 110.79) rot 0 (device centre (-14.05, -40.79)); F.Cu tracks and vias under the socket body; harmony-mark8-slab.kicad_pcb
findings.evidence: I took the hatched 'No conductive traces' areas (note 3) from the Hirose DM3 catalog, Recommended PCB mounting pattern, page 3. I scaled them from the drawing at 600 dpi and placed them in J3 footprint-local coordinates (pad 1 at x 2.85, contact pad edge y -6.95, P = 1.1). The pad positions match the footprint (pads 10, 11 and 12 at 3.7, 9.9 and 14.05 below the contact row), so the placement is reliable to about 0.1 mm. These F.Cu items fall inside the areas: (1) VBAT, a 0.4 mm track from local (-5.45, -1.24) to (2.7, -3.14), i.e. device (-8.6, -39.55) to (-16.75, -37.65). It crosses the 8.2 x 1.6 mm area at local y -2.55 to -0.95. A VBAT via sits at its end, inside the area. (2) SD_CD, 0.2 mm track from local (-5.95, -3.94) to (-6.0, 0.76) and on to pad 11. It runs along the strip at x -6.08 to -5.39, next to the card-detect spring. Another SD_CD segment and an SD_CS via at (-6.3, -5.79) are in the strip between the contact row and pad 11. (3) A 3V3_PERIPH via at (-7.2, -2.19) with its track, and a VBUS via and track at (-7.32, 0 to -0.89), on the edge of the same strip. (4) GND vias at (-5.84, 6.57) and (5.7, 7.55); these are harmless. My script is review-work/connectors/scripts/keepout.py.
findings.requirement: Hirose DM3 series catalog, DM3AT-SF-PEJM5, 'Recommended PCB mounting pattern', note 3: hatched areas = 'No conductive traces'. These areas sit under the metal eject mechanism and card-detect spring, which touch or come close to the board surface.
findings.consequence: The board works as built if the solder mask stays intact. Over many card insertions, a metal part of the socket (shell at GND, or the card-detect spring on SD_CD) can wear through the mask. VBAT or VBUS could then short to GND, or SD_CD could short to VBAT and put battery voltage on GPIO15. JLC 'plugged' vias are covered, which lowers the risk at the vias. The tracks are the main exposure.
findings.fix: Rev A: accept the risk, and check the mask under J3 on the first boards if a card-detect fault shows up. Rev B: move the VBAT, VBUS, 3V3_PERIPH, SD_CS and SD_CD copper out of the three hatched areas on L1, or drop it to L3 there. Add a keep-out rule area for these areas to the J3 footprint so DRC enforces them.

findings.title: No pull-up on SD CMD (MOSI, J3 pin 3)
findings.refs: J3 pad 3 net SD_MOSI (GPIO19, module pin 33); design.py J3 block (pull-ups R21 MISO, R22 CS, R23 DAT1, R24 DAT2 only)
findings.evidence: DAT0 (R21), DAT3/CS (R22), DAT1 (R23) and DAT2 (R24) have 10k pull-ups to 3V3_PERIPH. CMD/MOSI has none (netlist: SD_MOSI connects only U1 pin 33 and J3 pin 3). CLK correctly has no pull-up.
findings.requirement: SD Physical Layer Simplified Specification, bus topology and line loading: CMD and DAT0 to DAT3 need pull-ups (R_CMD, R_DAT, 10k to 100k) so the lines do not float while no host drives them. Espressif's SD pull-up requirements also list CMD among the lines that need one. I am working from memory of both documents and did not re-read either.
findings.consequence: Between power-up of 3V3_PERIPH and SPI bus setup, and whenever the firmware releases GPIO19, CMD floats. Most cards tolerate this in SPI mode, but some fail to enter SPI mode reliably or draw extra current.
findings.fix: Firmware: enable the GPIO19 internal pull-up (about 45k) before turning Q4 on, and keep MOSI driven or pulled while the card has power. Rev B: add a 10k from SD_MOSI to 3V3_PERIPH next to R21 to R24.

findings.title: Screen VCC runs at the top of its rated range
findings.refs: J2 pins 9, 10, 11 (IOVCC, VCC, VCC) on 3V3_PERIPH from U4 RT9080-33 through Q4
findings.evidence: VCC and IOVCC both come from the 3.3 V rail through the Q4 P-FET, which drops a few mV.
findings.requirement: DLC-T2.7DDS#1 spec v1.0 page 6, Electrical characteristics: VCC 2.4 min, 2.75 typ, 3.3 V max; IOVCC 1.65 to 3.3 V. Page 5: absolute maximum 4.6 V.
findings.consequence: A high-tolerance regulator can put VCC slightly above the 3.3 V operating maximum. That is well under the 4.6 V absolute maximum, so damage is unlikely, but it has no margin. I did not confirm the RT9080 output tolerance here.
findings.fix: None for rev A. If the screen misbehaves, measure 3V3_PERIPH at C19.

findings.title: The full backlight current goes through the single LEDK contact of J2
findings.refs: J2 pin 1 LCD_LEDK to Q5 drain; LEDA on pins 14 and 15 through R17 10R from VSYS
findings.evidence: The screen FPC has one LEDK pin (spec page 5). With VSYS 4.7 V on USB and VF 2.7 to 3.3 V, the LED current is (4.7 - VF) / 10 = 140 to 200 mA at 100 percent duty, all of it through J2 contact 1.
findings.requirement: DLC spec page 6: IF 200 mA total. FH35C contact current rating: I believe it is about 0.2 A per contact, but the LCSC drawing (C2889267) does not state it, so this is unconfirmed.
findings.consequence: Contact 1 can run at or near its rating while the backlight is at full duty on USB. README note 3 already caps the duty at 80 percent on USB, which keeps the average current below the rating.
findings.fix: Keep the firmware duty cap. Rev B could add series resistance or use a constant-current driver.

findings.title: Screen FPC width tolerance is wider than the FH35C slot allows
findings.refs: J2 FH35C-15S-0.3SHW(50); screen FPC tail
findings.evidence: Screen drawing (DLC-T2.7DDS1-mechanical-400dpi.png, tail dimensions): tail width 4.80 +-0.1, pitch 0.3, 15 contacts, thickness 0.20 +-0.03.
findings.requirement: Hirose FH35C drawing EDC3-338903-01, page 2 and table page 4: for 15 contacts, FPC width F = 4.8 +-0.05, slot reference width D = 4.83, FPC t = 0.2 +-0.03.
findings.consequence: A tail at the top of its tolerance (4.9 mm) is wider than the 4.83 mm slot and may not seat fully. A nominal 4.80 tail fits. The thickness and pitch match.
findings.fix: If the tail binds when inserted, trim it lightly. Do not force it, because the connector contacts deform (FH35C page 5).

checked: J2 screen pin map, from screen spec page 5 to the KiCad pads: 1 LEDK=LCD_LEDK, 2 GND, 3 FMARK=LCD_TE, 4 SDA=LCD_MOSI, 5 SCLK=LCD_SCK, 6 RS=LCD_DC, 7 CS=LCD_CS, 8 RESET=LCD_RST, 9 IOVCC and 10, 11 VCC=3V3_PERIPH, 12, 13 GND, 14, 15 LEDA=LCD_LEDA; fittings 16 and 17 GND. design.py, netlist.xml and the .kicad_pcb pads all agree.

Screen FPC orientation from the vendor drawing (front and back views): the tail runs +X, pin 1 is on the -Y edge, the contacts face +Z (front view shows the gold fingers, back view shows the 3.5 mm stiffener).

Effect of the FPC route on pin order: the S-bend down to the back plate turns about X twice in opposite directions, so the contacts still face +Z. The 180-degree fold about a Y-parallel line maps (x,y,z) to (-x,y,-z), so the contacts face -Z (away from the PCB) and pin 1 stays at -Y. The ramp S-curve keeps both. Result: FPC pin 1 (LEDK) lands at the -Y end of the slot.

J2 footprint in device coordinates (KiCad rot 270 = -90): the slot faces +X; pad 1 is at (-2.47, -41.1), the -Y end, with net LCD_LEDK. So screen pin 1 meets connector contact 1 after the fold. Pad 15 LEDA is at (-2.47, -36.9). The silk pin-1 dot and the '1' label sit at the -Y end.

FH35C opening side: datasheet page 1 (top view and side view a) puts the FPC opening and the metal fittings on the contact No.1 row (0.8 mm pads) and the back-flip actuator on the contact No.2 row. The footprint has the odd pads and fittings at local +Y, which points to device +X, toward the ramp. The pad sizes match the Hirose land pattern: 0.3 wide, 0.8 and 0.65 long, rows 2.88 apart, fittings 0.4 x 0.95.

FH35C contact type: it is dual contact. Page 2 shows both 'Contact No.1 (Bottom contact)' and '(Top contact)', and page 5 covers 'using contacts on the top'. The FPC enters with its contacts facing away from the PCB (top contacts), which the connector supports. Pin numbers are physical positions, so the contact face does not change the mapping.

ASSEMBLY.md steps 7 to 9 agree with the derivation: fold 180 degrees, contacts up toward the viewer (device -Z), pin 1 toward the USB-C end (-Y), slot faces left when viewed from the back (device +X), latch on the right (device -X).

Screen interface: the FPC has no IM or mode pins (fixed 4-line SPI, spec pages 3 and 5). TE goes to GPIO39, which is input only and suits an output from the screen. RESET goes to GPIO32. The backlight is low-side switched: LEDK to the Q5 AO3400A drain, LEDA through R17 10R from VSYS.

Screen FPC tail against FH35C: pitch 0.3, 15 contacts, conductor span 4.2 (C = 4.2 for 15S), width 4.8, thickness 0.20 +-0.03 (FH35C needs t = 0.2 +-0.03), stiffener on the side away from the contacts.

J3 DM3AT pin map against Hirose catalog page 3: pad 1 DAT2=SD_DAT2, 2 CD/DAT3=SD_CS, 3 CMD=SD_MOSI, 4 VDD=3V3_PERIPH, 5 CLK=SD_SCK, 6 VSS=GND, 7 DAT0=SD_MISO, 8 DAT1=SD_DAT1. Pad 1 is 3.2 mm from the card centre line, as the datasheet gives.

J3 card-detect switch: by position on the catalog drawing, pad 9 (next to contact 8) is switch B and pad 11 (left column, 9.9 below the contact row) is switch A. Pads 10, 12, 13 and 14 are the four cover ground points the catalog describes. The switch is normally open and closes with a card in. Pad 11 = SD_CD with R25 100k to the always-on 3V3; pad 9 = GND. A card pulls SD_CD low. Firmware slab_pins.h says 'low when a card is in', which matches.
J3 pull-ups: R21 DAT0, R22 CS, R23 DAT1 and R24 DAT2, each 10k to 3V3_PERIPH. CLK has none, which is correct. CMD has none (finding CONN-2). The card slot faces device -Y.

J1 USB-C pad order against the HRO TYPE-C-31-M-12 'Recommend PCB layout (component side)': A1/B12, A4/B9, B8, A5, B7, A6, A7, B6, A8, B5, B4/A9, B1/A12 from left to right, matching footprint local x -3.2 to +3.2, with the opening toward the PCB edge (local +Y, device -Y). The footprint is not mirrored.

J1 nets: A5=CC1 through R1 5.1k to GND and B5=CC2 through R2 5.1k to GND, separate resistors (USB Type-C Rd = 5.1k). A6 and B6 both USB_DP; A7 and B7 both USB_DN. Both combined VBUS pads (A4B9, B4A9) are VBUS and both combined GND pads are GND. SBU1 and SBU2 are not connected. Shell THT pads 1 to 4 go to GND. The NPTH pegs are 5.8 apart and the shell slots 8.66 x 4.18 apart, as the datasheet gives (5.78, 8.65, 4.18).

J4 JST PH SMD (XYECONN drawing): signal pads are at the back and the solder tabs at the mating side. In the footprint the tabs are at local +Y, which becomes device +Y at rot 180, so the cable enters along +Y, as intended. Pad 1 = GND at device (-22.0, -17.86), pad 2 = BAT_P at (-20.0, -17.86). Silkscreen '-' is at (-23.3, -18.96), next to pad 1, and '+' at (-18.7, -18.96), next to pad 2, which matches the README. Pad 1 at local x -1 follows the usual JST PH SM4 numbering. Tab pads 3 and 4 have no net (mechanical only).

SW2 and SW3 TS-1088-AR02016 (XunPu drawing): a 2-terminal switch, circuit diagram 1 to 2, with no internally paired pins, so a wrong pair is not possible. SW2: pad 1 BOOT, pad 2 GND, R6 10k pull-up. SW3: pad 1 ESP_EN, pad 2 GND, R5 10k and C4 1 uF. 'R' in the part number means no locating post, so no hole is needed. The land is 1.23 x 1.86 at +-2.18, close to the datasheet 1.05 x 2.0 at +-2.225.

SW1 Alps SKRTLAE010 circuit diagram: terminals 1 and 3 are common and terminal 2 switches against them. The footprint has 1=GND, 3=GND, 2=SIDE_BTN, so a press pulls SIDE_BTN low with no stuck-pressed risk. Mounting tabs 4 and 5 are GND, the two 0.9 NPTH guide holes are 4.25 apart, and the pad row is 3.2 wide x 1.8 long. No F.Cu track lies in the Alps 'Prohibited area of copper tracks' between the tabs. R26 100k pull-up and C23 100 nF on SIDE_BTN; GPIO38 is an RTC GPIO, so ext0 wake works.

Test pads TP1 to TP10: 1.0 mm circles on F.Cu with a mask opening and no paste. Nets: 3V3, VSYS, VBAT, GND, U0TXD, U0RXD, GPIO7, GPIO8, I2C_SDA, I2C_SCL. This is exactly the SPEC 6 list, and it agrees between design.py, netlist.xml and the PCB.
CPL rotations for J1 0, J2 270, J3 0, J4 180, SW1 270, SW2 and SW3 90 match the KiCad angles of the EasyEDA/JLC footprints, as listed in rotation-check.csv.

J2 actuator clearance: the closed actuator ends at device x -6.44 and the J3 body starts at -7.195, 0.75 mm away. The back-flip actuator swings up within J2's own footprint, so the two parts do not collide.
not_checked: The FH35C contact current rating: the LCSC drawing has no ratings table. CONN-4 is low confidence for this reason.

Fold line position: whether the 25.2 mm fold mark in ASSEMBLY.md and the enclosure fpc.py length budget put the tail tip at the slot. I checked pin order and contact face, not FPC length. Only a test against the real FPC settles this (README 'Check before paying' item 4).
Which wire is + on the LiPo pack: the XYECONN drawing does not number its pins, and the pack wiring is outside the board. The README already tells Dave to check the pack with a meter.
JLC's own placement preview for J1 to J4 and SW1: this needs the JLC web tool. I checked only that the CPL angles equal the KiCad angles of the EasyEDA footprints.
The DM3AT and SKRT keep-out areas on L1 GND pour copper (zone fill): GND pour is the same net as the shells, so I did not parse the filled zones.
SD and screen signal integrity, and ESD on the external connectors other than USB (no ESD parts on the microSD or side-button lines): outside this connector-mapping pass.
UMH3N Q1 auto-reset wiring and the U8 ESD part: left to the USB and power reviewers.
Exact RT9080 output tolerance for CONN-3: I did not read the C841192 datasheet in this pass.

verdicts.reasoning: Requirement checked in the primary source: Hirose DM3 catalog C114218.pdf p.3, DM3AT-SF-PEJM5 'Recommended PCB mounting pattern', note 3 'No conductive traces' on the hatched areas. I scaled the drawing myself (55.3 px/mm, using the 8.2MIN/8.9MIN and 4.4MAX/6MIN/14.1MAX dimensions). As a scale check, pad 14 (x 4.4), pad 10 (y -3.85 to -2.65), pad 11 (2.55 to 3.35) and pad 12 (5.7 to 8.5) in lib/Harmony8.pretty/DM3AT-SF-PEJM5.kicad_mod all land on the drawing within 0.05 mm. My areas in footprint-local mm: bar C x -5.35..3.35, y -2.55..-0.95 (4.4 to 6.0 below the contact-pad edge at y -6.95); card-detect strip B x -5.98..-5.31, y -1.24..6.34; side column A (between pads 10, 11 and 12) x -7.12..-6.40, y -7.08..0.97; bottom-right D x 3.04..5.58, y 7.15..8.47. These match the other reviewer's areas to within about 0.1 mm. J3 is at KiCad (164.05, 110.79), rot 0. I parsed harmony-mark8-slab.kicad_pcb with my own script (review-work/connectors-verify/ko.py). Results: VBAT (net 65) is a 0.4 mm F.Cu track from (-5.45,-1.24) to (2.7,-3.14). It crosses all of bar C and enters strip B, and the VBAT via at (-5.45,-1.24) sits inside both. SD_CD (net 49) tracks (-7.02,-7.74)->(-7.02,-5.79)->(-6.9,-5.69)->(-5.95,-3.94)->(-6.0,0.76)->(-6.75,2.34) run inside column A and strip B. The SD_CS via at (-6.3,-5.79) overlaps column A by about 0.15 mm. The 3V3_PERIPH via at (-7.2,-2.19) and its 0.4 mm track overlap A by about 0.17 mm. The VBUS 0.4 mm track at x -7.32 only reaches A's edge (overlap 0.004 mm, which is inside the drawing tolerance). The GND items (pad-10 stub, vias at (-5.84,6.57) and (5.7,7.55), F.Cu GND pour) are harmless because the shell is GND. The only F.Cu zone is GND, and the footprint has no extra mask openings, so all of this copper is under solder mask. The reviewer's facts reproduce. Consequence: there is no failure as built. The risk comes from mask wear by the socket's metal parts over card cycles. The worst case is VBAT to the GND shell (an unfused battery short that relies on the pack's protection circuit), or VBAT through the via in strip B onto the card-detect spring, which would put up to 4.2 V on GPIO15 (over the ESP32's 3.6 V absolute maximum). Plugged vias are covered by mask. This is minor: the risk is low-probability and long-term, and Hirose explicitly forbids the layout. Coverage checked as correct: J3 pad nets match design.py (1 DAT2, 2 CS, 3 CMD/MOSI, 4 3V3_PERIPH, 5 CLK, 6 GND, 7 DAT0/MISO, 8 DAT1, 9/10/12/13/14 GND, 11 SD_CD), and the footprint pitch is 1.1 mm.
verdicts.fix: Rev A: the cheapest real fix before ordering is to move the VBAT segment (-5.45,-1.24)->(2.7,-3.14) and its via out of bar C and strip B. VBAT is on WHEEL_TOLERANT_NETS, so it may run on L3 there. If re-routing is not practical now, accept the risk and inspect the mask under J3 on the first boards if a card-detect fault or a battery drain shows up. Rev B: add rule-area keep-outs (F.Cu tracks and vias) for the four hatched areas to the DM3AT footprint so DRC enforces them. Move VBAT, SD_CD, SD_CS and 3V3_PERIPH copper out of them.

verdicts.reasoning: Topology confirmed from primary sources. In netlist.xml, /SD_MOSI connects only J3 pin 3 (CMD) and U1 pin 33 (IO19). design.py lines 224-228 give pull-ups only on SD_MISO (R21), SD_CS (R22), SD_DAT1 (R23) and SD_DAT2 (R24), plus R25 on SD_CD. SPEC.md line 146 also lists SD_MOSI with no pull-up, but neither SPEC nor README gives a reason, so this is not an accepted exception. Requirement confirmed: the ESP-IDF 'SD Pull-up Requirements' page (docs.espressif.com, fetched today) says that in SPI mode or 1-bit SD mode the CMD and DATA (DAT0-DAT3) lines 'must be pulled up by 10 kΩ resistors'. It also says internal weak pull-ups cannot guarantee reliability. The Espressif HDG (hdg.txt §1.3.13) covers SDIO-mode pull-ups only. I did not re-read the SD Association spec. The reviewer's stated consequence is mostly wrong for this firmware. In firmware/mark-8/components/slab_board/slab_power_seq.c (lines 5-11 and 24-31), slab_periph_on() drives SD_MOSI low as an output before it pulls PERIPH_EN_N low. bench_storage_mount() refuses to run unless the peripheral rail is on, and spi_bus_initialize then drives MOSI. So CMD is never left floating while the card has power. At reset and in deep sleep, Q4 is held off (R13), so a floating CMD on an unpowered card does no harm. What remains is a documented deviation from Espressif's SPI-mode guidance, with a small risk if future firmware releases GPIO19 while the card is powered.
verdicts.fix: Rev A: no change is needed. Keep the slab_periph_on() order (MOSI driven before Q4 turns on). Optionally enable the GPIO19 internal pull-up when the SD bus is torn down. Rev B, or now if a 0402 fits in the R21-R24 row at about (-17.5,-31.3): add a 10k from SD_MOSI to 3V3_PERIPH.

verdicts.reasoning: Checked in netlist.xml: J2 pins 9 (IOVCC), 10 and 11 (VCC) are on /3V3_PERIPH, which comes from U4 RT9080-33GJ5 through Q4 AO3401A (source on /3V3, drain on 3V3_PERIPH). The DLC-T2.7DDS#1 spec v1.0 p.6 gives VCC 2.4 / 2.75 / 3.3 V (min/typ/max) and IOVCC 1.65 / 1.8 / 3.3 V. On p.5 the absolute maximum is 4.6 V for both, and the pin table labels them 'IOVCC1.8V' and 'VCC2.8V'. The RT9080 datasheet (C841192.txt, electrical characteristics) gives DC output accuracy of ±2% at 1 mA and 25 °C. So 3V3 can reach 3.366 V, and Q4 drops only a few mV at screen current (about 15 mA). That puts VCC and IOVCC up to about 66 mV over the 3.3 V operating maximum and 1.2 V under the absolute maximum. Logic levels are fine: the ESP32 drives from the same 3V3 rail, so VIH (0.7*IOVCC to IOVCC) is met. The reviewer's facts and severity hold.
verdicts.fix: None for rev A. If the screen misbehaves, measure 3V3_PERIPH at C19/C20. A later revision could use a 3.0 V or 3.1 V rail for the screen if a separate rail is ever added.

verdicts.reasoning: Checked items. DLC spec p.5: one LEDK pin (1) and two LEDA pins (14, 15). p.6: IF 200 mA total for 10 parallel LEDs, VF 2.7 to 3.3 V. In netlist.xml, /LCD_LEDK connects only J2 pin 1 and Q5 drain, and /LCD_LEDA connects J2 pins 14 and 15 and R17 (10R, 1206) from VSYS. With VSYS about 4.7 V on USB (README note 3), I = (4.7 - VF)/10 = 140 to 200 mA, all through contact 1. Each LEDA contact carries half of that. The firmware cap exists: slab_backlight.h defines SLAB_BL_USB_MAX_PERMILLE 800, and slab-player/main/player_power.c applies the duty. At 80 percent duty the RMS current is at most about 179 mA, with 200 mA peaks. Not settled: the FH35C per-contact current rating. The LCSC drawing (C2889267.pdf, EDC3-338903-01, pp.1-5) does not state it, and both hirose.com and Digi-Key returned 403. The pinout is fixed by the panel vendor, so no PCB change could split LEDK anyway.
verdicts.fix: Keep the firmware USB duty cap. To settle the question, read the rated current in the Hirose FH35C series catalog. If it is 0.2 A or more, this is a pure note. If it is lower, also cap the battery-side duty or raise R17 in a later revision. No PCB change for rev A.

verdicts.reasoning: Checked in reference/DLC-T2.7DDS1-mechanical-400dpi.png (tail detail, cropped at full resolution): FPC width 4.80 ±0.1, P0.3*15-0.3 = 4.20 ±0.1, contact width 0.20 ±0.03, thickness 0.20 ±0.03 (side view), stiffener zone 1.50/2.20/2.50 ±0.2. The Hirose FH35C drawing EDC3-338903-01 p.2 gives 'Recommended FPC' F ±0.05 and t 0.2 ±0.03. The p.4 table for FH35C-15S gives A 6.1, B 3.6, C 4.2, D (4.83, a reference dimension for the housing opening), E 5.53 and F 4.8. So the panel's nominal width matches F, but its ±0.1 tolerance is twice Hirose's ±0.05. A 4.90 mm tail exceeds the 4.83 opening, which is only a reference value, so the actual binding is unconfirmed. Pitch (0.3) and thickness match. The p.5 cautions (insert horizontally, do not twist, do not force) are confirmed. The J2 part (FH35C-15S-0.3SHW(50)) matches the 15-pin tail.
verdicts.fix: No design change. At assembly, insert the tail flat with the actuator open. If a tail binds, check its width with calipers and trim the edge slightly outside the outer contacts rather than forcing it.

areas.title: ESP32 module integration

findings.title: Antenna open end has ground copper 0.9 mm away on all four layers; the vendor clearance is not met
findings.refs: harmony-mark8-slab.kicad_pcb zone ANTENNA_KEEPOUT (KiCad x 122.8-128.2, y 91.8-107.9 = device x 21.8-27.2, y -37.9 to -21.8); design.py ANTENNA_KEEPOUT, U1_ORIGIN (16.2,-29.3) rot 90; README 'Antenna'; SPEC.md line 181
findings.evidence: U1 sits in the middle of the right edge (module y -35.9 to -22.7). The board goes on for about 12 mm past each end of the antenna. Datasheet Fig. 11 (top view) shows the two antenna legs (feed and short) on the pin-1 side, with the open end of the meander on the other side. On the board, pad 1 is at device (20.2,-35.2), so the feed is at the -y end and the open end is at y -22.7. I sampled the filled zones on F.Cu, In1.Cu, In2.Cu and B.Cu at x 22.2 to 26.5: there is solid GND on every layer from y -21.8 up to the top edge at y -10, only 0.9 mm past the open end. Parts near the open end: SW3 pad 1 at (20.2,-21.78), 1.85 mm away; R31/R32 pads at (23.9-24.9,-20.5), 2.2 mm away; SW1 side switch with a metal frame at (25.48,-15.6), about 5 mm away. The board also has FR4 under the antenna; it is copper-free there but not cut out. The keep-out margins (2 mm below, 0.9 mm above) look like a reading of the 'Max 2' and 'Max 1' marks in HDG Fig. 25 without its 'Min 15' clearance on the open-end side.
findings.requirement: ESP32 Hardware Design Guidelines (docs.espressif.com, esp32, sect. 1.4.8, Fig. 23-25): put the antenna's feed point at a board corner, with the antenna outside the board or the board cut away on both sides of and below the antenna. Fig. 25 clearance: at least 15 mm beyond the antenna's open end and at most 2 mm on the feed side. A module in the middle of an edge (position 2) is 'not recommended'. The guide also asks for at least 15 mm clearance inside the housing. SPEC.md line 181: 'No copper on any layer under the antenna or within the vendor keep-out.' Module datasheet v1.8 sect. 11.2 points to that HDG section.
findings.consequence: Ground close to the open (high-field) end of an inverted-F antenna detunes it downward and lowers its efficiency. Expect less Bluetooth range and margin, which can mean A2DP dropouts with the player in a pocket and the body between it and the headphones. No bodge wire or firmware change can fix this after fabrication. The size of the loss is not measured; the board may still work at short range.
findings.fix: Before ordering, at least: extend the all-layer keep-out on the open-end side (x 21.8 to 27.2) as far toward y -10 as the side button allows (at least to about y -17), and move R31/R32 out of that column. Better: move U1 so the feed end is at a board corner and the open end points off the board (HDG Fig. 24 positions 1 and 5 for a feed-on-the-left module), or cut the board away beside the open end. Either way, run an A2DP range test through a body on the first boards and record the result.

findings.title: GPIO13's internal pull-down after reset turns Q4 on: 3V3_PERIPH is not held off during boot
findings.refs: U1 pin 20 (GPIO13/MTCK) net PERIPH_EN_N; R14 10k (PERIPH_EN_N to PERIPH_GATE); R13 100k (3V3 to PERIPH_GATE); C18 100 nF; Q4 AO3401A; README Power ('R13 holds it off at reset'); firmware slab_board.c slab_board_init
findings.evidence: ESP32 Series Datasheet v5.3, Appendix IO_MUX, chip pin 20 MTCK: 'At Reset oe=0, ie=0' but 'After Reset oe=0, ie=1, wpd'. Module datasheet Table 15 gives RPD = 45 k. After reset is released, the gate therefore sits at 3.3 x (10k+45k)/(100k+10k+45k) = 1.17 V, so VGS = -2.13 V. The AO3401A datasheet gives VGS(th) -0.5 to -1.3 V and RDS(on) under 85 mOhm at -2.5 V, so Q4 conducts. It stays on until slab_board_init() drives GPIO13 high. That is after the ROM, the bootloader, the PSRAM memtest (CONFIG_SPIRAM_MEMTEST=y) and app start, typically a few hundred ms. Q4 also stays on for the whole time the chip waits in UART download mode, and for good on the 'Not a slab board' path, which leaves the outputs alone.
findings.requirement: README Power: 'GPIO13 low turns it on; R13 holds it off at reset'. SPEC 5.3/line 162 power-sequencing intent: the firmware controls when the screen and card get power.
findings.consequence: The screen and the card get power at every boot and in download mode while their lines float or sit at reset pulls (for example GPIO14 and GPIO5 weak pull-ups). Nothing is damaged, and the C18 ramp limits inrush to about 30 mA, so this is not a failure. But the documented 'off at reset' does not hold, and power-cycling the card or screen from firmware cannot rely on a known-off state before init. Deep-sleep current is not affected, because the firmware holds GPIO13 high with rtc_gpio_hold_en.
findings.fix: Option A, values: R13 4.7k, R14 1k, C18 1 uF (all JLC basic parts already in design.py). Off with the 45k pull-down: VG = 3.3 x 46/50.7 = 2.99 V, VGS -0.31 V. On with GPIO13 low: VGS about -2.7 V. Ramp tau about 0.8 ms. Option B: accept it and correct the README, and optionally drive GPIO13 high in a bootloader hook so the window is shorter.

findings.title: Card SPI runs through the GPIO matrix: 20 MHz is at the read-timing limit, and the Kconfig allows 26.7 MHz
findings.refs: U1 pins 29 (GPIO5 SD_SCK), 33 (GPIO19 SD_MOSI), 35 (GPIO21 SD_MISO), 15 (GPIO25 SD_CS); README block diagram 'ESP32 VSPI (5/19/21/25...)'; firmware components/slab_board/Kconfig SLAB_SD_SPI_KHZ range 400-26666, SLAB_LCD_SPI_HZ range to 80000000; bench_storage.c SPI3_HOST
findings.evidence: The VSPI IO_MUX pins are CLK 18, D 23, Q 19, CS0 5 (module datasheet sect. 5.2.2 and Table 3). Here GPIO5 is clock, GPIO19 is MOSI (its IO_MUX role is MISO) and GPIO21 is MISO (its IO_MUX role is HD), so the whole card bus goes through the GPIO matrix. ESP-IDF 5.3 (soc/esp32/soc.h) sets GPIO_MATRIX_DELAY_NS = 25, and spi_hal_get_freq_limit() gives 80 MHz/(floor((1+input_delay+25)x0.08)+1). That is 26.7 MHz for a card with zero output delay and 20 MHz for a card with the SD default-speed tODLY of 14 ns. sdspi_host.c does not set input_delay_ns, so the driver never warns. The screen bus is also on the matrix (GPIO27 and GPIO26 are not HSPI IO_MUX pins); 40 MHz write-only is at the documented matrix ceiling, but the Kconfig range allows up to 80 MHz.
findings.requirement: ESP-IDF spi_master.h (spi_bus_add_device notes): typical maximum 26 MHz on GPIO-matrix pins for an ideal slave; slave output delay lowers it further. SD Physical Layer spec, default-speed tODLY up to 14 ns (from memory; the spec is not in reference/).
findings.consequence: At 20 MHz a slow card can sample MISO late and give read CRC errors. At the 26.7 MHz Kconfig option, read errors are likely with some cards. The README diagram suggests IO_MUX VSPI pins, which can mislead later tuning.
findings.fix: Firmware: cap SLAB_SD_SPI_KHZ at 20000, and drop to 16000 if bring-up shows CRC errors. Set the Kconfig maximum for SLAB_LCD_SPI_HZ to 40000000. README: say that both buses use the GPIO matrix. A later revision can use 18/23/19/5 for IO_MUX VSPI.

findings.title: VBUS_SENSE puts 3.0 V on GPIO36, above the ADC's linear range
findings.refs: R29 100k (VBUS to VBUS_SENSE), R30 150k 0603 (VBUS_SENSE to GND), U1 pin 4 GPIO36 ADC1_CH0; firmware slab_analog.c ADC_ATTEN_DB_12, slab_analog_math.c slab_vsys_estimate_mv
findings.evidence: 5.0 V x 150/250 = 3.00 V at the pin, and 3.15 V at 5.25 V. The firmware reads it with 12 dB attenuation and line-fitting calibration, then uses vbus_mv - D1 drop to estimate VSYS for backlight compensation.
findings.requirement: ESP32 Series Datasheet v5.3, ADC characteristics: 'Atten = 3, effective measurement range of 150 ~ 2450 mV'. The note above that table says accuracy is worse when the result is above 3000 (about 2450 mV). There is no damage risk: the pin stays below VDD+0.3.
findings.consequence: VBUS reads are compressed or clipped near the top of the scale, so the VSYS estimate on USB is wrong by some tens to hundreds of mV. USB-present detection still works.
findings.fix: Change R30 to 75k 0603 (C23242, already in the BOM for R10). That gives 2.14 V at 5.0 V and 2.25 V at 5.25 V. Set SLAB_VBUS_DIVIDER_X1000 to 2333. Or keep the parts and use the reading only as a present/absent flag.

findings.title: U1 centre pad has 100 percent paste on all nine 1.45 mm pads; the datasheet warns that too much paste lifts the module
findings.refs: lib/Harmony8.pretty/ESP32-PICO-MINI-02.kicad_mod pad 49 (nine 1.45x1.45 rects, layers F.Cu F.Paste F.Mask, no paste margin); jlcpcb/gerbers F_Paste; jlcpcb/ORDER.md via-in-pad note
findings.evidence: Every pad-49 rectangle has a full paste aperture (about 18.9 mm2 in total) and no solder_paste_margin. ORDER.md accepts the nine open 0.3 mm vias in pad 49 because 'solder can wick into them'. With the JLC via covering now set to 'Plugged' rather than open or tented, that wicking may not happen. I could not confirm how JLC treats a plugged via inside an exposed pad.
findings.requirement: ESP32-PICO-MINI-02 datasheet v1.8 sect. 9: soldering the EPAD is optional. 'Too much soldering paste may increase the gap between the module and the baseboard. As a result, the adhesion between other pins and the baseboard may be poor.'
findings.consequence: The module may sit high on the centre pads, leaving opens or weak joints on the 0.4 mm perimeter pins. These cannot be inspected under a module, and a 53-pin module is hard to rework by hand.
findings.fix: Set a negative paste margin on pad 49, for example -0.2 mm (about 52 percent of the area), or paste only some of the nine pads. Then regenerate F_Paste. In the JLC DFM result, check how the pad-49 vias will be processed.

findings.title: LCD_TE on GPIO39 gets 80 ns low glitches whenever ADC1 is powered
findings.refs: U1 pin 7 GPIO39 LCD_TE; firmware slab_pins.h SLAB_PIN_LCD_TE; slab_analog.c ADC_UNIT_1
findings.evidence: The firmware reads VBAT and VBUS on ADC1. TE is currently unused (touch rule 2).
findings.requirement: ESP32 errata [GPIO-3.11]: powering SAR ADC1, SAR ADC2 or AMP pulls the inputs of GPIO36 and GPIO39 low for about 80 ns, on all revisions including v3.1. Workaround: ignore those inputs at that time.
findings.consequence: If TE is later enabled as an edge interrupt, every ADC conversion can produce a false TE edge. Ext0 and ext1 wake are on GPIO38 and GPIO34, which are not affected.
findings.fix: No action for rev A. If TE is ever used, mask its interrupt around ADC reads, or move TE in a later revision.

findings.title: Auto-reset on battery relies on CH9102F DTR/RTS staying high or high-impedance while VDD5 = 0
findings.refs: Q1 UMH3N (pin2 B1=DTR, pin1 E1=RTS, pin6 C1=ESP_EN; pin5 B2=RTS, pin4 E2=DTR, pin3 C2=BOOT); U2 pins 19 RTS, 23 DTR, 5 VIO=3V3
findings.evidence: On battery, U2 has VIO = 3V3 and V3 = VDD5 = 0, so its internal low-voltage reset holds it in reset. CH9102 datasheet sect. 5.2 says VIO draws about 2 uA and does not back-feed, and Table 6.2 lists 15-90 uA pull-ups on the serial pins. It does not state the DTR/RTS output levels while V3 = 0. If DTR sat high and RTS low, Tr1 would hold EN low and the board would not boot on battery.
findings.requirement: Module datasheet Table 3: do not leave EN floating; EN must be above VIH_nRST (0.75 x VDD) to run.
findings.consequence: Probably fine: symmetric pull-ups keep Vbe = 0, and Adafruit's Feather ESP32 V2 uses the same arrangement. But the datasheet does not confirm it.
findings.fix: On the first board, measure EN (at least 2.5 V) and IO0 (high) on battery with USB unplugged, as part of bring-up.

checked: Footprint ESP32-PICO-MINI-02 against datasheet v1.8 Fig. 3, 11 and 14, every pad: pins 1-11 on the left column at x -5.9, 0.8 pitch, pin 1 nearest the antenna; 12-24 bottom row left to right; 25-35 right column bottom to top; 36-48 top row right to left; 49 = 3x3 of 1.45 mm pads at 1.98 pitch (5.41 overall vs 5.4); 50-53 are 0.7 mm corner pads. Overall dimensions 12.6, 11.0, 10.6, 10.0, 9.2, 9.0, 8.4 and 11.2 match Fig. 14. Body 13.2 x 16.6 with a 5.4 mm antenna region at the footprint's -y end.

Placement transform: KiCad rot 90 puts the antenna tip at device x = 16.2+11 = 27.2 (flush with the right edge) and the module at x 10.6 to 27.2, y -35.9 to -22.7, as in the README and mechanical-interface.json. CPL U1 at (133.8,-99.3) rot 90 matches the pad-field origin.

netlist.xml U1 pin-to-net for all 53 pins matches datasheet Table 3, design.py, the README pin map and firmware slab_pins.h: GND on 1, 2, 11, 14 and 36-53; 3V3 on 3; NC pins 25 and 32, I37 (5) and IO12 (19) unconnected. PCB pad nets for U1 agree.

N8R2 internal pins: datasheet Fig. 8 shows flash on CLK/IO6, CMD/IO11, IO16, IO17, IO18, IO23 and PSRAM on SD2/IO9 and SD3/IO10, none pinned out or used. IO7 and IO8 (pins 27, 28) are pinned out, free, and go only to TP7/TP8.
GPIO20 (pin 26) exists on ESP32-PICO-V3-02; ESP-IDF 5.3 SOC_GPIO_VALID_GPIO_MASK includes it and gpio_periph.c notes it is PICO-V3 only. Using it for I2C SCL through the GPIO matrix is fine.
Strap GPIO0: R6 10k to 3V3, SW2 to GND, Q1 Tr2 collector. Reads 1 for SPI boot, 0 for download via SW2 or auto-reset.
Strap GPIO2: R19 100R plus R20 100k to GND (100.1k) plus internal wpd, so it reads 0. Download mode (GPIO0 = 0, GPIO2 = 0) works, and Q6 stays off at boot.
Strap GPIO12/MTDI: unconnected, internal wpd at and after reset (IO_MUX table), so it reads 0 and VDD_SDIO is 3.3 V, correct for the 3.3 V flash.

Strap GPIO15/MTDO: R25 100k pull-up, card-detect switch to GND (DM3AT detect switch is normally open). It reads 1 with no card and 0 with a card, which only disables the ROM UART log (datasheet Table 7); download still works.
Strap GPIO5: SD_SCK only, no external pull, internal wpu, so it reads the default 1 (SDIO slave timing, unused).

EN: R5 10k / C4 1 uF gives a 10 ms RC, matching the datasheet sect. 9 recommendation (R = 10k, C = 1 uF). tSTBL 50 us is met. SW3 shorts EN to GND. IO0 stays low through esptool's 50 ms after EN release, more than about 12 ms to VIH_nRST plus 1 ms tH.

Q1 UMH3N pinout against the CJ datasheet diagram (E1=1, B1=2, C1=6; E2=4, B2=5, C2=3; two DTC143T, R1 4.7k). Wired as the standard DTR/RTS circuit: DTR=1, RTS=0 pulls EN low; DTR=0, RTS=1 pulls IO0 low. EN low level is about VCE(sat) 0.1 V, below VIL_nRST 0.6 V. Base drive of about 0.55 mA discharges C4 in well under 1 ms.

UART0: GPIO1/TXD0 (pin 31) to R3 1k to CH9102F pin 20 RXD (input with pull-up); CH9102F pin 21 TXD to R4 1k to GPIO3/RXD0 (pin 30). CH9102F QFN24 pin numbers checked against the WCH datasheet pin table. VIO on 3V3, so the UART levels are 3.3 V. Test pads TP5 and TP6 are present.

Input-only pins: 34 TOUCH_IRQ (MPR121 open drain, R11 10k to 3V3), 35 VBAT_SENSE (analog), 36 VBUS_SENSE (analog), 38 SIDE_BTN (R26 100k to 3V3, C23 100 nF, 10 ms), 39 LCD_TE (push-pull from the screen), 37 unused. None is driven as an output by the board or the firmware. The pins needing pull-ups have external ones, since 34-39 have no internal pulls.

ADC: VBAT_SENSE on GPIO35 = ADC1_CH7 and VBUS_SENSE on GPIO36 = ADC1_CH0, both on ADC1 (no Bluetooth or Wi-Fi conflict). slab_analog.c uses ADC_UNIT_1, CH7 and CH0. VBAT 1M/1M gives 2.1 V at 4.2 V, inside the 150-2450 mV range at 12 dB. SD_CS on GPIO25 (ADC2_CH8) is used only as a digital pin.

Deep-sleep wake: GPIO38 = RTC_GPIO2 (ext0, level 0) and GPIO34 = RTC_GPIO4 (ext1 ALL_LOW, single pin). Both are RTC GPIOs with external pull-ups to 3V3, which stays on in sleep (player_power.c and bringup.c).

Sleep hold: slab_board_prepare_deep_sleep holds PERIPH_EN_N (GPIO13 = RTC_GPIO14) high, and LCD_BL (GPIO4) and BUZZER (GPIO2) low, with rtc_gpio_hold_en. It isolates the RTC screen and card pins and holds the non-RTC card pins 5, 19 and 21 low with gpio_hold_en plus gpio_deep_sleep_hold_en. R13 is a failsafe pull-up if the hold is lost. On wake, release_holds and then idf_output(13,1) re-drive it within microseconds, and the C18 RC keeps Q4 off during that gap.

SPI pin routing: screen SCK GPIO14 is HSPICLK (IO_MUX), but MOSI 27 and CS 26 are not HSPI IO_MUX pins, so SPI2 runs through the GPIO matrix. 40 MHz half-duplex write-only (SPI_DEVICE_HALFDUPLEX, spics_io_num -1) is at the GPIO-matrix ceiling, and no MISO timing applies. The card bus is all GPIO matrix (see finding ESP32-3).

Power and decoupling: 3V3 reaches module pin 3 with C5 22 uF (pad 1.8 mm from pin 3) and C6 100 nF, matching datasheet Fig. 10 (C1 22 uF, C2 0.1 uF). Supply range 3.0-3.6 V. The RT9080 600 mA rating is at least the 0.5 A IVDD in datasheet Table 14. Every GND pad (1, 2, 11, 14, 36-53) is on net GND, and DRC reports 0 unconnected.

Antenna keep-out in the PCB file: the rule area ANTENNA_KEEPOUT covers F.Cu, In1.Cu, In2.Cu and B.Cu and forbids tracks, vias, pads and pour. I parsed every filled polygon, segment, via and pad: none lies inside it (the pours stop exactly on its boundary). The nearest via is 1.23 mm from the antenna region. The wheel electrodes are at least 5.2 mm away and the L2 hatch at least 4.2 mm away. The enclosure README keeps screws, inserts and bosses out of the keep-out (nearest insert about 8 mm below it), and the battery sits under the screen, more than 18 mm away.
Firmware config consistent with the module: ESP32-PICO-V3-02 package check through efuse, 8 MB flash DIO, 2 MB PSRAM (CONFIG_SPIRAM), CONFIG_ESP32_REV_MIN_3, Bluetooth Classic A2DP only.
not_checked: Real antenna performance (return loss, detuning, range). It needs a VNA or a range test on built boards; the severity of ESP32-1 is a judgment from the Espressif guideline, not a measurement.
CH9102F DTR/RTS output levels while V3 and VDD5 are at 0 V with VIO powered. The WCH datasheet does not state them (finding ESP32-7).
The SD card output delay tODLY (14 ns default speed). It is quoted from memory of the SD Physical Layer spec, which is not in reference/.

The ESP-IDF documentation sentence that the GPIO matrix limits SPI clocks to 40 MHz. The local ESP-IDF 5.3 package has no docs and the driver does not enforce it. I relied on the spi_master.h comment (26 MHz for reads through the matrix) and on memory for the 40 MHz output figure.
The ST7365P maximum SPI write clock. It belongs to the screen reviewer; Kconfig notes a 66 ns minimum write cycle (15 MHz) against 40 MHz in use.
How JLC processes 'Plugged' vias that sit inside exposed SMD pads (U1 pad 49), and JLC's library origin and rotation for C2980306. Both need the JLC DFM result and placement preview.
I did not run kicad-cli DRC or ERC myself. I relied on drc.json and erc.json plus my own parse of the board file under review-work/esp32/.
Ground-via density along the antenna feed side, and the 3V3 track IR drop from U4 to U1 pin 3. I only checked these against README/verify.py summaries (3V3 at 0.4 mm except neck-downs).

verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced from primary sources. (1) Feed side: module datasheet v1.8 Fig. 11 top view shows the two antenna legs (feed and short) on the left, the open end of the meander on the right ending short of the body. Fig. 3 and Fig. 14 put pin 1 at the top left, next to the antenna. In harmony-mark8-slab.kicad_pcb (top side, not flipped) U1 pad 1 is at device (20.2,-35.2), pads 1-11 run along y -35.2 and pads 36-48 along x 21.1. So the feed is at the -Y end (y -35.9) and the open end is at y -22.7. The device transform (x,y) to (150-x, 70-y) is a 180 degree rotation and does not mirror. (2) Copper: zone ANTENNA_KEEPOUT is KiCad x 122.8-128.2, y 91.8-107.9, which is device x 21.8-27.2, y -37.9 to -21.8. I point-sampled the filled polygons (scripts/zones.py in my scratch folder). L1_GND, L2_GND_SOLID, L3_GND and L4_GND are all solid at x 22.2-26.5 from y -21.6 to -11, so there is ground on all four layers 0.9 mm beyond the open end. The column has small gaps only for R31/R32 (pads (23.89/24.91,-19.3) and (-20.5)) and one L3 track at x 22.2. The board continues to y -10.0, 12.7 mm past the open end. FR4 sits under the whole antenna because the module is flush with the edge (module x 10.6-27.2, board edge 27.2), not overhanging. (3) Requirement: HDG 1.4.8 (hdg.pdf p.27-29) says to put the antenna outside the board with the feed near the edge. Otherwise, cut the board away on both sides of and below the antenna. Fig. 25 shows a clearance area of at least 15 mm beyond the open end, with the board notched there. A clearance of at least 15 mm inside the housing is also recommended. This layout is worse than Fig. 23/24 position 2 (mid-edge, 'not recommended') because the antenna does not overhang either. SPEC.md line 181 says no copper 'within the vendor keep-out', and that is not met if the vendor keep-out is read as Fig. 25. README 'Antenna' does not list this as an accepted exception. One correction to the reviewer: in HDG Fig. 24, positions 1 and 5 put the feed at the corner with the antenna outside the board outline; the open end runs along the edge, not 'off the board'. Severity: no bodge or firmware change can fix it after fabrication. The loss has not been measured, and the radio is likely to work at short range, so major (not blocker) is right, with medium confidence on the size of the loss. Checked and correct: the antenna strip itself (x 21.8-27.2, y -35.9 to -22.7) has no copper on any layer, and the keep-out stays outside the wheel hatch.
verdicts.fix: Before ordering, at least: extend ANTENNA_KEEPOUT on the open-end side from y -21.8 to about y -18.2, the edge of SW1's GND guide pad at y -17.72. Move R31/R32 (I2C pull-ups, free to sit anywhere on the bus) out of x 21.8-27.2, reroute the L3 track at x ~22.2, then refill and rerun DRC. The open-end clearance goes from 0.9 mm to about 4.5 mm on every layer. The full HDG fix is a re-layout: the feed end at the bottom-right corner, with the board cut away beyond the open end, or the antenna overhanging the edge. That fights the ramp zone and the enclosure, so treat it as rev B unless range tests fail. On the first boards, run an A2DP range test through a body (player in a pocket) and record it. Keep metal (screws, inserts, the battery) away from the right wall near y -36 to -10.

verdicts.reasoning: ESP32 Series Datasheet v5.3, Appendix Table IO_MUX, pin 20 MTCK: 'At Reset oe=0, ie=0' and 'After Reset oe=0, ie=1, wpd' (esp32_datasheet_en.txt line ~4014). MTDI and GPIO2/4 also show wpd. Module datasheet v1.8 Table 15 gives RPD 45 kOhm (typical only, no min or max). Netlist: U1 pin 20 IO13 is on /PERIPH_EN_N with R14 10k to /PERIPH_GATE; R13 100k from /3V3 to /PERIPH_GATE; C18 100 nF from gate to 3V3; Q4 AO3401A has S on 3V3, D on 3V3_PERIPH, G on PERIPH_GATE. After reset, VG = 3.3 x 55/155 = 1.17 V, so VGS = -2.13 V. AO3401A (C15127): VGS(th) -0.5/-0.9/-1.3 V; RDS(on) 60/85 mOhm at -2.5 V. Q4 is solidly on. Firmware slab_board.c: slab_board_init() sets GPIO13 high only after the identity check. The 'Not a slab board' branch returns early with 'outputs left alone', so Q4 stays on there. That includes a first board whose CONFIG_SLAB_EXPECTED_MAC does not match. slab-player and slab-bringup set CONFIG_SPIRAM_MEMTEST=y, which lengthens the window. UART download mode also leaves Q4 on. During reset itself (EN low, ie=0, no pull), R13 does hold Q4 off, so the README sentence is true only for the reset pulse, not for boot. Nothing is damaged: the ESP32 lines are not driven, so there is no back-power path, and the C18 ramp limits inrush. Deep sleep is not affected because rtc_gpio_hold_en holds GPIO13 high.
verdicts.fix: Option A (parts already on the BOM): R13 4.7k (C25900), R14 1k (C11702), C18 1 uF 0402 (C52923). With the 45k pull-down: VG = 3.3 x 46/50.7 = 2.99 V, VGS -0.31 V, which is off (below the -0.5 V minimum threshold). With GPIO13 driven low: VGS about -2.7 V. The ramp tau is about 0.8 ms. Cost: about 0.58 mA from 3V3 only while 3V3_PERIPH is on. RPD has no minimum in the datasheet; with a 20k pull-down VGS would be -0.6 V, so measure gate voltage on the first board, or use R13 3.3k for more margin. Option B: keep the parts, correct the README ('Q4 is on from reset release until firmware init'), and optionally drive GPIO13 high in a bootloader_before_init hook. Download mode is still not covered.

verdicts.reasoning: The facts are right, but nothing here needs fixing. Netlist: SD_SCK U1 pin 29 IO5, SD_MOSI pin 33 IO19, SD_MISO pin 35 IO21, SD_CS pin 15 IO25. None of these is in its VSPI IO_MUX role, so the bus uses the GPIO matrix. In the ESP-IDF in use (tangara-fw/lib/esp-idf v5.5), hal/esp32/include/hal/gpio_ll.h sets GPIO_LL_MATRIX_DELAY_NS 25. spi_hal_get_freq_limit gives 80/(floor((1+d+25)x0.08)+1): 26.67 MHz for d=0 and 20 MHz for d=14 ns. sdspi_host.c configure_spi_dev does not set input_delay_ns. However: (a) 20 MHz is exactly the IDF default for SDSPI (SDMMC_FREQ_DEFAULT 20000 in sd_protocol_types.h), and IDF says 'SPI master working at this limit is OK'. (b) components/slab_board/Kconfig SLAB_SD_SPI_KHZ defaults to 20000, and its help already says the card pins use the GPIO matrix, that IDF allows full duplex up to about 26.7 MHz, and to raise the clock only after clean reads. README Power note 5 says the same. (c) The screen bus is half-duplex and write-only (st7365p.c sets SPI_DEVICE_HALFDUPLEX, miso -1, default 40 MHz). IDF spi_master.rst says write-only output 'can be 80 MHz, even if the GPIO matrix is used', so the 80 MHz Kconfig upper bound is not wrong in itself. (d) README's 'ESP32 VSPI (5/19/21/25...)' names the host (SPI3), not IO_MUX pins. The suggested later fix is wrong for this module: datasheet Fig. 3 / Table 3 show that GPIO18 (VSPICLK) and GPIO23 (VSPID) are not brought out on ESP32-PICO-MINI-02, so an IO_MUX VSPI bus cannot be built. The HSPI IO_MUX pins 12/13/14/15 are exposed, but GPIO12 is the MTDI strap: a card DAT0 pull-up on it would select 1.8 V VDD_SDIO when 3V3_PERIPH is up at boot, which ESP32-2 shows it is.
verdicts.fix: No hardware change. Optional: add one README line that both SPI buses use the GPIO matrix (with no IO_MUX option on this module, because GPIO18/23 are not brought out). Leave the Kconfig as is, or lower its maximum to 20000 if you want to rule out the 26.7 MHz setting.

verdicts.reasoning: Netlist: R29 100k from /VBUS to /VBUS_SENSE, R30 150k from /VBUS_SENSE to GND, U1 pin 4 I36. 5.00 V x 150/250 = 3.00 V; 5.25 V gives 3.15 V. ESP32 Series Datasheet v5.3 Table 4-4: 'Atten = 3, effective measurement range of 150 ~ 2450 mV'. The note above it says accuracy is worse when the result is above 3000 (about 2450 mV). Firmware slab_analog.c reads ADC_CHANNEL_0 at ADC_ATTEN_DB_12 with line-fitting calibration. slab_pins.h SLAB_VBUS_DIVIDER_X1000 1667, and slab_vsys_estimate_mv uses vbus_mv - 350. The VBUS-present threshold (4300 mV, 2.58 V at the pin) still works, but the absolute VBUS and the VSYS estimate on USB come from an out-of-range, compressed reading. 3.15 V is under VDD+0.3, so there is no damage risk.
verdicts.fix: Change R30 to 75k 0603 (C23242, already on the BOM for R10). That gives 2.14 V at 5.0 V and 2.25 V at 5.25 V. Set SLAB_VBUS_DIVIDER_X1000 to 2333. SLAB_VBUS_PRESENT_MV 4300 then sits at 1.84 V at the pin and needs no change. Or keep the parts and use VBUS_SENSE only as a present flag.

verdicts.reasoning: The facts check out: lib/Harmony8.pretty/ESP32-PICO-MINI-02.kicad_mod pad 49 is nine 1.45x1.45 rects on F.Cu/F.Paste/F.Mask with no paste margin. The board has no global paste margin. The F_Paste gerber has nine 1.45x1.45 apertures at U1 (KiCad 131.82-135.78, 97.32-101.28), 18.9 mm2 in total. There is one 0.5/0.3 via in the centre of each sub-pad. But this is Espressif's own recommended land pattern (datasheet Fig. 14), and it already splits the paste into window panes: 18.9 mm2 is 65 percent of the 5.4 x 5.4 mm (29.2 mm2) exposed-pad area. That is in the 50-80 percent range commonly used for thermal pads (IPC-7525 practice, from memory, not in reference/). The module's own bottom pads (Fig. 11 bottom view) are the same nine 1.45 mm squares, so the paste is 1:1 with the matching pads, exactly like the signal pins. Paste height per wetted area is the same at the centre and at the perimeter, so there is no inherent lift. Datasheet section 9 asks for 'the correct amount' but gives no number, so there is no requirement to break. Open vias would wick solder away (less standoff, not more). One real open question belongs to the fab review: what JLC's forced 'Plugged' via covering does to vias inside an exposed SMD pad (ink in the pad, possible bump or outgassing). ORDER.md still says 'Tented' and 'open', so it is out of date.
verdicts.fix: No footprint change needed. Optional and harmless: a -0.05 to -0.1 mm paste margin on pad 49 (about 58 or 48 percent coverage). Settle the via-in-pad handling under 'Plugged' in JLC's DFM result, update ORDER.md to match the form, and check X-ray or a side view of U1 on the first boards if JLC offers it.

verdicts.reasoning: ESP32 Series SoC Errata v3.1, item 3.12 [GPIO-3.11] (errata.txt line ~842): powering SAR ADC1, SAR ADC2 or AMP pulls the inputs of GPIO36 and GPIO39 low for about 80 ns, on revisions v0.0 to v3.1, with no fix scheduled. Workaround: ignore those inputs at that time. Netlist: /LCD_TE is J2 pin 3 FMARK and U1 pin 7 I39. Firmware slab_analog.c uses ADC_UNIT_1 (GPIO35, GPIO36), and slab_pins.h marks GPIO39 'left unused (touch rule 2)'. GPIO36 is VBUS_SENSE, an analog input, so it is not affected in a way that matters. Wake inputs SIDE_BTN (GPIO38) and TOUCH_IRQ (GPIO34) are not affected. No current impact.
verdicts.fix: No action for rev A. If TE is ever used as an edge interrupt, mask or debounce it around ADC conversions, or move TE off GPIO36/39 in a later revision.

verdicts.reasoning: Netlist: Q1 UMH3N, pin2 B1=/DTR, pin1 E1=/RTS, pin6 C1=/ESP_EN, pin5 B2=/RTS, pin4 E2=/DTR, pin3 C2=/BOOT. U2 pin 23 DTR, pin 19 RTS, pin 5 VIO on /3V3, VDD5 and VBUS on /VBUS. R5 10k and C4 1 uF are on EN; R6 10k is on BOOT. EN or IO0 is pulled low only if one of DTR/RTS is high while the other is actively driven low. CH9102 datasheet V1.4 section 5.2 says that with V3 and VDD5 at 0 V, VIO current behaves the same as in suspend: no current when outputs are unloaded and inputs are floating (internal pull-up) or high, and VIO does not back-feed. Section 5.4: an internal low-voltage reset watches V3 (VRV3 2.5-2.9 V, Table 6.2), so on battery the chip is held in reset. Table 6.2 gives VOH only for the 'non-reset state' (非复位态) and lists IPUP 15-90 uA at VIO 3.3 V for the 'serial and RST pins' (串口和RST引脚). That suggests DTR and RTS sit weakly pulled up to VIO in reset, which keeps both Vbe at 0. No line states the DTR/RTS level in reset directly, so this cannot be settled from the datasheet. Module datasheet Table 15: VIH_nRST is 0.75 x VDD, so about 2.48 V is needed on EN.
verdicts.fix: Bring-up step: on battery with USB unplugged, measure EN (expect about 3.3 V, at least 2.5 V), IO0 (high) and U2 pins 19 and 23 (expect about 3.3 V). If either pin is driven low, add a 10k pull-up from the low line to 3V3, or power U2 VIO from VBUS through the documented VBUS/PMOS scheme.

areas.title: Footprints, BOM and placement rotation

findings.title: USB-C J1 shell legs have no solder paste and no plan for soldering them
findings.refs: lib/Harmony8.pretty/USB-C_HRO_TYPE-C-31-M-12.kicad_mod pads 1-4 (thru_hole oval, layers *.Cu *.Mask only, no F.Paste); board J1 at KiCad (150.0, 115.47) rot 0; shell slots at Gerber (145.67/154.33, -113.76) and (145.67/154.33, -117.94); jlcpcb/gerbers/harmony-mark8-slab-F_Paste.gtp; jlcpcb/ORDER.md (Standard PCBA, top side, no hand-solder remark)
findings.evidence: I parsed the F_Paste Gerber. It has 341 flashes and none of them lands within 0.8 x 1.2 mm of any of the four shell-leg slots. The PTH drill file has the four G85 plated slots, so the legs go through the board but get no paste. The footprint is marked 'attr smd', so it goes out as an SMT part with no hand-soldering line. ORDER.md does not mention these legs in any remark to JLC.
findings.requirement: HRO TYPE-C-31-M-12 drawing (C165948.pdf): the four shell legs are the only mechanical retention. The recommended PCB layout has plated slots, and insertion and removal forces reach up to 2.0 kgf. The 16 SMD signal pads (0.3 x 1.3 mm) are not made to carry those forces.
findings.consequence: If JLC reflows the part from the paste layer only, the shell legs stay unsoldered. Then the 0.3 mm signal pads alone hold the receptacle against cable forces, and it can tear off the board after a few plug cycles (the A6/A7/B6/B7 pads lift first). Hand-soldering 4 joints on each board fixes it, but the owner wants no soldering. I could not confirm how JLC treats an SMD-classed part with THT legs, so confidence is medium.
findings.fix: Before paying, either (a) add a remark on the order: 'J1 (C165948): solder the 4 shell through-hole legs (pin-in-paste or hand solder)', or (b) add F.Paste to pads 1-4 for pin-in-paste. For (b), use a paste aperture larger than the slot and check JLC's DFM. Then confirm in the DFM or placement result that the legs are listed as soldered.

findings.title: J1 power pads are 0.7 mm wide, not HRO's 0.6 mm, which leaves a 0.10 mm GND-to-VBUS gap
findings.refs: USB-C_HRO_TYPE-C-31-M-12.kicad_mod custom pads A1B12 (-3.2,-2.47), A4B9 (-2.4,-2.47), B4A9 (2.4,-2.47), B1A12 (3.2,-2.47): each spans 0.70 x 1.40 mm (0.6 x 1.3 polygon plus 0.1 stroke). Nets: A1B12/B1A12 GND, A4B9/B4A9 VBUS. README 'Changes from spec' row 'Track and space 0.127 minimum'.
findings.evidence: I measured the primitives. A1B12 spans x -3.55 to -2.85 and A4B9 spans x -2.75 to -2.05, so the GND-VBUS gap is 0.10 mm (README reports 0.09). Mirrored on the B side.
findings.requirement: HRO TYPE-C-31-M-12 recommended PCB layout (C165948.pdf): A1/B12, A4/B9, B4/A9 and B1/A12 pads are 0.60 wide on 0.80 centres, which gives a 0.20 mm gap. The README says the 0.09 mm gap is 'the manufacturers' own land pattern (HRO)', but that is wrong. The 0.1 mm gap comes from EasyEDA's widened 0.7 mm pads.
findings.consequence: No solder-mask dam can survive between GND and VBUS at 0.1 mm, so a paste bridge there shorts USB VBUS to GND at the receptacle. The board then gets no USB power, and the host port's current limit trips. Rework can fix it, so this is not a blocker. This footprint is common at JLC and usually solders fine.
findings.fix: Narrow the four power-pad polygons to 0.6 mm (HRO), which gives a 0.2 mm gap. Re-run DRC, and drop the J1 0.09 mm rule from the .kicad_dru. Otherwise, keep the design and correct the README reasoning.

findings.title: J2 FH35C paste apertures are full pad size; Hirose specifies a reduced stencil
findings.refs: lib/Harmony8.pretty/FH35C-15S-0.3SHW.kicad_mod: odd pads 0.3 x 0.8, even pads 0.3 x 0.65, fittings 16/17 0.4 x 0.95, all with F.Paste at 1:1 (board pad_to_paste_clearance 0)
findings.evidence: The footprint copper matches Hirose: 0.3 wide, 0.6 pitch per row, rows 0.65 and 0.8 long, 2.15 between rows, 3.6 overall, B = 3.6 and C = 4.2 for 15 contacts, fitting 0.4 x 0.95 with 0.2 offset. But there is no paste reduction, so the stencil openings are 0.3 x 0.8 and 0.3 x 0.65. The fitting pad sits 0.46 mm from contact 1's centreline to its inner edge, against Hirose's 0.5 +-0.03.
findings.requirement: Hirose EDC3-338903-01 sheet 1 'Recommended stencil pattern' (C2889267.pdf p.1): openings 0.23 +-0.02 wide, 0.55 (contact-2 row) and 0.7 (contact-1 row) long, t = 0.1 mm. Fitting stencil 0.3 x 0.9.
findings.consequence: About 30 to 40 percent more paste than Hirose specifies on a 0.3 mm pitch staggered back-flip connector. This raises the risk of bridges and of solder wicking into the contact area, which stops the FPC from seating or contacting. A wick or bridge on a 0.3 mm FPC connector is hard to rework by hand.
findings.fix: Set a pad-level paste margin on J2's signal pads (about -0.035 mm in X and -0.05 to -0.075 mm in Y), or draw custom paste apertures to Hirose's stencil pattern. Optionally move fittings 16/17 out by 0.04 mm (to x = +-2.80).

findings.title: Copper in the DM3AT 'No conductive traces' areas under J3
findings.refs: J3 at KiCad (164.05, 110.79) rot 0. Hirose DM3 catalogue (C114218.pdf p.3) 'Recommended PCB mounting pattern', note 3 hatched areas, mapped to board coordinates: strip A x 156.94-157.64, y 103.69-111.74; strip B x 158.02-158.68, y 109.54-117.17; band C x 158.72-167.41, y 108.25-109.85; area D x 167.08-169.62, y 117.94-119.32
findings.evidence: I aligned the drawing to the footprint by contact 1 (local x 2.85), pad 14 (+1.55), the left pad column (-6.75) and pad 13 (6.75, 7.55, 1.3 x 1.9), which all match. Then I checked F.Cu tracks and vias. Band C: VBAT track (158.6,109.55)-(166.75,107.65) and VBAT via (158.6,109.55). Strip A: SD_CD track, SD_CS via (157.75,105.0), 3V3_PERIPH via (156.85,108.6), VBUS via (156.73,110.79). Strip B: SD_CD track (158.1,106.85)-(158.05,111.55). Area D: GND via (169.75,118.34) at its edge.
findings.requirement: Hirose DM3AT-SF-PEJM5 recommended PCB mounting pattern, note 3: 'No conductive traces' in the hatched areas (where the card-detect spring and the push-push mechanism sit on the board).
findings.consequence: Under solder mask this is usually harmless. The risk is that the detect spring or the ejector metal rubs through the mask over many insert cycles. VBAT then touches the GND shell, which is a direct battery short with no fuse, or SD_CD and SD_CS short to the spring. The probability is low, and it cannot be fixed with a wire after the fact. My coordinate mapping is good to about +-0.2 mm.
findings.fix: For rev A, accept it and note it. In the next spin, add rule-area keep-outs (no F.Cu tracks or vias) for the four hatched areas to the DM3AT footprint, and reroute VBAT and the vias out of them.

findings.title: R18 33R 0805 (1/8 W) is over its rating while the buzzer plays
findings.refs: BOM R18 C17634 = UniOhm 0805W8F330JT5E (0805, 1/8 W); design.py R18 VSYS-BZ_P, BZ1 MLT-5020, Q6 AO3400A, D2
findings.evidence: MLT-5020 datasheet (C94598.pdf p.2): coil resistance 12 +-3 ohm, rated 3.0 Vo-p, max 100 mA, driven with a 4 kHz 50 percent square wave. With R18 = 33R, the on-state current is VSYS/(33+12): 104 mA at 4.7 V (USB) and 93 mA at 4.2 V. R18 then dissipates 0.36 W (USB) or 0.29 W (battery) while on. At 50 percent duty that averages 0.18 W or 0.14 W. The coil time constant (about 1 mH / 45 ohm, roughly 25 us) is short against the 125 us half-period, so the current reaches steady state. README says 'about 0.1 W'.
findings.requirement: UniOhm 0805W8F series: 0.125 W rated at 70 C. MLT-5020: max 100 mA.
findings.consequence: During sustained tones R18 runs 15 to 45 percent over its rating, and the buzzer sits at or slightly above its 100 mA maximum on USB. If firmware ever leaves GPIO2 high, R18 takes 0.36 W continuously and can overheat. Short beeps are fine.
findings.fix: Swap R18 to a 1206 (or 0805 1/4 W) basic part. Alternatively, raise it to 47 to 56 ohm, which also brings the buzzer current under 100 mA. Or cap the PWM duty in firmware (25 percent or less) and limit the tone length.

findings.title: RT9080 output capacitor C11 (1 uF 0402 X5R) gives less than 1 uF effective at 3.3 V
findings.refs: C11 C52923 = Samsung CL05A105KA5NQNC (1 uF, 25 V, X5R, +-10 %, 0402) at U4 pin 5 (3V3), device (-22.3, -30.8); nearest bulk 3V3 cap C5 22 uF at device (18.6, -37.0), about 41 mm of track away
findings.evidence: RT9080 datasheet (C841192.txt l.129-132 and application circuits l.270-299): 'The minimum required output capacitance for stable operation is 1 uF effective capacitance after consideration of the temperature and voltage coefficient.' A 1 uF 0402 X5R at 3.3 V DC bias keeps about 60 to 80 percent, before its -10 % tolerance and temperature drift. I estimated this from typical Samsung CL05A curves, not from a measured curve for this exact part.
findings.requirement: RT9080: COUT of at least 1 uF effective at the output pin.
findings.consequence: The local output capacitance is probably below the stated minimum. The distant C5 22 uF and the other 3V3 decoupling likely keep the loop stable in practice, so the risk is ringing or reduced margin, not failure.
findings.fix: Use the 10 uF 0603 basic part already in the BOM (C19702, CL10A106KP8NNNC 10 V) for C11. Or use a 2.2 uF 0402 or 0603 X5R rated 10 V or more. The 0603 needs about 0.6 mm more length at (-22.3, -30.8).

findings.title: JLC's forced 'Plugged' via option conflicts with the open vias inside U1 and U2 thermal pads; ORDER.md still says 'Tented'
findings.refs: U1 pad 49 (nine 1.45 mm pads, 9 x 0.3 mm GND vias), U2 pad 25 (2.5 x 2.5, 4 x 0.3 mm vias), all with F.Paste and F.Mask openings; jlcpcb/ORDER.md 'Via covering | Tented'; README accepted exception 'open vias in the U1 and U2 thermal pads'
findings.evidence: The task states JLC's 4-layer form forces 'Plugged'. ORDER.md still lists 'Tented' and reasons that solder may wick into open vias. The accepted exception assumed the vias in pad stay open. With solder-mask plugging, ink can also be pushed into, or left proud of, vias that sit inside mask openings.
findings.requirement: JLC's via options: 'Plugged' fills vias with solder-mask ink. JLC's recommendation for via-in-pad is epoxy-filled and capped. I could not read JLC's exact current wording, hence low confidence.
findings.consequence: Ink nubs or partial plugs on U1's centre pads or U2's exposed pad can tilt the LGA module or cause voids. This reduces the thermal and ground contact of the EP, and the ESP32 module's outer pins may solder poorly. The accepted exception's reasoning (open vias, solder wicks) no longer describes what will be built.
findings.fix: Correct ORDER.md to 'Plugged'. Add an order remark: 'vias inside U1 and U2 pads: keep pads flat, no solder-mask ink on pads'. Or pay for epoxy filled and capped. Or move the 13 vias just outside the pads in a re-spin. Check JLC's DFM images of U1 and U2 before production.

findings.title: MPR121 corner pads are 0.32 mm wide (EasyEDA), not NXP's; the README attributes the tight gaps to NXP
findings.refs: lib/Harmony8.pretty/QFN-20_3x3_P0.4.kicad_mod custom pads 1,5,6,10,11,15,16,20 (polygon +-0.112 plus 0.1 stroke = 0.324 wide); README 'Changes from spec' row (0.12 inside the U6 land pattern, 'manufacturers' own land patterns (HRS, NXP...)')
findings.evidence: Computed edge gaps: pins 1-2, 4-5, 6-7 and 19-20 are 0.138 mm; pins 1-20, 5-6, 10-11 and 15-16 are 0.151 mm; the regular pads (2-3) are 0.20 mm. The adjacent nets include IRQ/VDD, ADDR(3V3)/VREG, VREG/VSS and VSS/REXT.
findings.requirement: NXP MPR121 datasheet package 98ASA00021D (C91322.pdf p.23): every terminal is 0.15-0.25 wide, 0.40-0.60 long, 0.4 pitch, with no exposed pad. NXP gives no land pattern with widened corner pads.
findings.consequence: It works for JLC (0.13+ mm), but the corner pads are wider than any terminal, which raises bridge risk at pins 5-6 (VREG to VSS). The README's stated reason for the DRC exception is inaccurate. The pad length and position otherwise fit the package (toe 0.3, heel about 0).
findings.fix: No action needed for rev A. In a re-spin, make the corner pads 0.2 to 0.22 wide like the others, and update the README wording.

findings.title: MLT-5020 footprint pads sit 0.45 mm outboard of the buzzer terminals
findings.refs: lib/Harmony8.pretty/Buzzer_MLT-5020.kicad_mod pads 1/2/3: 1.7 x 0.7 at x +-2.3, y +-1.75 (copper x 1.45 to 3.15); EasyEDA name 'P4.60' and 'W5.5'
findings.evidence: Huawha MLT-5020 dimension drawing (C94598.pdf p.4, measured at 400 dpi): body 5.0 +-0.3. There are three terminals of 1.5 x 0.8 at 3.5 mm row pitch, with a 2.0 mm gap between the bottom pair, so each terminal spans x 1.0 to 2.5 from centre. The footprint pad covers x 1.45 to 3.15, so about 1.05 mm of each 1.5 mm terminal is on copper and the pad extends 0.65 mm beyond the body. Polarity is correct: pad 1 (+) is at lower left in top view, matching the datasheet '+POLARITY'. The missing pad is at the chamfered top-right corner, which matches.
findings.requirement: Huawha MLT-5020 specification, section 4 (dimensions).
findings.consequence: Shear strength is somewhat lower but the joints are adequate (the terminals wrap the sides). JLC places this LCSC part with this footprint routinely.
findings.fix: None for rev A. Optionally shift the pads inward 0.3 to 0.4 mm in a re-spin.

findings.title: Exposed-pad paste is 100 percent on U2 and U1 centre pads
findings.refs: U2 QFN-24 pad 25: 2.5 x 2.5 paste with 4 open vias; U1 pad 49: nine 1.45 x 1.45 paste openings (18.9 mm2) with 9 open vias; U5 pad 9: 1.2 x 0.8 full paste
findings.evidence: Footprints carry F.Paste at pad size (pad_to_paste_clearance 0). CH9102F package drawing (C2858418.pdf p.7): EP 2.7 +-0.2, terminals 0.25 x 0.35, pitch 0.5. The footprint EP is 2.5 with a 0.35 mm EP-to-pad gap, which is fine.
findings.requirement: Usual QFN and LGA practice (for example IPC-7093) is 50 to 80 percent paste coverage on large thermal pads to avoid float and tilt and bridging on the perimeter pins.
findings.consequence: Slightly higher risk of the CH9102F or the module floating, with opens or bridges on 0.5 mm pins. It usually works at JLC.
findings.fix: Optional: windowpane the U2 EP paste (4 x 1.0 mm squares) and reduce U1's nine apertures to about 1.15 mm.

findings.title: rotation-check.csv leaves several polarised parts off the eye-check list
findings.refs: jlcpcb/rotation-check.csv: U3 (SOT-23-5), U4 (TSOT-23-5), U8 (SOT-23-6, rot 270), Q2, Q3, Q4 (AO3401A), Q5 (AO3400A rot 90), Q6, SW2/SW3 have an empty 'Check in JLC preview' column
findings.evidence: The README 'Check before paying' list names U2, U5, U6, U7, Q1, LED1, D1, D2 and the connectors, but not these 3-, 5- and 6-pin parts. Their land patterns are not symmetric, so a wrong rotation would put pins on the wrong nets.
findings.requirement: JLC applies its own library orientation per LCSC part. The owner's placement-preview check is the only guard against a database rotation error.
findings.consequence: A 90 or 180 degree database error on, for example, U4 or U8 would short rails (U8 pin 5 is VBUS, pin 2 GND).
findings.fix: In JLC's preview, also confirm the pin-1 marks of U3, U4, U8 and the SOT-23 orientation of Q2 to Q6 (single pin 3 opposite pins 1 and 2).

findings.title: MCP73831 input capacitor C7 derates to about 2.5 uF at 5 V
findings.refs: C7 C19666 = Samsung CL10A475KO8NNNC (4.7 uF, 16 V, X5R, 0603) on VBUS at U3 pin 4; C1 C15850 = CL21A106KAYNNNE (10 uF, 25 V, X5R, 0805) on VBUS at J1
findings.evidence: MCP73831 datasheet (C424093.txt l.837-845): VDD 'Bypass to VSS with a minimum of 4.7 uF'. A 4.7 uF 0603 X5R at 5 V typically keeps about 50 to 60 percent (estimate from typical curves). C1 adds about 5 to 6 uF effective on the same net, roughly 25 mm away. VBAT C8 (CL10A106KP8NNNC, 10 V) at 4.2 V keeps about 5 uF, which meets the 4.7 uF VBAT bypass.
findings.requirement: MCP73831: 4.7 uF minimum on VDD and on VBAT.
findings.consequence: Probably fine thanks to C1. The charger has only marginal local input bypass.
findings.fix: None required. Optionally use the 10 uF 0805 25 V (C15850) for C7.

findings.title: DRV2605L VSSOP-10 pads are shorter on the heel side than TI's land pattern

verdicts.reasoning: Checked the primary data myself. Footprint lib/Harmony8.pretty/USB-C_HRO_TYPE-C-31-M-12.kicad_mod: pads 1-4 are thru_hole oval with (layers "*.Cu" "*.Mask"), no F.Paste, and the footprint is (attr smd). PTH.drl has the four G85 slots at X145.67/154.33, Y-113.41..-114.11 and Y-117.74..-118.14. I parsed F_Paste.gtp: 341 D03 flashes, no region (G36) fills. Within 1.5 x 2 mm of each slot the only flashes are (146.8,-113.0) and (153.2,-113.0), which are the A1B12/B1A12 signal pads. So the slots get no paste. ORDER.md names the 'through-hole shell legs' only as a reason for Standard PCBA. It has no remark asking JLC to solder them. JLC's own pin-in-paste guide says JLC opens a through-hole stencil aperture only if the pad is on the paste layer of the Gerbers. JLC's assembly FAQ covers hand soldering only for parts marked 'wave soldering' in its library, and C165948 is an SMT part. HRO drawing C165948.pdf gives plated slots, insertion force 0.5-2.0 kgf and removal force 0.8-2.0 kgf (note 3), and IR reflow (note 6), so HRO means the legs to be soldered. I could not settle whether JLC's engineers add apertures on their own for this part. The data as sent gives no paste on the legs and no instruction, so I confirm the problem but not the outcome. Mitigation: unsoldered legs still sit in plated slots and take some shear, and if they come out unsoldered it is 4 easy hand joints, so this is major, not a blocker. Extra detail: the EasyEDA slots are 0.8 mm wide x 1.5/1.2 mm long. HRO's recommended slots are 0.60 wide x 1.70/1.40 long, with 0.90 x 2.00/1.70 pads. So pin-in-paste fill with these wider slots needs more paste than HRO's geometry would.
verdicts.fix: Before paying, add an order remark: 'J1 (C165948): please solder the 4 shell through-hole legs (stencil apertures over the slots / pin-in-paste, or hand solder)'. Then check JLC's DFM or stencil preview, or ask support, to confirm. If that is refused, plan 4 hand joints per board at bring-up. In a re-spin, add F.Paste to pads 1-4 with apertures larger than the slot, or move to HRO's 0.6 mm slot geometry.

verdicts.reasoning: Footprint primitives: A1B12 at x -3.2, polygon x -0.30..+0.30 plus a 0.1 stroke, so copper runs x -3.55..-2.85. A4B9 at x -2.4 runs -2.75..-2.05. The gap is 0.10 mm. B1A12/B4A9 mirror this. Nets per board: A1B12/B1A12 GND, A4B9/B4A9 VBUS. I read HRO drawing C165948.pdf at 600 dpi. 'Recommend P.C.B layout' gives '4-0.60' power pads, A1/B12 centres at 6.40 (±3.20) and A4/B9 centres at 4.80 (±2.40). That is 0.8 mm pitch with 0.60 width, so the gap is 0.20 mm. The README 'Changes from spec' row (0.09 inside the J1 land pattern, 'manufacturers' own land patterns (HRO...)') and ORDER.md 'Check before paying' item 2 misattribute the gap: it comes from EasyEDA's 0.70 mm pads, not from HRO. The paste apertures are also 0.70 wide (FreePoly0-2 in F_Paste.gtp span ±0.35), so the GND-VBUS paste gap is 0.10 mm. Bridge risk goes up but this footprint is common at JLC. A bridge is found with a meter before USB is plugged in and can be reworked, so minor.
verdicts.fix: Rev A: either narrow the four custom power-pad polygons so copper is 0.60 wide (polygon ±0.25 plus the 0.1 stroke, or a plain 0.6 x 1.3 rect). That gives a 0.20 mm gap and lets the J1 0.09 rule go from the .kicad_dru. Or keep the pads and correct the README and ORDER.md wording. At bring-up, measure VBUS to GND resistance before the first USB plug-in.

verdicts.reasoning: Footprint FH35C-15S-0.3SHW.kicad_mod: odd pads 0.3 x 0.8, even pads 0.3 x 0.65, fittings 0.4 x 0.95, all on F.Paste. There are no solder_paste_margin or ratio entries, and the board setup has none either (only pad_to_mask_clearance 0), so the stencil is 1:1. Hirose EDC3-338903-01 sheet 1 (C2889267.pdf p.1, read at 300 dpi) 'Recommended stencil pattern (t=0.1)' gives 0.23 ±0.02 wide openings, 0.55 ±0.02 long (contact-2 row) and 0.7 ±0.02 long (contact-1 row), and fitting openings 0.3 ±0.02 wide. Aperture area: 0.24 vs 0.161 mm2 and 0.195 vs 0.127 mm2, about 50 percent more paste than Hirose specifies (more than the reviewer's 30-40 percent), and more again if JLC cuts a 0.12 mm stencil. The fitting position is minor: contact 1 centreline (x 2.1) to fitting inner edge (2.76-0.2 = 2.56) is 0.46 against Hirose's 0.5 ±0.03. Fitting y offset 0.205 against 0.2 is fine. Copper otherwise matches. Risk: bridges or wicking on the 0.3 mm pitch screen connector, which is hard to rework, but the board is not dead by default.
verdicts.fix: Rev A: set a pad-level solder_paste_margin of about -0.035 mm on J2 pads 1-15, which gives 0.23 wide openings and roughly 0.73/0.58 long.
