verdicts.reasoning: I rendered Hirose DM3 catalogue p.3 'Recommended PCB mounting pattern' at 900 dpi and aligned it myself. Contact-1 centreline maps to J3 local x 2.85, the contact-row lower edge to y -6.95, the left pad column to x -7.25..-6.25 and pad 13 (1.3 x 1.9) to y 6.6..8.5. The 9.1, 3.25, 1.3 and 14.05 dimensions all check at 41.5 px/mm. The hatched 'No conductive traces' areas in board coordinates (J3 at 164.05,110.79, rot 0) are: A x 156.88-157.68, y 103.67-111.74; B x 158.03-158.68, y 109.57-117.12; C x 158.68-167.36, y 108.25-109.82; D x 167.02-169.48, y 117.89-119.29. These agree with the reviewer to about 0.06 mm. F.Cu copper inside them, from the parsed .kicad_pcb: in C, the VBAT 0.4 mm track (158.6,109.55)-(166.75,107.65) runs about 5 mm inside the band, and the VBAT via at (158.6,109.55) is at its edge. In A, vias SD_CS (157.75,105.0), 3V3_PERIPH (156.85,108.6) and VBUS (156.73,110.79), plus SD_CD, 3V3_PERIPH and VBUS tracks. In B, the SD_CD track (158.1,106.85)-(158.05,111.55). D is clear (the GND via at 169.75 is just outside). All are under solder mask. VBAT under band C sits below the metal push-push and detect parts, and a mask wear-through would short VBAT to the GND shell. That is low probability, and the battery pack's own protection limits it.
verdicts.fix: Accept for rev A and record it in README. In a re-spin, add rule-area keep-outs (no F.Cu tracks or vias) for the four hatched areas to the DM3AT footprint, and move VBAT and the three vias out, VBAT first.

verdicts.reasoning: BOM R18 = C17634, which stock.json gives as UNI-ROYAL 0805W8F330JT5E. 'W8' in UniRoyal's part code means 1/8 W, the same scheme as R17 1206W4 = 1/4 W. I did not open the UniRoyal datasheet. design.py: R18 33R from VSYS to BZ_P, BZ1, Q6 AO3400A low side, D2 flyback across the coil, so R18 conducts only while Q6 is on. MLT-5020 spec (C94598.pdf p.2): coil 12 ±3 ohm, max 100 mA, rated 3.0 Vo-p, driven with a 50 percent square wave. On-state current is VSYS/(33+12): about 104 mA at VSYS 4.7 V on USB and 93 mA at 4.2 V. R18 dissipates about 0.36 W or 0.29 W while on, about 0.18 W or 0.14 W at 50 percent duty, against 0.125 W. Firmware slab_buzzer.c caps duty at 50 percent (line 36) and drives short clicks by default, but slab_buzzer_tone() allows sustained tones. README line 270 'about 0.1 W' is low for full battery or USB. Short clicks are fine (0805 thermal time constant, short-time overload). Sustained tones run R18 over its rating, and the buzzer sits at about its 100 mA maximum on USB. Firmware can fix this, so minor.
verdicts.fix: Lowest effort: in firmware, cap sustained-tone duty at about 30 percent and limit tone length (clicks unchanged). Part fix: change R18 to 47 ohm 0805. That gives 80 mA, 0.21 W on, about 0.1 W at 50 percent, and keeps the buzzer under 100 mA. Or use a 1206 1/4 W 33R, which needs a footprint change.

verdicts.reasoning: RT9080 datasheet (C841192.txt l.129-132): 'minimum required output capacitance for stable operation is 1uF effective capacitance after consideration of the temperature and voltage coefficient'. The application circuits also say 'Effective Capacitance 1uF'. C11 = C52923 = Samsung CL05A105KA5NQNC (stock.json), 1 uF X5R 0402 ±10 %. On the board C11 is about 3.2 mm from U4 pin 5 (3V3). The next 3V3 bulk is C5 22 uF at about 43 mm straight line, and C13 is 100 nF at about 21 mm. A 1 uF 0402 X5R at 3.3 V bias typically keeps well under 100 percent of nominal. I did not have the Samsung DC-bias curve, so the exact figure is an estimate. With -10 % tolerance the local effective capacitance is very likely below 1 uF. The distant 22 uF probably keeps the loop stable (track inductance about 40-50 nH is small against the LDO bandwidth), so the risk is margin, not failure.
verdicts.fix: Swap C11 to the 10 uF 0603 basic part already in the BOM (C19702, CL10A106KP8NNNC). This needs the 0603 footprint at C11 and a quick DRC. If the footprint must stay 0402, use a 2.2 uF 0402 rated 6.3 V or more and check its bias curve keeps 1 uF or more at 3.3 V. On the first board, check 3V3 for ringing during a WiFi or BT transmit burst.

verdicts.reasoning: I confirmed the facts: 9 vias inside U1 pad 49 and 4 inside U2 pad 25 (counted from the parsed board), all in pads with F.Paste and F.Mask openings. ORDER.md still says 'Via covering | Tented'. But the claimed consequence does not hold. JLC's via-covering help page says 'holes in pad, and vias with a distance less than 0.35mm from the pad cannot be plugged with ink', and that such vias need epoxy or copper filling. So with 'Plugged' JLC does not push mask ink into the U1 and U2 pad vias. They stay open, which is exactly what README and ORDER.md already accept (solder may wick, pads are GND and thermal, the pins carry the signals). The 'ink nubs tilt the LGA module' mechanism is not supported by JLC's own description. What remains is a documentation mismatch: ORDER.md names an option the 4-layer form does not offer. Side note: many GND fan-out vias with 0.25 mm stubs also sit within 0.35 mm of pads, so JLC will not ink-plug those either. They are still covered by mask in the Gerbers, so expect a DFM comment, nothing worse.
verdicts.fix: Edit ORDER.md: 'Via covering: Plugged (the only 4-layer option; JLC does not ink-plug vias in pads or within 0.35 mm of a pad, so the U1 and U2 pad vias stay open as accepted)'. No design change. Look at JLC's DFM images of U1 and U2 before production as already planned.

verdicts.reasoning: Footprints have F.Paste at full pad size: U2 pad 25 is 2.5 x 2.5 with 4 vias, U1 pad 49 is nine 1.45 x 1.45 with 9 vias, U5 pad 9 is 1.2 x 0.8. verdicts.reasoning: jlcpcb/rotation-check.csv: the 'Check in JLC preview' column is empty for U3 (rot 0), U4 (rot 0), U8 (rot 270), Q2/Q3/Q4 (rot 0), Q5 (rot 90), Q6 (rot 0), SW2/SW3 (rot 90), matching cpl.csv. verdicts.reasoning: MCP73831 datasheet (C424093.txt l.837-845): VDD 'Bypass to VSS with a minimum of 4.7 uF'. C7 = C19666 = CL10A475KO8NNNC (4.7 uF 16 V X5R 0603), about 4.7 mm from U3 pin 4 on the board. At 5 V DC bias it keeps substantially less than nominal. The reviewer's figure of about 2.5 uF is a typical-curve estimate, which I could not confirm for this exact part. Correction: C1 10 uF 0805 is not about 25 mm away. It sits at J1, about 43 mm in straight line from U3 pin 4, so it helps less. The MCP73831 is a linear charger, and the input cap mainly damps cable inductance, so this is unlikely to cause a fault. VBAT C8 (C19702 10 uF 0603 10 V) meets the 4.7 uF VBAT recommendation (l.1257) with margin.
verdicts.fix: None required. Optionally use the 10 uF 0805 25 V part (C15850) for C7, which needs the 0805 footprint.

verdicts.reasoning: VSSOP-10_DRV2605L.kicad_mod: pads 0.3 x 1.3 at y ±2.35, so copper runs 1.70..3.00. TI DGS0010A 'Example board layout' (C527464.txt l.3891-3912): 10X (0.3) x (1.45) on (4.4) row centres, so pads run 1.475..2.925. Package E 4.75-5.05 and L 0.4-0.7 (detail A). Worst-case foot inner end = 2.375-0.7 = 1.675, so at most 0.025 mm of the heel is off the pad. Toe extension is longer than TI's. Joints are acceptable.
verdicts.fix: None for rev A. In a re-spin, use TI's 1.45 mm pad on 4.4 mm centres.

areas.title: PCB layout and manufacturability

findings.title: USB-C J1 VBUS and GND pads are 0.1 mm too wide (footprint import error), which leaves a 0.10 mm VBUS-to-GND gap where HRO specifies 0.20 mm
findings.refs: lib/Harmony8.pretty/USB-C_HRO_TYPE-C-31-M-12.kicad_mod pads A1B12, A4B9, B4A9, B1A12 (custom gr_poly 0.6 x 1.3 with (width 0.1) stroke). Board: J1.A1B12 GND x 146.45-147.15 and J1.A4B9 VBUS x 147.25-147.95 (KiCad, y 112.3-113.7; device x +3.2 / +2.4, y -43.0); the same on B4A9/B1A12 at KiCad x 152.05-153.55. Same import error on U6 (lib/.../QFN-20_3x3_P0.4.kicad_mod, 8 corner pads 1,5,6,10,11,15,16,20). kicad_dru rules 'J1 USB-C vendor land pattern' and 'U6 MPR121 0.4 mm pitch land pattern'.
findings.evidence: Measured pad copper (pcbnew dump): A1B12 and A4B9 are 0.70 x 1.40 mm, with 0.100 mm between them. The custom pad polygon is 0.6 x 1.3 mm, but easyeda2kicad kept the EasyEDA outline stroke (width 0.1), which adds 0.05 mm on every side. Paste and mask follow the copper, so the two stencil apertures are 0.70 mm wide with 0.10 mm between them, and the mask dam is 0.10 mm. The U6 corner pads are the same: 0.224 mm polygon + 0.1 stroke = 0.324 mm wide, so the gap is 0.138 mm instead of about 0.19 mm.
findings.requirement: HRO TYPE-C-31-M-12 drawing (C165948.pdf, 'Recommend P.C.B layout'): '4-0.60' for the GND/VBUS pads, '8-0.30' for the signal pads, at 0.8 mm GND-to-VBUS centre spacing, so the gap is 0.20 mm. JLCPCB capabilities: the solder mask bridge needs pad spacing of at least 0.10 mm for green and 0.13 mm for black or white. README 'Changes from spec' says the 0.09 mm gap is 'the manufacturers' own land pattern'. That is wrong: it comes from the import, not from HRO.
findings.consequence: A solder bridge between VBUS and GND at the receptacle is likely enough to plan for: full-width paste at 0.10 mm spacing with a dam at JLC's minimum (and no dam at all if black mask is chosen). A bridge shorts USB VBUS, so the board cannot be powered or charged from USB until the joint is reworked with an iron. The U6 0.4 mm-pitch corner pads have the same smaller margin.
findings.fix: Before ordering, remove the 0.1 stroke from the custom pad primitives in both footprints (set width 0, or redraw the pads as 0.6 x 1.3 rectangles at the HRO positions). Then rerun DRC, delete the J1 and U6 exceptions from the .kicad_dru (they will no longer be needed), and regenerate the Gerbers. Order green mask, not black. The board colour cannot be seen in the device: L4 sits behind the front skin and the wheel disc. With the import error left in place, black (0.13 mm minimum) also removes the J1 dams. At bring-up, measure VBUS to GND before the first USB plug-in.

findings.title: J1 shell plated slots (0.8 x 1.2 and 0.8 x 1.5) break JLC's 2:1 plated-slot rule and differ from HRO's 0.6 mm slots
findings.refs: J1 pads 1-4 (GND): KiCad (145.67/154.33, 113.76) drill 0.8 x 1.5, pad 1.2 x 2.0; (145.67/154.33, 117.94) drill 0.8 x 1.2, pad 1.2 x 1.8. jlcpcb/gerbers PTH.drl T3 C0.800 with G85 slots. lib/Harmony8.pretty/USB-C_HRO_TYPE-C-31-M-12.kicad_mod.
findings.evidence: Drill file: T3 0.8 mm, 4 G85 slots: 145.67 y 113.41 to 114.11 (1.5 long) and 117.74 to 118.14 (1.2 long). Length-to-width ratios are 1.875 and 1.5.
findings.requirement: JLCPCB PCB capabilities: 'The length of the slot should be at least 2 times of the width' (plated slot). HRO drawing: slot 0.60 wide ('0.60' inner / '0.90' outer), 1.70 long at the front and 1.40 long at the rear, giving ratios 2.8 and 2.3.
findings.consequence: JLC's DFM may flag the slots, or drill them as short, misshapen slots. The legs still fit (they are about 0.3 thick), but the slots are not what the maker specifies and the DFM can hold the order.
findings.fix: Change the four slots to HRO's 0.6 x 1.7 (front) and 0.6 x 1.4 (rear), with 0.9 x 2.0 and 0.9 x 1.7 pads. Make this change in the same footprint pass as L1.

findings.title: With 'Plugged' via covering, the vias in pads stay open on top and tented underneath; one in-pad via (U8 pin 2) is not documented, and 6 of U1's are under electrode ELE3
findings.refs: U1 pad 49: 9 vias 0.3/0.5 at KiCad x 131.82/133.80/135.78, y 97.32/99.30/101.28. U2 pad 25: 4 vias at (137.5/138.7, 115.0/116.2). U8 pad 2 (GND): via at KiCad (141.30, 115.60), device (8.70, -45.60), not listed in README or ORDER.md. jlcpcb/ORDER.md 'Via covering: Tented' and 'Via in pad'.
findings.evidence: Measured: 44% of the U8.2 via hole lies inside the U8.2 mask opening, so the via is partly in the pad. All 14 in-pad vias have an F.Mask opening above them. B.Mask has only 10 openings (SW1, H1, H2 and J1 holes), so these vias are covered by mask on L4. The U1 vias at x 133.80 and 135.78 (r 14.2 to 16.6 from the wheel centre) lie inside the ELE3 electrode outline on L4.
findings.requirement: JLC via-covering help page: plugged vias must have no soldermask opening on either side; 'No ink filling for single or double-sided pad openings'; the >98% plugging rate excludes vias in pads; for vias in pads, use epoxy or copper fill. JLC capabilities, plugged vias: '>= 0.35 mm clearance from other soldermask openings'.
findings.consequence: The plugged option does not change these 14 vias. They are open on the pad side and mask-tented on L4, which is the case README accepted for tented vias. Paste wicks into each barrel (about 0.04 mm3 each), which gives voids under the U1/U2 ground pads. That is acceptable: both parts have other GND pins, and the ESP32-PICO-MINI-02 datasheet says the EPAD does not have to be soldered. Two risks are new. (1) U8 pin 2 is the only ground of the USB ESD clamp; the via barrel holds more solder than the 0.53 x 1.07 mm pad's paste gives, so the joint can starve. Then ESD protection is lost, but USB still works. (2) Trapped gas in the 6 U1 vias under ELE3 can push solder through the L4 tent and leave a bump on the touch face under the wheel disc, which can make the disc rock.
findings.fix: Preferred: order 'Epoxy Filled & Capped' (check the price on the quote). It fills and caps every via, including the 14 in pads and the 148 near pads (see L4). Otherwise, move the U8.2 via out of the pad (it has room toward -X), keep Plugged, and after assembly inspect L4 around the U1 vias (device x 14.2 to 16.2, y -27.4 to -31.3). In both cases, update ORDER.md: it still says 'Tented'.

findings.title: About 60% of the vias cannot be ink-plugged under JLC's 0.35 mm rule, and one signal via is 0.02 mm from a QFN pad opening
findings.refs: 148 vias whose pad edge is less than 0.35 mm from a mask opening, plus the 14 in-pad vias from L3: 162 of 272 in all. Worst case: the DTR via at KiCad (138.85, 118.17), device (11.15, -48.17), 0.02 mm from the U2.23 (DTR) opening. Others at 0.13 to 0.15 mm: BAT_P (169.118, 88.018) to J4.2, TOUCH_IRQ (136.2, 104.418) to U1.9, I2C_SCL (134.418, 85.4) to TP10, HAPTIC_EN (173.667, 105.835) to U7.10, SD_MOSI (131.4, 92.612) to U1.33. Scratch list: review-work/layout/via_mask_dist.json.
findings.evidence: Computed from the pad mask polygons (mask expansion 0) and via annuli. Distances from the via pad edge: 0.0-0.1 mm: 1 via, 0.1-0.2: 27, 0.2-0.3: 111, 0.3-0.35: 9. Measured from the hole edge, 153 vias are within 0.35 mm.
findings.requirement: JLC capabilities, plugged vias: 'Filled vias should have >= 0.35 mm clearance from other soldermask openings (e.g. pads)'. JLC via-covering page: 'vias with a distance less than 0.35mm from the pad cannot be plugged with ink'.
findings.consequence: JLC does not say what it does with these vias. Most likely they are tented, which is what the design assumed, so the function is not at risk. Expect a DFM query or a hold. At the DTR via, a 0.05 mm mask misregistration exposes the via ring beside U2 pin 23. Solder can then wick from that 0.28 mm pin, so the auto-reset can fail; the BOOT and RESET buttons still work.
findings.fix: Choosing Epoxy Filled & Capped (L3) removes the question. Otherwise, move the DTR via about 0.2 mm away from U2.23, and add 'vias closer than 0.35 mm to pads may be tented instead of plugged' to the order remark, so the DFM engineer does not hold the order.

findings.title: The L1 GND pour fills the Alps 'prohibited area of copper tracks' under SW1
findings.refs: SW1 SKRTLAE010 at KiCad (124.52, 85.6) rot -90; area between the rear pads 4 and 5, KiCad x 123.10-124.30, y 84.6-86.6 (device x 25.7-26.9, y -14.6 to -16.6). Zone L1_GND (F.Cu), plus L2/L3/L4 GND inner pours.
findings.evidence: Shapely intersection: L1_GND covers 2.40 mm2 of this 2.0 x 1.2 mm region (100%). No track or via is there.
findings.requirement: Alps SKRTLAE010 datasheet (C110293.pdf p.3, Land Dimensions): a hatched 2 x 1.2 mm 'Prohibitted area of copper tracks' between the two rear pads.
findings.consequence: The copper is under mask and on GND, so a short is unlikely. Pad 2 (SIDE_BTN) is the switched contact, though, and the switch's underside sits on this area. If the mask is scuffed or thin there, SIDE_BTN can short to GND and read as a button held down. This deviates from the vendor land pattern.
findings.fix: Add an F.Cu keep-out rule area over this rectangle (pour only) and refill. It does not affect routing.

findings.title: SD_SCK is 82 mm long with no series termination, and 35 mm of it runs over the 25% hatch; README says the SD lines go around the wheel, but they cross it
findings.refs: Net SD_SCK (ESP32 GPIO5 to J3 pin 5): L1 35.4 mm inside r<16.6, 6.5 mm at r 16.6-17.6, 39.1 mm outside, 1.3 mm on L3. SD_MOSI 32.8 mm and SD_MISO 36.2 mm on L1 inside r<16.6. README 'Firmware notes' item 5. firmware/mark-8/components/slab_board/Kconfig SLAB_SD_SPI_KHZ default 20000; no gpio_set_drive_capability call in components/ or slab-*/.
findings.evidence: Sampled every track at 0.1 mm against the L2 zone fills: SD_SCK has 41.9 mm over the L2 hatch, 38.1 mm over solid L2, 1.0 mm over antipads. There is no resistor in series with GPIO5. Coupling to other nets is small (at most 7.2 mm within 0.3 mm of VBAT, 3.2 mm of SD_MISO).
findings.requirement: Rule of thumb: an unterminated line behaves as a transmission line when it is longer than about 1/6 of the edge length. ESP32 GPIO default drive is about 20 mA (CAP_2), with edges of about 1-2 ns, which is about 35-40 mm in FR-4. AN3863 sec. 3.1: keep traces away from the back of electrodes. ESP32 HDG 1.4.9: SD clock over a continuous reference plane.
findings.consequence: Ringing on the card clock edges can double-clock the card. Lowering the SPI frequency does not help, because ringing depends on the edge rate. The README's 'go around' statement also understates the SD bus switching behind the electrodes (about 105 mm on L1 over the hatch).
findings.fix: Firmware only, no board change: set GPIO5 (and GPIO19) to GPIO_DRIVE_CAP_0 or _1 before mounting the card. If reads fail, test at 10 MHz with weak drive. Correct README note 5. Include card reads in the touch-noise test (README item 6 already does this).

findings.title: The VBUS and 3V3 path resistances are about 70% higher than README states
findings.refs: VBUS: J1 A4B9/B4A9 to D1.2 = 171 mOhm, to U3.4 = 178 mOhm. 3V3: U4.5 to U1.3 = 127 mOhm, to Q4.2 = 50 mOhm. VSYS: D1.1 to U4.1 = 98 mOhm. README 'Touch-wheel re-route', VBUS paragraph ('about 0.1 ohm').
findings.evidence: Nodal solve over every track segment, with L1 at 35 um and L3 at 17.5 um (0.5 oz inner, as in ORDER.md), and vias and pads at zero resistance. The narrow sections alone come to 23.5 + 37 + 45.5 = 106 mOhm, which matches README's 0.1 ohm. The 0.4 mm sections add about 70 mOhm more.
findings.requirement: IPC-2221 external: 0.2 mm x 1 oz at 0.75 A rises about 12 K. Inner 0.3 mm x 0.5 oz at 0.75 A rises about 15-20 K (IPC-2152 style). Both are acceptable.
findings.consequence: On USB, the charger (370 mA) plus the VSYS load through D1 (backlight up to 170 mA, plus the ESP32) puts about 0.6-0.8 A on the shared trunk. The drop is about 0.11-0.14 V, not 50 mV. From a weak 4.75 V port, U3 sees about 4.6 V. 3V3 at U1 sags about 60 mV at 0.5 A RF peaks. This is not a failure, but README's margin numbers are optimistic.
findings.fix: No board change needed. Correct the README number. On the first boards, measure VBUS at U3 and D1 while charging with the backlight at full.

findings.title: The order documents are stale against the forced 'Plugged' option and the expected DFM comments
findings.refs: jlcpcb/ORDER.md PCB form 'Via covering: Tented' and 'Via in pad'; README 'Check before paying' item 3 and 'Changes from spec' row 'Track and space 0.127 minimum'; SW1 NPTH holes at KiCad (124.6, 83.47) and (124.6, 87.72).
findings.evidence: ORDER.md still says Tented. README lists 0.09 mm in J1 and 0.12 mm in U6; the measured gaps are 0.100 and 0.138 mm. The SW1 0.9 mm NPTH holes are 0.075 mm from SW1 pads 1 and 3. That is the Alps pattern (accepted in README) but below JLC's 'NPTH to Track 0.2 mm'. README item 3 says 'anything else, stop and look', yet it omits the SW1 NPTH clearance, the J1 slot ratio (L2) and the 0.35 mm plugging rule (L4).
findings.requirement: JLC capabilities: NPTH to track 0.2 mm; plated slot length at least 2x width; plugged-via clearance 0.35 mm.
findings.consequence: DFM comments that the documents do not predict will stop the order, or lead to a wrong accept or reject. The SW1 comment is harmless: JLC clips the pad corners.
findings.fix: Update ORDER.md (via covering, colour green, remark text) and README item 3 to list the SW1 NPTH clearance, the slot ratio (if not fixed), and the plugging-distance comment.

findings.title: Electrode feed lines ELE8 and ELE2 run on L3 0.1 mm behind other electrodes, and their vias sit inside other electrodes
findings.refs: ELE8 (0.127 mm): L3 under ELE0 8.1 mm, ELE1 3.6 mm, ELE2 4.1 mm, 2.6 mm in gaps; vias at KiCad (150.75, 89.05) inside ELE1 and (151.65, 98.15). ELE2: L3 under ELE0 5.2 mm; via (147.3, 98.7) inside ELE0. ELE1 on L1 under ELE2 7.0 mm and ELE3 2.9 mm.
findings.evidence: Per-net sampling against the L4 electrode fills. All 9 electrodes are single pieces of 72-78 mm2 (centre 146 mm2), and each contains its E1 pad.
findings.requirement: AN3863 sec. 3.1, 'Routing layers': route touch traces on a layer other than the electrodes, keep them away from the electrode area, and keep the trace area small compared with the electrode. Checklist: traces that cross go on another layer, perpendicular.
findings.consequence: Where the trace is fully under the other electrode's copper, that copper shields it from the finger. Crosstalk comes only at the 0.4/0.8 mm gaps and the 0.2 mm2 via pads on L4, so expect a small ELE8 response to touches on ELE1/ELE2/ELE0. README already mentions ELE2/ELE8 on L3; the numbers here are for the threshold tuning.
findings.fix: No action for rev A. When logging noise (README item 5), also log ELE8 while touching ELE1, ELE2 and the centre.

findings.title: The L3 DC nets behind the electrodes are not all quiet, and the L2 hatch is denser than AN3863 recommends
findings.refs: L3 track inside r<16.6 (verification.json): 383 mm in all, including VBUS 40.9 mm, 3V3 41.2, 3V3_PERIPH 28.1, VSYS 23.5, VBAT 20.3, LCD_LEDA 11.9. L2_GND_HATCH_25PCT: copper fraction 0.356 (verification.json). LCD_LEDK (backlight PWM drain) 16.6 mm on L1 over the hatch. BZ1 at r 7.1 behind the ELE0/ring boundary. U1 module partly behind ELE3.
findings.evidence: 0.4 mm track at 0.1 mm below an electrode is about 0.16 pF/mm parallel-plate (more with fringing), so VBUS alone is about 7-10 pF. The hatch at 0.55 mm is about 2 pF per sector electrode.
findings.requirement: AN3863 sec. 3.4: an X-hatch of about 20% with about 50 mil spacing under electrodes; avoid traces and components behind electrodes, especially noisy ones.
findings.consequence: The README classes VBUS (charger and adapter ripple when plugged in) and 3V3_PERIPH (SD card current spikes through the trace resistance) as DC, but both carry AC noise that couples directly into the electrodes. The baseline offset is well inside the MPR121 range, so sensitivity is fine, but expect touch noise to rise while charging and while the card reads.
findings.fix: No board change for rev A. Extend README item 5's noise logging to include 'USB charger plugged in (cheap adapter)' and the backlight PWM sweep. The PWM sweep is already mentioned.

findings.title: Silkscreen labels are below JLC's minimum size
findings.refs: F.Silkscreen texts 'BOOT', 'RST', 'M+', 'M-', '1' (0.6 mm high, 0.12 stroke), 'BAT', 'M8 SLAB A' (0.7/0.12), 'JLCJLCJLCJLC' (0.8/0.15). 128 graphic segments at 0.12 mm, 24 at 0.06, 1 at 0.10.
findings.evidence: pcbnew text and shape query on the saved board.
findings.requirement: JLC capabilities: silkscreen line width at least 0.15 mm, text height at least 1.0 mm.
findings.consequence: The motor polarity marks M+/M- and the BOOT/RST labels may print blurred. Function is not affected. SPEC asks for plain battery +/- marks; check that the J4 +/- marks are graphics of at least 0.15 mm.
findings.fix: Raise these texts to 1.0 mm / 0.15 mm where space allows, or accept them as they are.

findings.title: The J1 shell legs have no paste aperture, so the legs are soldered only if JLC adds a through-hole step
findings.refs: J1 pads 1-4 (thru_hole oval, layers *.Cu *.Mask, no F.Paste); F_Paste.gtp has no flash at (145.67/154.33, 113.76/117.94).
findings.evidence: Pad layer list from the dump. F_Paste.gtp has 341 flashes, none at the slot positions.
findings.requirement: JLC Standard PCBA makes the stencil from the paste layer. Through-hole joints need wave, selective or hand soldering, or a paste-in-hole aperture.
findings.consequence: If JLC treats J1 as SMD only, the four shell legs stay unsoldered. Then the 12 signal pads take every plug insertion force, and the receptacle can lift. JLC normally solders these legs for this LCSC part, but nothing in the files asks for it. The enclosure's L4 reliefs assume soldered legs.
findings.fix: Add an order remark ('please solder the 4 USB-C shell legs'), or add paste apertures over the shell pads (pin-in-paste). Check the legs on arrival.

findings.title: Smaller package items: a floating L2 copper fragment, E1 holes classed as component holes, drill-map files in the zip, and an unverified stack-up
findings.refs: L2_GND_HATCH_25PCT fragment of 0.04 mm2 with no via or pad at KiCad (135.26-135.48, 107.30-107.60), device (14.6, -37.4). E1 pads: 0.3 drill / 0.6 pad PTH in PTH.drl tool T2 (ComponentDrill), 0.2775 mm from the L2 hatch and 0.283 mm from the VSYS track at E1.8 on L3. Zip includes PTH-drl_map.gbr and NPTH-drl_map.gbr. gbrjob stack-up shows three 0.2133 mm dielectrics.
findings.evidence: Island scan, hole-to-copper scan and file listing.
findings.requirement: JLC: inner-layer PTH pad hole to copper 0.3 mm (via hole 0.2 mm); PTH annular ring 0.15 minimum, 0.20 recommended. README's touch numbers assume L3 is about 0.1 mm behind L4, which is true only for JLC's 0.8 mm default with a thin prepreg.
findings.consequence: Each item is cosmetic or a DFM-comment risk. If JLC's default 0.8 mm stack-up is not the thin-prepreg build, the L3-to-electrode spacing changes, which helps the touch coupling numbers.
findings.fix: Optional: make E1 pads vias, or accept a DFM note. Remove the two drl_map files from the upload zip. When JLC shows the stack-up during ordering, note its prepreg thickness.

checked: Gerber zip unpacked into scratch: all 15 files byte-identical to jlcpcb/gerbers; zip sha256 7d3a07df... and board sha256 c0e475cb... match jlcpcb/package.json

Layer set complete for 4-layer, top-side assembly: F/In1/In2/B copper, F/B mask, F paste, F/B silk, Edge_Cuts (Profile), PTH and NPTH Excellon, job file. The B silk holds only clear flashes, so L4 has no silkscreen, as SPEC requires

Gerbers consistent with the board: F.Cu 638 flashes = 272 vias + 366 pads; B.Cu/In2 285 = 272 vias + 9 E1 + 4 slots; B.Cu has 10 regions = 9 electrodes + L4 GND; F.Cu has 16 regions = the 16 L1 GND pieces; In2 has 17 = the L3 GND pieces

Drill files: PTH T1 0.3 x 272 (vias), T2 0.3 x 9 (E1), T3 0.8 x 4 G85 slots (J1 shell); NPTH 0.6 x 2 (J1 pegs, HRO Ø0.60), 0.9 x 2 (SW1 bosses, Alps 2-Ø0.9), 1.6 x 2 (H1, H2). All NPTH are at least JLC's 0.5 mm minimum
Board outline: one closed valid polygon, 54.45 x 39.65 mm (KiCad 122.8-177.2 x 80-119.6), no internal cutouts. Bottom notches are r 2.9 about the bosses (KiCad 125.3/174.7, 117.15), matching SPEC 6

DRC rerun with kicad-cli 8.0.9 on a scratch copy: 32 warnings (15 silk_edge, 11 silk_overlap, 6 silk_over_copper), 0 errors, 0 unconnected, same as drc.json. No rule severities are hidden except missing_courtyard, npth/pth_inside_courtyard and footprint_type_mismatch (ignore)

All 32 DRC silkscreen warnings reviewed against drc.rpt: each is outline or label silk at the board edge or over pads. JLC clips silk at the edge and removes it from pads; no copper, mask or assembly effect
Track widths: minimum 0.127 mm (35 L1 and 31 L3 segments), others 0.15-0.5; JLC multilayer minimum 0.09 mm. OK

Copper clearance per layer, independent of KiCad: no different-net copper closer than 0.0995 mm on any layer; the only pairs below 0.127 mm are the two J1 GND/VBUS gaps (0.100); JLC minimum 0.09. OK (see L1 for the cause)

Vias: all 272 are 0.3 drill / 0.5 pad (0.1 ring; JLC needs pad at least hole + 0.1, 0.15 preferred). Via hole to other-net copper at least 0.2 on every layer (JLC 0.2). Via-to-via hole edges at least 0.30 (JLC 0.2)
PTH J1 slot holes to other-net copper: at least 0.28 on outer layers and 0.3 on inner layers (JLC 0.28 / 0.3); slot pads give 0.2 mm ring across the slot (JLC PTH 0.15 minimum, 0.2 recommended)
Copper to board edge: at least 0.300 mm on all four layers (J4.3/4, SW1.4/5, pours at 0.3005); JLC routed edge 0.2 mm

Mask webs from pad mask polygons (expansion 0): smallest per part U6 0.138, U2 0.22, U5 0.22, U7 0.20, Q1 0.23, J2 FH35C 0.30, U1 0.40, U8 0.418, J3 0.25, J1 0.10. Only J1 is at or below JLC's 0.10 (green) / 0.13 (black)

USB: D+ 15.90 mm / D- 14.91 mm (1.0 mm skew, fine for 12 Mbit/s), 0.2 mm tracks with 0.3 mm gap from U8 to U2. U8 USBLC6 is in-line (pins 4 to 3 and 6 to 1), with no T-stubs except the necessary 0.5-1 mm A6/B6 and A7/B7 joins. D+ uses one L3 hop (vias at KiCad 150.25,115.0 and 145.8,116.3), outside r 17.1 and over L4 GND

Antenna: the rule area covers KiCad x 122.8-128.2, y 91.8-107.9 (device x 21.8-27.2, y -37.9 to -21.8) on all four layers. No track, via, pad or pour fill intersects it on any layer. The nearest copper is U1.36 at 0.30 on L1, vias at 0.65 on L2/L4, and the VBUS L3 track at 0.0 (it runs along the inner edge). 9 GND vias lie within 3 mm. Antenna end flush with the edge, matching the module land pattern (datasheet v1.8 Fig. 14, about 5.4 mm antenna area)
L2 GND: one connected piece (1279 mm2), solid outside r 17.6, hatch inside. No slot or split under any switching net; the only voids are via antipads and the antenna keep-out. No L2 tracks

Reference planes for the SPI clocks: LCD_SCK 18.9 mm all on L1 over the hatch (40 MHz); SD_SCK 38.1 mm over solid L2 and 41.9 mm over the hatch. Same-layer parallel coupling to SD_SCK is small (VBAT 7.2 mm, SD_MISO 3.2 mm within 0.3 mm); LCD_SCK has none. Clock-net vias have a GND via within 2-3.2 mm

Power widths and resistance: BAT_P 0.4 mm only, J4 to Q2 31 mOhm; VBAT Q2 to Q3 27 mOhm; VSYS Q3 to U4 13.6 mOhm, Q3 to R17 78 mOhm; LCD_LEDA R17 to J2.14 31 mOhm; LCD_LEDK J2.1 to Q5 17 mOhm (170 mA gives about 3 mV); MOTOR_P 25 mOhm; 3V3_PERIPH Q4 to J2.9 61 mOhm. All fine for their currents

VBUS 0.2 mm bottleneck (documented exception): the narrow sections compute to 106 mOhm (README 0.1 ohm correct for the narrow part only). 0.2 mm x 1 oz at 0.5 A rises about 4 K by IPC-2221 (README 'well under 10 K' correct)
Pads in pours use solid connection (zone pad connection FULL); pour thermal settings 0.2 gap / 0.25 spoke for thermal pads

Touch wheel on L4: 9 single-piece electrodes, each containing its E1 pad (ring sectors 71.9-77.8 mm2, centre 145.6 mm2). Electrode traces 0.15/0.127 mm (AN3863: 5-7 mil). L4 GND ring from r 17.6 (1.0 mm from the ring). L2 hatch 0.2 mm lines at 1.5 mm pitch (AN3863: about 50 mil spacing); measured fill 0.356 vs about 20% recommended

L3 keep-out rule: no L3 GND copper inside the disc; L3 switching-net lengths inside r<16.6 match the README caps (I2C_SDA 34.5, LCD_DC 23.1, LCD_TE 22.9, SD_CS 12.2, LCD_CS 11.8, I2C_SCL 7.0, BZ_GATE 4.1 mm)

L4 face: B.Mask openings only at the SW1, H1, H2 and J1 holes and the J1 shell pads. All vias and E1 are mask-covered, so the touch face is flat apart from the J1 legs. The enclosure gives those legs 0.5 mm reliefs (mechanical-interface.json touch_side_protrusions; enclosure README item 3). SW1 bosses (model z min -0.5) do not protrude through 0.8 mm
GND pour islands: every L1 and L3 GND piece touches at least one GND pad or via, except a 0.04 mm2 L2 hatch fragment (L13)
Zones were filled in the plotted board (IsFilled True for all 15 zones; filled regions present in the Gerbers)

SW1 NPTH-to-pad 0.075 mm confirmed as the Alps land pattern (C110293 p.3: holes 2-Ø0.9 at 4.25 spacing, touching the pad corners). README's acceptance is sound; only the DFM expectation is missing (L8)
J1 placement against the HRO drawing: slot pitch 8.66 (HRO 8.65), front-to-rear 4.18 (HRO 4.18), peg holes 0.6 at 5.80 spacing (HRO Ø0.60, 5.78)
not_checked: JLC's exact default stack-up for 4-layer 0.8 mm (prepreg and core thicknesses). The JLC laminate page does not list it in text, so README's 'L3 about 0.1 mm behind L4' is unverified
What JLC's CAM actually does with vias that cannot be ink-plugged under the 0.35 mm rule (tent, open or hold). JLC's pages do not say; confirm in the DFM result
The price of Epoxy Filled & Capped for this order (only visible on the live quote, which this review did not open)
JLC assembly edge-rail and overhang handling (J1 overhang at the device bottom edge, SW1 and U1 at the right edge) with 'tooling holes added by JLC'. This needs JLC's DFM
The MPR121 recommended land pattern. The C91322 datasheet extract has no land drawing, so the U6 corner-pad bloat is judged against the footprint's own rectangular pads, not an NXP drawing
Stencil thickness and aperture rules JLC applies (assumed 1:1 from F_Paste)
RF performance of the antenna placement (no copper under the antenna confirmed; housing and battery clearance are outside layout scope)
Impedance values (no controlled impedance ordered; full-speed USB and SPI only)
Thermal behaviour of U3 MCP73831 at 370 mA (power design area); only confirmed its pads connect solidly to the pours
Component placement, rotation and footprint pin mapping beyond J1, SW1, U6 and U1 (other reviewers' areas), and the schematic and netlist
Through-the-wheel touch performance itself (needs a built board, per README item 6)

verdicts.reasoning: I reproduced this from the footprint, the stencil Gerber and the maker's drawing. lib/Harmony8.pretty/USB-C_HRO_TYPE-C-31-M-12.kicad_mod: pads A1B12 (-3.2), A4B9 (-2.4), B4A9 (+2.4) and B1A12 (+3.2) are custom pads. Each one is a gr_poly of 0.600 x 1.300 mm with (width 0.1) and (fill yes). KiCad adds half the stroke width on every side, so the copper is 0.70 x 1.40. jlcpcb/gerbers/F_Paste.gtp defines FreePoly0/1/2 with x +-0.35 and y +-0.70, so the stencil apertures are also 0.70 x 1.40. The board has J1 at (150, 115.47) with GND at x 146.8 and VBUS at x 147.6. The centres are 0.80 apart, so the copper, paste and mask gap is 0.100 mm. HRO drawing C165948.pdf ('RECOMMEND P.C.B LAYOUT'): '4-0.60' for the GND/VBUS pads, '8-0.30' for the signal pads, and 6.40 / 4.80 centre spans (+-3.2 / +-2.4). The intended gap is 0.20 mm. The README 'makers' own land pattern' claim is therefore wrong: the error comes from easyeda2kicad keeping the stroke. A second gap the reviewer did not mention: VBUS A4B9 (right edge 147.95) to B8 (SBU2, left edge 148.10) is 0.15 mm, where HRO gives 0.20. U6 QFN-20: the corner pads 1, 5, 6, 10, 11, 15, 16 and 20 are 0.224 mm polygons with a 0.1 stroke, so they are 0.324 wide. The gap from corner pad 1 (edge -0.638) to pad 2 (edge -0.5) is 0.138 mm, not about 0.188. JLC capabilities (fetched today): minimum pad spacing for the mask bridge is 0.10 mm for green and 0.13 mm for black or white. ORDER.md offers 'Black or green'. With black, the J1 dams go entirely. The severity fits: the joint can be reworked with an iron, but a VBUS-GND bridge on a receptacle is a real paste-bridge risk and the fix costs nothing before ordering.
verdicts.fix: Before ordering, set the gr_poly width to 0 in the four J1 custom pads and the eight U6 corner pads (or redraw them as plain 0.6 x 1.3 and 0.224-wide pads). Refill, rerun DRC, tighten or remove the J1/U6 exceptions in the .kicad_dru, and regenerate the Gerbers. Choose green mask. At bring-up, measure VBUS to GND with an ohmmeter before the first plug-in.

verdicts.reasoning: In the footprint, pads 1 and 4 are drill oval 0.8 x 1.5 with 1.2 x 2.0 pads, and pads 2 and 3 are drill oval 0.8 x 1.2 with 1.2 x 1.8 pads. PTH.drl tool T3 C0.800 has G85 slots from 145.67 Y-113.41 to Y-114.11 (1.5 long) and from Y-117.74 to Y-118.14 (1.2 long), and the same at x 154.33. The length-to-width ratios are 1.875 and 1.5. JLC capabilities (fetched): 'The length of the slot should be at least 2 times of the width', and the multilayer minimum plated slot width is 0.35 mm. The HRO drawing shows 0.60 slot / 0.90 pad widths, with slot/pad lengths of 1.70/2.00 at the front and 1.40/1.70 at the rear (ratios 2.8 and 2.3). The finding holds. It is a DFM and drill-shape risk, not a functional failure: this LCSC footprint is commonly built, and the legs fit the wider slot.
verdicts.fix: In the same footprint pass as L1, change the slots to 0.6 x 1.7 (front) and 0.6 x 1.4 (rear), with 0.9 x 2.0 and 0.9 x 1.7 pads, as the HRO drawing shows. Rerun DRC against the U8/J1 neighbours. If you leave them as they are, expect and accept a JLC DFM comment on the slot ratio.

verdicts.reasoning: pcbnew check of all 272 vias against the F.Mask pad openings (mask expansion 0). There are 13 vias fully inside openings: U1.49 has 9 at x 131.82/133.80/135.78 and y 97.32/99.30/101.28, and U2.25 has 4 at (137.5/138.7, 115.0/116.2). The U8.2 (GND) via at (141.30, 115.60) has its centre only 0.014 mm outside the pad opening, so about half of it is in the pad. A 14th case the reviewer did not list: the 3V3_PERIPH via at (163.6, 102.4) overlaps the J3.4 opening by 0.01 mm. It is the same net and the hole is not exposed, so it is negligible. B.Mask has only 10 pad openings (SW1 x2, H1, H2, J1 x6), so every via is mask-covered on L4. README and ORDER.md document only U1 and U2. U8 is not mentioned. Electrode check: the 6 U1 vias at x 133.80 and 135.78 (r 14.2 to 16.6 from the wheel centre at 150, 97.75) lie inside the ELECTRODE_3 outline (bbox x 133.40 to 142.72). JLC via-covering help page (fetched): for plugged vias, 'No ink filling for single or double-sided pad openings'; the >98% plugging rate excludes vias in pad; epoxy or copper filling covers vias in pad. So under 'Plugged' these vias behave as the design assumed: open on top, tented underneath. The U8.2 joint-starvation risk and the bump-under-the-wheel risk are plausible but not certain. The USBLC6 has a single GND pin, so a weak joint loses only ESD protection.
verdicts.fix: Either order Epoxy Filled & Capped (check the quote delta; it also settles L4), or move the U8.2 via about 0.3 mm toward -X, clear of the pad, and keep Plugged. In both cases, update ORDER.md (it still says 'Tented' and says not to order epoxy fill) and list U8.2 as an in-pad via if it stays. After assembly, inspect L4 over the U1 pad vias for bumps before fitting the wheel disc.

verdicts.reasoning: My own pcbnew computation, from the via annulus edge to the nearest F.Mask pad opening: 13 vias fully in pad, 3 at 0 to 0.1 mm, 97 at 0.1 to 0.2, 47 at 0.2 to 0.3 and 3 at 0.3 to 0.35. That is 163 of 272 vias within 0.35 mm, matching the reviewer's 162. My distance bins differ from the reviewer's (27/111 in the middle bins), but the total and the worst cases agree. Worst case: the DTR via at (138.85, 118.17), 0.020 mm from the U2.23 opening. The next ones are BAT_P at (169.118, 88.018) to J4.2, TOUCH_IRQ to U1.9 and I2C_SCL to TP10.1 (all 0.132), and HAPTIC_EN to U7.10 (0.133). JLC capabilities: 'Filled vias should have >= 0.35 mm clearance from other soldermask openings'. JLC via-covering page: vias 'with a distance less than 0.35mm from the pad cannot be plugged with ink'. Most likely these end up tented, as the design assumed, so function is not at risk. The 0.02 mm mask sliver at DTR cannot be printed, so the via ring will be exposed beside U2.23. That pad is on the same net, so there is no short, but solder can wick away from the pin.
verdicts.fix: Choose Epoxy Filled & Capped, or move the DTR via about 0.2 mm away from U2.23 and add an order remark: 'vias closer than 0.35 mm to pads may be tented instead of plugged'. Then accept the expected DFM comment.

verdicts.reasoning: Alps SKRT datasheet (C110293.pdf p.3) shows a hatched 'Prohibitted area of copper tracks', 2 mm wide, between the two rear mounting pads. Those pads have a 2.4 mm inner-edge gap, which matches the footprint: pads 4 and 5 at (123.55, 83.75/87.45), 1.3 long, inner edges at y 84.4 and 86.8. Sampling L1_GND's filled polygon on a 0.02 mm grid over x 123.10 to 124.30, y 84.6 to 86.6 gives 98% copper coverage. No tracks or vias are there. The copper is under mask and on GND, and pads 4 and 5 (the frame) are also GND. It shorts SIDE_BTN only if the metal under that area is the switched contact and the mask is damaged. That is a plausible but small risk, and it is a deviation from the vendor land pattern.
verdicts.fix: Add an F.Cu rule area (no copper pour) over the 2 x 1.2 mm hatched rectangle at SW1 and refill. It does not affect routing.

verdicts.reasoning: Measured from track segments: SD_SCK is 81.0 mm on F.Cu plus 1.3 mm on In2.Cu (82.3 mm in all), with 35.4 mm of the L1 length inside r<16.6. SD_MOSI has 32.5 mm and SD_MISO 36.0 mm on L1 inside r<16.6. design.py puts no series resistor on SD_SCK (U1 pin 29 to J3 pin 5 directly). firmware/mark-8/components/slab_board/Kconfig sets SLAB_SD_SPI_KHZ default 20000, and a grep for drive_capability or DRIVE_CAP under firmware/mark-8 found nothing, so the GPIOs keep the ESP-IDF default (CAP_2). README 'Firmware notes' item 5 says the SD lines 'go around the touch wheel', which is wrong: they cross it on L1. README line 124 allows that crossing behind the L2 hatch, so this is a documentation error, not a broken rule. The ringing risk is plausible for 82 mm of unterminated line, but the rise time is not specified in the ESP32 datasheet and I did not confirm it, so the consequence stays a risk, not a fact.
verdicts.fix: No board change. In firmware, set the SD clock and data pins to GPIO_DRIVE_CAP_0 or _1 before mounting the card, and step down to 10 MHz if reads fail. Correct README note 5. Log touch noise during card reads (README item 6 already does this).

verdicts.reasoning: The README quote is narrower than the finding implies. README line 191 says 'All the narrow track adds about 0.1 ohm', which covers only the 0.2/0.3 mm sections. Those reproduce exactly: L1 0.2 mm 9.57 mm = 23.5 mOhm, L1 0.3 mm 22.66 mm = 37.1 mOhm, L3 0.3 mm 13.88 mm at 17.5 um = 45.5 mOhm, 106 mOhm in all. The optimistic part is the README's conclusion ('about 50 mV', 'more than 4.6 V'), which leaves out the 0.4 mm track. My single-path Dijkstra over every VBUS segment (no parallel paths, so an upper bound) gives J1 to D1.2 = 272 mOhm and J1 to U3.4 = 293 mOhm. Those paths are about 125 mm long and include 56 to 63 mm of 0.4 mm track on L3 at 0.5 oz. The same method gives U4.5 to U1.3 (3V3) = 199 mOhm and D1.1 to U4.1 (VSYS) = 143 mOhm. The reviewer's nodal 171/178/127/98 mOhm with parallel paths is consistent with these bounds. A drop of 0.1 to 0.15 V at 0.6 to 0.8 A is not a failure: MCP73831 and RT9080 still have headroom from a 4.75 V port.
verdicts.fix: No board change. Correct README line 191 to give the whole-path resistance (about 0.17 to 0.27 ohm on VBUS). On the first board, measure VBUS at U3 pin 4 and D1 while charging with the backlight at full.

verdicts.reasoning: jlcpcb/ORDER.md still lists 'Via covering | Tented', says 'Do not order Epoxy filled and capped', and gives 'PCB color | Black or green'. Its 'Check before paying' item 2, and README item 3, expect '0.09 mm pad gaps' in J1 and '0.12 mm' in U6. The measured values are 0.100 and 0.138 (see L1). README item 3 ends 'Anything else, stop and look' but does not predict the SW1 NPTH comment, the slot ratio or the plugging distance. SW1 NPTH holes: 0.9 mm at (124.6, 83.47) and (124.6, 87.72) in NPTH.drl. The edge of pad 1 (rotated to 1.8 x 0.75, y 83.995 to 84.745, x from 124.6) is 0.075 mm from the hole edge. JLC capabilities (fetched): 'NPTH to Track 0.2mm'. The .kicad_dru already accepts this clearance as the Alps pattern, and that is sound. Only the order documents lag behind.
verdicts.fix: Update ORDER.md: via covering Plugged (or Epoxy Filled per L3), colour green, and an order remark. Update README item 3 and ORDER.md item 2 to the measured gaps (or to the fixed values after L1), and add the SW1 NPTH-to-pad comment, the slot ratio (if L2 is not fixed) and the 0.35 mm plugging comment to the expected-DFM list.

verdicts.reasoning: My own sampling against the L4 electrode fills reproduced the reviewer's numbers. On In2.Cu, ELE8 runs 8.0 mm under ELE0, 3.4 mm under ELE1 and 3.7 mm under ELE2, and ELE2 runs 5.1 mm under ELE0. On F.Cu, ELE1 runs 6.9 mm under ELE2 and 2.8 mm under ELE3. Via positions: ELE8 (150.75, 89.05) is inside the ELE1 outline, ELE8 (151.65, 98.15) (the U6.16 fan-out) is inside ELE0, and ELE2 (147.30, 98.70) is inside ELE0. README item 6 already says 'ELE2 and ELE8 run partly on L3'. The numbers add detail for threshold tuning only. AN3863 sec. 3 says to route touch traces on another layer and keep their area small compared with the electrode, which is consistent with calling this a note.
verdicts.fix: No board change. While tuning, log ELE8 while touching ELE1, ELE2 and the centre, and ELE2 while touching the centre.

verdicts.reasoning: verification.json l3_track_in_disc_mm gives VBUS 40.93, 3V3 41.23, 3V3_PERIPH 28.14, VSYS 23.50, VBAT 20.28 and LCD_LEDA 11.91, and l2_hatch_copper_fraction is 0.356. README line 122 calls the hatch '25 percent' (0.2 mm lines, 1.3 mm gaps), but README line 250 itself reports 0.36. AN3863.txt lines 318-319: 'The X-hatch pattern recommended is round 20%... line spacing proximate to 50 mils'. The README rule (line 123) classes VBUS and 3V3_PERIPH as DC/static. In fact VBUS carries adapter and charger ripple while plugged in, and 3V3_PERIPH carries card current steps through the trace resistance. These are noise sources to log, not design errors. I did not check the reviewer's parallel-plate pF estimates numerically.
verdicts.fix: No board change. Add 'charging from a cheap adapter' and 'card read burst' to the README item 5/6 noise-logging conditions, next to the backlight PWM sweep.

verdicts.reasoning: pcbnew text query on F.Silkscreen: 'M+', 'M-', '1', 'BOOT' and 'RST' are 0.6 mm high with 0.12 mm stroke, 'BAT' and 'M8 SLAB A' are 0.7/0.12, and 'JLCJLCJLCJLC' is 0.8/0.15. The battery '+' and '-' marks are 1.0/0.15 and the BZ1 +/- marks are 1.0/0.2, so the SPEC polarity marks meet JLC's minimum. JLC capabilities (fetched): line width >= 0.15 mm, text height 1.0 mm. I did not recount the graphic segment widths (128 at 0.12, and so on).
verdicts.fix: Optional: enlarge M+/M-, BOOT and RST to 1.0 mm / 0.15 mm where space allows, or accept them as possibly blurred.

verdicts.reasoning: J1 pads 1 to 4 (GND shell legs, thru_hole oval) have layers *.Cu and *.Mask only, with no F.Paste. The F_Paste.gtp aperture list has no shell-leg apertures (only the 0.3 x 1.3 signal pads and the 0.70 x 1.40 FreePoly power pads). ORDER.md itself cites 'through-hole shell legs on the USB-C receptacle' as a reason for Standard PCBA, so the designer expected a through-hole soldering step. What JLC actually does with the THT legs of this LCSC SMD-classed part is not documented in the files, and I could not confirm it from a JLC source.
verdicts.fix: Add an order remark asking JLC to solder the 4 USB-C shell legs, and check the legs on arrival (reflow them by hand if they are dry). Pin-in-paste apertures are an alternative, but they change the stencil and are not needed.

verdicts.reasoning: Partly refuted. 'Floating L2 fragment': the 0.035 mm2 island of L2_GND_HATCH_25PCT at (135.26-135.48, 107.30-107.60), at r about 17.55 on the hatch boundary, has no GND via or pad. It does abut the L2_GND_SOLID fill, though: the minimum distance is 0.000 mm and the shared edge is about 0.2 to 0.3 mm. Both zones are GND on In1, so in the Gerber it is contiguous with the plane and not floating. That item is refuted. The other items hold. E1 pads 1-8 and C are PTH 0.3 drill / 0.6 pad, flashed on In1 and In2, and emitted in PTH.drl as T2 'ComponentDrill' (vias are T1 'ViaDrill'). Their hole edge is 0.277 mm from the L2 hatch copper, against JLC's 'Inner layer PTH pad hole to copper clearance 0.3mm' (via holes need 0.2), which can draw a DFM comment. The gerber zip includes PTH-drl_map.gbr and NPTH-drl_map.gbr, which are harmless but untidy. The gbrjob stack-up has three 0.2133 mm dielectrics, which is KiCad's default and not JLC's real build. The L3-to-L4 spacing that README assumes (about 0.1 mm) is therefore unverified until JLC shows its stack-up.
verdicts.fix: Optional: convert the E1 pads to vias (or accept a DFM note), remove the two drl_map files from the upload zip, and record the prepreg thickness that JLC's order page shows for the 0.8 mm 4-layer default.

verdicts.reasoning: This is not a finding; it records coverage. Checked and correct: HRO land-pattern centre spans (+-3.2 GND, +-2.4 VBUS, 0.3 signal pads at +-0.25/0.75/1.25/1.75) match the footprint except for the stroke error. J1 NPTH pegs are 0.6 at (147.1/152.9, 114.26). Board mask expansion and mask minimum web are 0, and vias carry no mask opening on either side (B.Mask has only 10 pad openings). README/verification.json numbers for the narrow VBUS track (106 mOhm), the L3 lengths in the disc, the vias-in-wheel counts and the 0.36 hatch fraction all reproduce. JLC rules (slot ratio, NPTH-to-track 0.2, inner PTH hole-to-copper 0.3, filled-via 0.35, mask bridge 0.10/0.13, silk 0.15/1.0) were confirmed on jlcpcb.com today, and the plugged/epoxy rules on jlcpcb.com/help/article/pcb-via-covering. Not checked: the MPR121 recommended land dimensions (only the stroke-inflated gap was checked), ESP32 GPIO edge rates (no datasheet figure), a full nodal resistance solve with parallel paths (only a single-path upper bound), JLC's actual THT handling of the C165948 shell legs, the silkscreen graphic segment counts, the coupling-capacitance estimates in L10, and whether the U1-pad via bumps can actually make the wheel disc rock (that needs the enclosure stack-up). My scripts are in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-dave-projects-assistant/7e2488f2-c1f8-48ea-8311-4ecfb642e182/scratchpad/review-work/layout-verify/s/.
verdicts.fix: None. This entry only records what was checked.

areas.title: Mechanical fit with the case

findings.title: ASSEMBLY step 12 cannot work as written: the screen's bottom edge blocks the battery plug from going into J4
findings.refs: J4 (XY-S2B-PH-SM4-TB) at device (-21, -14.93), entry face y -10.53 (mechanical-interface.json battery_connector); screen body; enclosure extras.py battery_plug(); enclosure ASSEMBLY.md steps 4, 6 and 12
findings.evidence: In the mated position the enclosure's own plug model is box x -23.2..-18.7, y -10.53..-8.03, z -6.9..-2.4 (extras.py). Its rear face is 0.19 from the screen edge at y -7.84 (README clearances: 'Battery plug to the screen 0.19'). I sectioned the vendor screen STEP (solid 22, the body, in sources.py device offsets) at x -21.5. The body is full thickness, z -3.15 to -1.0, at y -7.8 and -7.0, so there is no thin glass ledge at the J4 end. The XYECONN drawing puts the contact 2.28 above the PCB with a 5.48/5.60 tall body. A PH housing around that contact must reach above z -3.15 (the model has its top at -2.4), so the plug overlaps the screen by about 0.75 in Z. The gap from the J4 entry face to the screen edge is only 2.69 (y -10.53 to -7.84), and every PH plug is longer than that. So for all of its insertion stroke except the last 0.19 mm, the plug's rear end sits in the screen's footprint, 0.75 into the screen's Z range. ASSEMBLY.md places the screen (step 4) and the board (step 6) before 'Plug the cable into J4' (step 12).
findings.requirement: The assembly order must allow the PHR-2 plug to travel straight along -Y into J4 (JST PH mating is linear; the J4 cavity leaves no room to tilt the plug). ASSEMBLY.md step 12 assumes it can.
findings.consequence: Step 12 cannot be done with the screen and board seated. A user who forces or levers the plug pushes on J4, which is held by SMD pads only (pads 1 to 4), and on the screen's bottom edge. That risks lifting J4's pads (a solder repair on a board meant to need none) or cracking the panel edge. Unplugging the battery later for service has the same problem.
findings.fix: No board change is needed for rev A. Change ASSEMBLY.md in one of two ways. (a) Plug the battery into J4 while the board is out of the case (before step 6), then tilt the board in with the pack attached. I checked the arc: the plug corner moves about 0.0 in Y while the top end is lowered, so the 0.19 clearance holds. (b) Lift the top end of the board about 1 mm, pivoting on the USB-C end and keeping the board on the H1 pin. This lowers the plug top to about z -3.4, below the screen back, while you insert the plug, then press the board flat. Try it on the first dry fit. For rev B, consider a connector whose plug enters along X, or another place for J4.

findings.title: The charge-LED light tube in the back plate has 0.21 mm to J1 and to J3, less than the tolerance stack
findings.refs: enclosure params.py LED_X -5.83, LED_TUBE_OD 2.3, LED_TUBE_TOP -2.9, LIP_GAP 0.15, PIN_D 1.45 in 1.6 holes; LED1 (-5.9, -48); J3 body x max -7.195; J1 shell x min -4.47 (mechanical-interface.json)
findings.evidence: The tube spans x -6.98 to -4.68 and z -8.3 to -2.9. That overlaps J3's Z range (-1.8 to -3.48) and J1's shell (-1.8 to -5.06) at y -48. The enclosure README reports 0.21 to J1 and 0.21 to J3. Tolerance stack, from params.py: the back plate floats on its lip with 0.15 gap per side, the board floats 0.075 on its pins, and FDM XY error is about 0.1. That gives about 0.33 worst case per side, against 0.21.
findings.requirement: The tube must not touch J1's shell or J3's cover when the back plate is screwed down.
findings.consequence: Worst case, the 0.65-wall PLA tube lands on the J1 shell or the J3 cover. The back plate then does not seat, or the thin tube cracks or pushes on the board. The board is not damaged.
findings.fix: Enclosure only. Shrink the tube to about 1.9 OD (0.45 wall), or end it below J3's top (z about -3.6) with a chamfered tip, or cut it to a half shroud on the open sides. Check it on the first print.

findings.title: The battery foam thickness in ASSEMBLY.md (1 mm) differs from the battery-fit model (0.2 mm); the '4.8 mm maximum pack' claim is wrong
findings.refs: enclosure params.py BAT_FOAM 0.2, BAT_TOP_Z -3.15, SPLIT_Z -8.3; README 'Battery fit' (largest pack 52 x 47.65 x 4.8); ASSEMBLY.md parts list ('1 mm double-sided foam tape') and step 12
findings.evidence: The space from the screen back to the back plate is 5.15 (z -3.15 to -8.3). The fit table uses 0.2 foam and gives 4.95 for the pack. ASSEMBLY.md tells the builder to use 1 mm foam. With 1 mm foam, about 4.15 is left. A 4.0 mm 404050 fits with 0.15 to spare. A pack near the published '4.8 maximum', or a 404050 at +0.2 thickness tolerance or swollen, does not fit.
findings.requirement: The documents must give one stack height. A LiPo pouch needs room to swell over its life without pressing on the LCD backlight.
findings.consequence: A buyer who orders a thicker pack from the README table gets 0.65 interference. Even a 4.0 pack has little swelling room and puts pressure on the panel back. That can show as mura on the screen.
findings.fix: Use 0.2 to 0.5 mm foam, or change the README limit to about 4.1 when 1 mm foam is used. Keep buying 4.0 mm packs (404050 or 403450).

findings.title: The U1 antenna has much less clearance in the case than Espressif's 15 mm, from the plastic wall and nearby metal
findings.refs: U1 antenna region x 21.8..27.2, y -35.9..-22.7; copper keep-out ends 0.9 above and 2.0 below the module (mechanical-interface.json antenna); right wall inner face x 27.7 (params X_IN); SW1 body y -17.902..-13.302; FPC fold apex x 18.65 at y -36.6..-41.4 (enclosure README FPC table); bottom-right insert (24.7, -47.15); screen frame from y -7.84
findings.evidence: Espressif ESP32 Hardware Design Guidelines, section 1.4.8: 'A clearance of at least 15 mm is recommended in all directions' inside the housing. If the antenna cannot overhang the board, the guide says to cut the base board away on both sides of and below the antenna. Here the measured distances from the antenna region are: PLA wall 0.5 (1.6 thick); SW1's metal body 4.8 above the module edge; the screen FPC's folded tail and fold apex (GND and SPI copper) about 3.2 to the left of the keep-out and 0.7 below the module edge; the bottom-right M2 insert and screw about 9.7 below; the screen's metal frame 14.9 above. The board's own GND copper continues 0.9 above and 2.0 below the module on the same edge.
findings.requirement: Espressif HDG section 1.4.8 (15 mm housing clearance; base board cut away beside and below a non-overhanging antenna).
findings.consequence: The antenna is detuned and Bluetooth range drops. For a pocket player streaming to headphones, that can mean dropouts through the body. The board works; only radio performance suffers.
findings.fix: Rev A: nothing on the board. If possible, keep the folded FPC tail left of x about 16 and away from the antenna corner. Measure the RSSI and range against a reference ESP32 board early in bring-up. Rev B: move the module so its antenna overhangs a board corner, or cut the board beside and below it.

findings.title: The microSD slot in the case is placed using a vendor-library 3D model that is 0.21 mm taller than the Hirose drawing
findings.refs: J3 DM3AT-SF-PEJM5; lib/model_geometry.json DM3AT z 0..1.891, card_opening_z 0.8..1.881; make_lib.py MODEL_FIX z offset 1.89; mechanical-interface.json microsd card_plane_z -3.141; enclosure params SD_SLOT_H 1.4 centred on -3.14
findings.evidence: Hirose DM3AT drawing (C114218.pdf p.3): overall height 1.68. The STEP the enclosure used is 1.891 tall, and its card gap runs 0.8 to 1.881 above the board, so the card centre is taken as 1.34 above the board. If the real card sits under a cover at 1.68, its centre is about 1.1 to 1.15 above the board (z about -2.95). A 1.0 mm card then reaches z -2.45. The 1.4 mm slot, centred at -3.14, stops at z -2.44. That leaves about 0.0 to 0.1 margin, before print error.
findings.requirement: In the locked position the card's rear end sits inside the wall (lock at 17.55 from the socket rear puts the card edge at y -50.685). Push-push eject (4.0 mm stroke, datasheet) needs the card to slide freely through the slot.
findings.consequence: If the real card plane is lower than modelled, the card rubs the top edge of the slot. The eject spring may not push it out fully, and inserting it is harder. The fix is a front-shell reprint, not a board change.
findings.fix: When the boards arrive, measure the card height above the PCB with a card in J3. Before printing, consider making the slot 1.8 tall (z about -2.24 to -4.04) or centring it on the measured plane.

findings.title: USB-C cable pull-out force is held only by the two 1.45 mm printed pins
findings.refs: H1 (-12, -11.4), H2 (24.6, -40.6), pins 1.45 dia in 1.6 holes (params PIN_D); board bottom edge y -49.6 vs inner wall y -50.15; bottom bosses in r 2.9 notches (0.2 clearance)
findings.evidence: HRO TYPE-C-31-M-12 drawing (C165948.pdf): insertion force 0.5 to 2.0 kgf, removal force 0.8 to 2.0 kgf (up to about 20 N). In +Y (insertion), the board notches meet the full-height bottom bosses after 0.2. In -Y (removal), only the pins resist, plus friction from the press posts. The pins are printed upright, so a bending load at the root acts across a layer line. At 10 N per pin, applied 0.4 above the root, the root stress is about 13 MPa. That is within, but not far below, typical FDM interlayer strength.
findings.requirement: Repeated plug cycles must not shear the pins.
findings.consequence: If a pin breaks, the board can move 0.55 toward the bottom wall before the edge stops it. The connector does not come loose, but the board rattles and the alignment of the card slot and the LED shroud changes.
findings.fix: Enclosure only. Add two or three small standoffs on the inside of the bottom wall (away from the J1 and J3 openings) that close the 0.55 gap to about 0.1.

findings.title: Side button: only about 0.10 mm margin between switch actuation and the cap's stop
findings.refs: SW1 actuator tip (27.46, -15.6, -3.5); enclosure params CAP_REST_GAP 0.12, CAP_STOP 0.42
findings.evidence: Alps SKRTLAE010 drawing: actuator centre 1.7 above the board (matches z -3.5); tip 2.05 in front of the guide bosses. The footprint guide holes sit at device x 25.40, so the tip is at 27.45, which matches the JSON. Travel is 0.2. Needed travel is 0.12 + 0.2 = 0.32 against a 0.42 stop, so the margin is 0.10. It must absorb 0.075 of pin play, FDM error and the switch placement tolerance.
findings.requirement: The cap must press the actuator its full 0.2 before the head bottoms out.
findings.consequence: On some prints the button may not click before it stops, or may be partly pressed at rest. The README already says to sand the inside face of the head.
findings.fix: None for the board. Keep the sanding step, or print the cap with 0.05 to 0.1 less rest gap.

findings.title: The J1 rear shell legs sit inside the ELE5 (play/pause) electrode ring, under a thinned part of the disc
findings.refs: J1 pads 1 and 4 at (+-4.33, -43.76), inner edge at r 15.47 from the wheel centre (0, -27.75); ELE5 B.Cu zone; wheel disc pockets (enclosure conflict 3)
findings.evidence: I ran shapely on the filled zones in harmony-mark8-slab.kicad_pcb. ELE5 copper is 0.127 from both GND leg pads. The GND pour reaches the legs inside r 17.6. The ring runs from r 7.8 to 16.6, so the legs are inside it. ELE5's area is 72.1 mm2, the same as the other odd sectors, so the cut-out is small. Over the legs the disc is only 0.5 thick, because of the pockets.
findings.requirement: NXP AN3863: keep ground away from the electrode edges, or account for the extra base capacitance.
findings.consequence: ELE5 has a higher base capacitance, and the 6 o'clock edge of the play/pause sector responds differently from the others. MPR121 autoconfig handles the baseline; the thresholds may need to be set per electrode.
findings.fix: No change for rev A. During bring-up, check ELE5's delta at the r 15 to 17 edge, and give ELE5 its own touch and release thresholds if needed.

findings.title: FPC fold position: the insertion depth assumption and the screen drawing's tolerances
findings.refs: enclosure README FPC table (fold line 25.2 from the contact end, X slack 0.0, insertion 1.3); J2 FH35C-15S
findings.evidence: Hirose FH35C drawing (C2889267.pdf p.1, detail a): the FPC end sits about 1.45 (reference) inside the front face, not 1.3. Per the enclosure README, that moves the fold line by about 0.075 mm, which is negligible. The DLC drawing gives the tail tip at 17.25 +-0.50 beyond the screen outline and the tail edge at 42.99 +-0.50 below the screen. The Y error goes into the 7.2 mm loop. The X error (up to 0.5) changes how deep the tip goes in, because X has zero slack. The model's fold has a 0.2 inner radius (r/t = 1). The DLC spec gives no bend radius. Everything else matches: FPC width 4.80 vs FH35C F = 4.8 +-0.05; thickness 0.2 including a 3.5 stiffener vs 0.2 +-0.03 with a stiffener of at least 2.85; pin 1 at the -Y edge before and after a fold about a Y-parallel line; dual-contact FH35C.
findings.requirement: FH35C recommended FPC: thickness 0.2 +-0.03 and full insertion. Usual FPC practice avoids sharp creases.
findings.consequence: If the fold is marked at exactly 25.2, the tail may stop up to about 0.5 mm short of full insertion, or buckle. A sharp crease can crack traces.
findings.fix: Mark the fold from a dry fit with the real screen (README check 1 already says to dry-fit), and make the fold soft. A softer fold does not move the tip to first order.

checked: Coordinate transform: device_x = -(kx-150), device_y = -(ky-70). I recomputed J1, J2, J3, J4 and SW1 positions from the kicad_pcb footprints; all match mechanical-interface.json (J1 legs (+-4.33,-43.76)/(+-4.33,-47.94), J2 pin 1 (-2.47,-41.1) at the -Y end, J3 card CL x -13.7 = contact 1 + 3.2 per Hirose drawing, J4 pins at y -17.86, SW1 at (25.48,-15.6) rot -90 with the actuator toward +X)

Wheel electrodes vs printed labels: shapely centroids of the B.Cu zones give ELE1 89.9 deg (12 o'clock), ELE2 44.9, ELE3 0.3 (3 o'clock), ELE5 -89.9 (6 o'clock), ELE7 179.6 (9 o'clock), so clockwise from the front. netlist ELEn maps to MPR121 pins 8 to 16 (ELE0 pin 8 ... ELE8 pin 16) and E1 pads. enclosure parts.py puts HOME at 12, previous at 9, next at 3, play/pause at 6, at r 12.2 (middle of the ring 7.8 to 16.6). Firmware wheel.c sector_deg and zones (90 HOME, 0 NEXT, -90 PLAY, 180 PREVIOUS) agree. The disc prints front up, so the labels are not mirrored. The key tab at 45 deg matches ASSEMBLY step 2.
Electrode areas from the fill: ELE1 to ELE8 are 71.9 to 77.8 mm2, ELE0 145.6 mm2. ELE5's cut-out for the J1 legs is small.

USB-C J1 Z: shell 8.94 x 3.26 from z -1.8 to -5.06 and centre line -3.46 match the HRO drawing (3.26 tall, 8.34 x 2.56 opening). The wall opening is 9.3 x 3.6 (0.14 to 0.2 clearance). The mating face y -50.4 is within SPEC -50.4 +-0.2.

USB-C plastic pegs at (+-2.9, -44.26), r 16.76 under the disc: sectioning the J1 STEP shows they end 0.6 to 0.7 below the board top, so they do not come through a 0.8 board. Only the shell legs (to -0.85 in the model) reach L4, and they are covered by the 0.5 reliefs.

SKRTLAE010: actuator centre 1.7 above the board and 3.3 tall match the Alps drawing. Tip = guide boss + 2.05 = x 27.45, which matches the JSON 27.46. The 0.45 guide bosses do not pass through the 0.8 board.

DM3AT: lock 17.55, over-stroke 16.75 and eject 21.55 per the Hirose drawing. The locked card edge is at y -50.685 (inside the wall), the ejected edge 2.94 past the outer face. The card centreline is 3.2 from contact 1.
J4 height 5.501 vs XYECONN 5.48 +-0.1 body / 5.60 +-0.2 overall. Worst case z -7.6, still 0.7 clear of the back plate at -8.3. It sits outside the FPC run zone.

Every part's height is within its zone limit (82 parts, all ok in the JSON; tallest J4 5.5, SW1 3.3, J1 3.25 in the run zone, limit 4.9). Only J2 sits in the strip where the FPC lies flat at z -2.2 (x -2.24 to 5.17, y -41.4 to -36.6), so nothing is under the flat FPC end.

Board outline vs case: x +-27.2 in a +-27.7 interior (0.5 per side); y -10.0 to -49.6 vs interior -50.15 and screen edge -7.84 (2.16 FPC dive gap); bottom bosses r 2.7 in r 2.9 notches (0.2); J3 body 0.95 from the bottom-left boss; locating pins 0.075 radial.

Screen FPC from the DLC drawing and STEP: contacts on the +Z face (z -1.43 to -1.45) and stiffener on -Z (3.5 long, x 40.43 to 43.93), pin 1 at the -Y edge, tail width 4.80, total thickness at the contacts 0.20. This matches FH35C-15S (F = 4.8, FPC t 0.2 +-0.03, stiffener 2.85 or more, dual contact). A fold about a Y-parallel line keeps pin 1 at -Y, matching J2 pin 1 at y -41.1. The FPC entry z of -2.2 matches FH35C (FPC 0.35 above the PCB).

FPC length budget: tail centre line at y -48.43 flat (42.99 below the screen edge, minus 2.4). The slanted route lands about -46.2, so Y slack is positive (7.2 as a loop). The X length is set by the fold mark, so the FPC is long enough in both axes.
Screen body is full thickness (z -1.0 to -3.15) right down to its bottom edge at x -21.5 (vendor STEP section). The top bosses stop 0.45 below the screen back.

Battery: 404050 (40 x 50 x 4.0) at y -3.5 to 46.5, x +-20, 2.0 from the top bosses; 403450 fits; cable bay y -7.84 to -3.5 behind the screen is separate from the FPC dive zone (x -14 to 19, y -7.8 to -10.0); plug wires at z -4.65 pass behind the screen.
Motor seat (-20, -39.5) 10.4 dia: 1.1 to the boss, 0.7 to post PP1, 2.1 to the nearest board part. Pads M+ and M- are within reach.
Press posts PP1 to PP4 are outside the FPC zones and 0.95 or more from parts. The buzzer grille is centred on BZ1 (-3.6, -21.6). BOOT and RESET (SW2, SW3) are reachable with the back plate off.

Bottom mask (B_Mask gerber) has openings only at the NPTH holes, the SW1 guide holes and the J1 legs. All vias, including the U1 and U2 in-pad vias, are covered on L4, so no solder bumps on the touch side where the board and disc lie on the skin.
Screws: M2 x 4 ends 0.3 short of the hole bottom in the top bosses; M2 x 5 would bottom out (as documented).
not_checked: I did not re-run the enclosure exact-solid interference check or open the 73 MB board STEP / 85 MB assembly STEP. I relied on the enclosure's published clearance table, apart from spot checks of the USB-C STEP, the screen STEP and the board zones.

Real J4 cavity and PHR-2 housing dimensions: neither the XYECONN drawing nor the scratchpad has a PHR-2 drawing. The plug overlap with the screen (about 0.75) comes from the contact height (2.28) and the enclosure's plug model. The blocking conclusion holds for any PH housing that surrounds that contact.
DM3AT card plane height: the Hirose catalog drawing gives only the 1.68 overall height. The real card Z needs a measurement on a built board.
Board tilt-in insertion (USB-C into its opening while the pins engage at 0.075 clearance): only a rough angle estimate. It needs a dry fit.

Antenna RF performance: no simulation or measurement; this review compares geometry with Espressif HDG section 1.4.8 only. The ESP32-PICO-MINI-02 datasheet's own keep-out figure was not read (figure only).
FPC minimum bend radius: the DLC spec gives none, so the 0.2 inner-radius fold is judged only against general FPC practice.
Touch sensitivity through 1.0 mm black PLA, and noise from the FPC leg and loop running under the wheel through the L2 hatch: an electrical question for the touch review, not measured.
Print tolerances (Bambu A1 XY and Z error, PETG vs PLA shrink) were assumed at about 0.1 mm; nothing has been printed yet.

verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced from primary sources. (1) Screen: I sectioned the vendor STEP (reference/DLC-T2.7DDS1.step, solid 22 'body', with the sources.py offsets) using cadquery 2.8.0 at x -23.0, -21.5 and -19.0. The body back face is at z -3.15 at y -7.8, -7.5, -7.0, -6.0 and -4.0. It is full thickness (z -3.15 to -1.0) to y -7.0, so there is no thin ledge at the J4 end. The DLC drawing gives outline thickness 2.15 +-0.10. (2) J4: mechanical-interface.json battery_connector gives entry face y -10.53, z range -1.8 to -7.301 and cable entry direction (0,1). The XYECONN drawing (C54582899.pdf) gives a header height of 5.48/5.60 and the contact 2.28 +-0.1 above the PCB, which is z about -4.08. A PH plug housing about 4.5 tall (my recollection of the JST PHR size; not confirmed from a JST drawing) has to fit inside the 5.5 header around that contact, so its PCB-side face is at z -2.8 or higher. That is above the screen back at -3.15 for any plausible housing, and the enclosure model puts it at -2.4. (3) Y: the gap from the J4 face to the screen edge is 2.69 (-10.53 to -7.84), and the modelled mated plug leaves 0.19 (README clearance table 'Battery plug to the screen 0.19'). The insertion stroke of any PH plug is several mm, so during insertion the plug's rear end lies over the screen footprint while it overlaps the screen in Z. To clear the screen, the plug would have to stay tilted about 7 to 16 degrees for almost the whole stroke inside a close-fitting cavity, which is not practical. (4) ASSEMBLY.md puts the screen at step 4 and the board at step 6, before 'Plug the cable into J4' at step 12. So step 12 is impossible as written, and forcing it loads J4's SMD pads and the panel edge. Severity minor is right: the fix is only a change to the procedure. Fix (a) holds: if the board is tilted in with the plug already mated, the plug's top-rear corner moves toward -Y, away from the screen (about 0.6*sin(theta), with the pivot at the USB end), so the 0.19 clearance does not close.
verdicts.fix: Change ASSEMBLY.md: mate the battery plug in J4 before step 6 (check polarity first, which means moving step 11 before step 6). Then tilt the board in with the pack hanging, and lay the pack on the foam after the FPC steps. Unplugging the battery for service needs the board lifted the same way; say so in the doc. Another order that also works is board and plug first, then lower the screen straight into its pocket (0.19 clearance). Rev B: an X-entry or top-entry battery connector, or move J4 so its plug path does not cross the screen footprint.

verdicts.reasoning: params.py: LED_X -5.83, LED_TUBE_OD 2.3, so the tube spans x -6.98 to -4.68. The tube runs from the plate (z -8.3) to LED_TUBE_TOP -2.9. mechanical-interface.json: J3 body x max -7.195, z -1.8 to -3.48 (connector_height 1.68). J1 shell x min -4.47, z -1.8 to -5.06. J1 body y -50.4 to -43.05 and J3 body y -49.095 to -33.135 both include LED y -48. The gaps are 0.215 and 0.21, matching the enclosure README clearances ('LED shroud tube to J1 0.21 / to J3 0.21'). Location: LIP_GAP 0.15 per side is the only XY location of the back plate (the screw holes are 2.4 for M2). The board has 0.075 radial play on the pins (PIN_D 1.45 in 1.6 holes). The worst-case sum with about 0.1 of FDM error is about 0.33, which is more than 0.21. The RSS is about 0.20, so contact is marginal, not certain. The J1 side is an obround shell, so a misaligned tube would cam off it. The J3 side is the flat back face of the cover at z -3.48, and the tube top at -2.9 passes 0.58 beyond it. A misalignment toward -X therefore gives a hard stop that keeps the plate 0.58 short of seating. The board is not damaged. This is enclosure-only.
verdicts.fix: Enclosure only: reduce the tube OD to about 1.9, or end it at z of about -3.6 (below J3's back face) with a chamfered tip, or cut the tube away on the J3 and J1 sides. Otherwise trim it with a knife at the first dry fit.

verdicts.reasoning: params.py BAT_FOAM = 0.2, BAT_TOP_Z -3.15, SPLIT_Z -8.3, BAT_MAX thickness 4.8. extras.largest_battery gives z_space = -3.15 - 0.2 + 8.3 = 4.95, and the enclosure README battery table says 'less 0.2 foam' and a largest pack of 4.8. ASSEMBLY.md's parts list says '1 mm double-sided foam tape (a 35 x 45 piece for the battery)', and step 12 says 'Stick 1 mm foam tape on the back of the screen.' With 1 mm foam, 5.15 - 1.0 = 4.15 is left. A 4.0 404050 fits with 0.15 to spare. A 4.8 pack does not fit. The DLC drawing's thickness tolerance of 2.15 +-0.10 can take another 0.1 off. So the README's 4.8 maximum is valid only with 0.2 foam, and the two documents contradict each other. Foam does compress, but that pressure then goes into the panel back. The swelling margin for a 4.0 pack on 1 mm foam is small.
verdicts.fix: Make the documents agree. Either use 0.2 to 0.5 mm foam (or adhesive dots) in ASSEMBLY.md, or keep the 1 mm foam and state a pack limit of about 4.0 in the README battery table. Buy 4.0 mm packs (404050 or 403450).

verdicts.reasoning: The HDG quote is verified (espressif/hdg.txt, section 1.4.8 'General Principles of PCB Layout for Modules', p.27): 'Then cut off the base board on both sides of the antenna and below it...' and 'A clearance of at least 15 mm is recommended in all directions.' Geometry: the JSON antenna region is x 21.8 to 27.2, y -35.9 to -22.7, and the copper keep-out is y -37.9 to -21.8. The board outline continues at x 27.2 above and below the module, so the antenna is flush with the edge and does not overhang, and the board is not cut away beside it. params X_IN 27.7 puts the PLA wall 0.5 from the antenna end. SW1 body y -17.902 is 4.8 above the module edge at -22.7. The bottom-right insert at (24.7, -47.15), r 1.6, is about 9.7 below. The FPC fold apex at x 18.65 (enclosure README FPC table) is about 3.2 left of the keep-out, and its z is on the back plate, about 6 behind the board. The board README only says 'Espressif recommends no metal near the antenna' and does not accept the 15 mm or board-cut guidance as an exception, so this is not known_accepted. In a 58.6 mm pocket device the 15 mm recommendation cannot be met. The effect is reduced range, not a failure, so minor is correct.
verdicts.fix: Rev A: no board change. Keep the FPC fold and loop as far from the antenna corner as the route allows. Early in bring-up, compare BT RSSI and range in the closed case against an open board and a reference ESP32 dev board. Rev B: let the antenna overhang the board edge, or cut the board beside and below it as HDG 1.4.8 says.

verdicts.reasoning: The Hirose DM3AT drawing (C114218.pdf p.3, side view) gives an overall height of 1.68. lib/model_geometry.json gives the DM3AT-SF-PEJM5 STEP as z 0 to 1.891 with card_opening_z 0.8 to 1.881, and make_lib.py MODEL_FIX sets a z offset of 1.89. The X and Y sizes of the model match the drawing (13.85 and 15.96 against 13.85 and 15.95), but Z is 0.21 too tall. A free gap whose top is at 1.881 cannot exist under a 1.68 cover, so the card plane in mechanical-interface.json (z -3.141, 1.341 above the board) must be too far from the board. With a 1.0 card under a 1.68 cover of about 0.1 sheet, the card centre is about 1.08 above the board or less, so its board-side face is about 0.58 or less above the board. The slot (SD_SLOT_H 1.4 centred on -3.141) has its board-side edge 0.641 above the board, about 0.06 of interference at nominal. The reviewer's 0.0 to 0.1 margin is slightly optimistic, and the direction is right. The real card height is not in the drawing, so the exact amount needs a measurement. The card is cantilevered beyond the connector face at the slot, so a rub adds friction to the weak push-push eject spring rather than locking it.
verdicts.fix: Enclosure only: before printing the front shell, grow the slot toward the board side (for example z -2.15 to -3.84, or 1.8 tall centred near -3.0). Better, measure the card height above the PCB with a card in J3 on a real board and centre the slot on that value.

verdicts.reasoning: The central claim, that in -Y (removal) only the pins resist and a broken pin lets the board move 0.55 to the wall, misreads the outline. From the board outline in mechanical-interface.json, each bottom-corner notch is an arc of r 2.900 about the boss centre (+-24.7, -47.15). Points (-27.2,-45.68), (-24.645,-44.251), (-21.802,-47.254) and (-23.148,-49.6) are all at 2.90. The arc spans about 150 deg through 90 deg (top, y -44.25) down to -58 deg on the inner side. parts.py builds the bottom bosses at BOSS_D 5.4 (r 2.7) full height from z -7.7 to the skin, plus boss_fill, so they pass through the board's thickness. When the board is pulled toward -Y by the plug, the top of the arc meets the top of the boss (-44.45) after 0.20, so the bosses stop removal. In +Y, the inner lower arc at -58 deg meets the boss after about 0.24. So both directions have a full-height plastic backstop at about 0.2, not 0.55. The datasheet values are right: C165948.pdf gives insertion 0.5 to 2.0 kgf and removal 0.8 to 2.0 kgf. The pins (0.075 radial) do carry the force first. My own check of the root stress for 10 N per pin at 0.4 mm lever is about 13 MPa bending and 6 MPa shear, about half of typical PLA interlayer strength, which agrees with the reviewer's number. Even if a pin fails, the bosses limit motion to 0.2, so the 'rattle and misalignment' consequence and the bottom-wall standoff fix are not needed.
verdicts.fix: No change needed. Optionally, if pin breakage is seen after many plug cycles, reduce the notch clearance to the bosses from 0.2 to about 0.1 so the bosses share the load sooner.
