verdicts.reasoning: Verified: params CAP_REST_GAP 0.12 and CAP_STOP 0.42 (the comment says 'gap 0.12 + switch travel 0.2 + 0.1 for print tolerance'). Alps SKRTLAE010 travel is 0.2 mm (C110293.pdf, basic information). JSON actuator tip is (27.46, -15.6, -3.5), centre 1.7 above the board. The enclosure README conflict 6 gives the same 0.1 budget, and 'Check on the first print' item 4 says: 'It should click before the head bottoms out. If it does not, sand the inside face of the head.' The reviewer's fix is exactly that. One correct addition: the board's 0.075 X play on the pins can take most of the 0.1 budget, leaving about 0.025 in the worst direction. The opposite case also matters. At nominal the cap stop is 0.1 past full switch travel (README: 'plunger past the actuator rest tip 0.30, switch travel 0.2'). So a hard press bottoms SW1 before the cap reaches its stop, and the finger force goes into SW1 and its pads. I could not confirm a maximum static load for SKRTLAE010.
verdicts.fix: Keep README check 4 (sand the head if it does not click). If the click is weak, print the cap with 0.05 less rest gap. Consider reducing CAP_STOP so the cap, not SW1, takes a hard press.

verdicts.reasoning: I parsed the B.Cu filled zones in harmony-mark8-slab.kicad_pcb with shapely (device x = pcb x - 150, y = 70 - pcb y; J1 at (150, 115.47) maps to (0, -45.47)). J1 pads 1 and 4 are thru-hole ovals 1.2 x 2.0 at local (+-4.33, -1.71), device (+-4.33, -43.76). Their nearest point to the wheel centre (0, -27.75) is at r 15.6 (the reviewer said 15.47), inside RING_R (7.8, 16.6) from design.py. The nearest ELE5 copper is 0.127 from both pads, and GND copper touches the pads. ELE5 is sector 5, whose SECTOR_ANGLES value is -90 deg (6 o'clock). Zone areas: ELE5 72.12, ELE3 72.49, ELE4 72.41, ELE6 71.91, ELE7 72.9 mm2. So the cut-out is small, but the GND legs sit inside the outer edge of the play/pause sector. The pockets that leave the disc 0.5 thick over the legs are in enclosure README conflict 3.
verdicts.fix: No change for rev A. In bring-up, log ELE5's baseline and delta at its outer 6 o'clock edge, and give ELE5 its own touch and release thresholds if needed.

verdicts.reasoning: FH35C drawing (C2889267.pdf p.1, detail a at 25:1): the FPC end sits about (1.45) as a reference value from the front face, and the 4.2 body depth matches the JSON J2 body x -6.438 to -2.238. params FPC_INSERT is 1.3. Enclosure README decision 9 says each 0.1 of error moves the fold line 0.05, so the fold shifts about 0.075, which is negligible. The README already lists the insertion depth as an open risk. DLC mechanical drawing (reference PNG): tail tip 17.25 +-0.50 beyond the outline, tail edge 42.99 +-0.50, tail width 4.80 +-0.1, FPC 0.20 +-0.03, stiffener 3.50 +-0.30. These match the reviewer's quotes. The enclosure README FPC table gives X slack 0.0 and fold inner radius 0.2. If the fold is marked from the contact end, a +-0.5 length error between the screen and the fold must go into the X run, so the tip can stop short or the tail can buckle. README check 1 already asks for a dry fit before printing the back plate.
verdicts.fix: At the dry fit, mark the fold position on the real screen rather than at exactly 25.2, check full insertion under the latch, and make a soft fold, not a crease.

areas.title: Firmware against hardware

findings.title: Q4 turns 3V3_PERIPH on at every chip reset: GPIO13 has an internal pull-down at reset that beats R13
findings.refs: netlist.xml: PERIPH_EN_N = U1 pin 20 (IO13) -> R14 10k -> PERIPH_GATE (Q4 G, R13 100k to /3V3, C18 100nF to /3V3); hardware README 'Power' bullet 5 ('R13 holds it off at reset'); firmware components/slab_board/slab_board.c slab_board_init() (returns with 'outputs left alone' when the identity check fails)
findings.evidence: ESP32 TRM v5.9 Table 6.10-1 (IO_MUX Pin Summary): GPIO13/MTCK reset value 2 = IE=1, WPD=1 (internal pull-down). ESP32 datasheet: RPD = 45 kOhm typ (no min/max given). Gate voltage at reset = 3.3 x (45k+10k)/(100k+45k+10k) = 1.17 V, so Vgs = -2.13 V (-1.74 V even if RPD were 80k, -2.36 V at 30k). AO3401A datasheet (C15127): VGS(th) -0.5/-0.9/-1.3 V, RDS(on) < 85 mOhm at -2.5 V. Q4 is therefore fully on whenever GPIO13 is in its reset state. Calculations in scratch review-work/firmware-hw/calcs.txt.
findings.requirement: README 'Power': 'R13 holds it off at reset'; SPEC 5.3 and README Power note 1: the screen and card rail is switched under firmware control; the firmware docs assume Q4 is off until slab_periph_on().
findings.consequence: 3V3_PERIPH (screen VCC/IOVCC, card VDD) is on from reset release until slab_board_init() runs: ROM, bootloader, the 2 MB PSRAM memory test, app start. It is also on for the whole of every download-mode and flashing session, probably while EN is held low, and permanently if slab_board_init() refuses the board (for example, a CONFIG_SLAB_EXPECTED_MAC mismatch) or any other firmware runs. This causes no damage: the parts are powered, so nothing is back-powered, and deep sleep is unaffected because GPIO13 is RTC-held high through the sleep and the wake. But the README statement is wrong. The panel powers up with RESX floating, because GPIO32 has no reset pull. The player turns Q4 off in slab_board_init() and on again tens of ms later, so the card sees a partial dip instead of a clean power cycle. bench_storage's CMD0 wrapper mitigates this. The extra load also falls during brown-out reset loops.
findings.fix: Choose one. (a) BOM-only change for rev A: R13 4.7k, R14 1k, C18 1 uF. The Vgs at reset becomes -0.31 V (-0.43 V if RPD = 30k), so Q4 is off. GPIO13 driven low gives Vgs -2.72 V, so Q4 is on. The ramp tau is 0.82 ms (now 0.91 ms). The cost is 0.58 mA only while the peripherals are on. Re-check the inrush with the new C18. (b) For rev B: move PERIPH_EN_N to a pad with no reset pull (GPIO25/26/27/32/33, reset value 0). One way is to swap it with LCD_RST on GPIO32, so that GPIO13's reset pull-down also holds the panel in reset during boot. (c) Accept the behavior and correct the README and firmware comments. With (a) or (b), note that the GPIO14 and GPIO5 reset pull-ups (45k) then feed about 60 uA into the unpowered panel and card during boot, which is negligible.

findings.title: Bring-up: a stuck-low side button auto-passes BUTTON, SCREEN and BUZZER (and HAPTIC with a motor)
findings.refs: firmware/mark-8/slab-bringup/main/bringup.c wait_press(), test_button_and_screen(), test_buzzer(); net SIDE_BTN (GPIO38, SW1, R26 100k, C23 100nF)
findings.evidence: wait_press() waits only 3 s for a release ('let go first'). It then treats a line that is still low as a new press, waits up to 10 s, and returns about 10000, which result() reports as BU_PASS 'pressed for 10000 ms'. The next prompts then use the same wait_press(15000), so the SCREEN 'picture confirmed' and BUZZER '3 beeps heard' prompts (and the motor 'buzz felt' prompt) are answered automatically. Only go_to_sleep(1) notices that the button is still low, and reports WAKE_BTN as FAIL.
findings.requirement: The bring-up claims that each block's PASS means that the block works. The screen and buzzer blocks must need a person's confirmation.
findings.consequence: With SW1 shorted or bridged, C23 shorted, R26 open (GPIO38 has no internal pull, so the input floats), or the case pressing the actuator, the SCREEN and BUZZER lines say PASS without anyone looking or listening. The summary still says FAIL because of WAKE_BTN, but the per-block lines point the diagnosis the wrong way.
findings.fix: In wait_press(), arm only after the line has been high for about 100 ms, and return -1 if it never releases. Reject presses that reach the 10 s cap, and have BUTTON report FAIL when the press lasts that long.

findings.title: Screen SPI clock: the default and the suggested fallbacks are all outside the module timing; the Kconfig range allows more than the GPIO-matrix limit
findings.refs: components/slab_board/Kconfig SLAB_LCD_SPI_HZ (default 40000000, range up to 80000000, help suggests 26666666 or 20000000); firmware README section 2 screen row; st7365p.c (SPI2, MOSI GPIO27 is not the HSPI IO_MUX MOSI pin GPIO13)
findings.evidence: DLC-T2.7DDS#1 spec v1.0 p.7, 4-line SPI: TSCYCW min 66 ns, TSHW/TSLW min 15 ns. 40 MHz gives a 25 ns cycle with 12.5 ns high and low, so both limits are violated. 26.67 MHz gives 37.5 ns and 20 MHz gives 50 ns, so both still violate the cycle time. Only 15.15 MHz or less meets it (13.33 MHz = 80 MHz/6). ESP-IDF 5.5 spi_master.rst line 448: GPIO-matrix signals go 'only up to 40 MHz'. The Kconfig range goes to 80 MHz.
findings.requirement: Panel serial write timing in the DLC module sheet; the IDF GPIO-matrix clock limit.
findings.consequence: The firmware README section 6 already lists 40 MHz as a known risk. What is new is that the suggested fallbacks are also out of spec, and that a setting above 40 MHz is accepted on GPIO-matrix pins. If the picture shows noise, the documented fallbacks may not cure it.
findings.fix: Add 13333333 as the in-spec fallback to the Kconfig help and the README troubleshooting table, and cap the range at 40000000.

findings.title: Card SPI range up to 26.666 MHz ignores the card's output delay on GPIO-matrix MISO
findings.refs: components/slab_board/Kconfig SLAB_SD_SPI_KHZ range 400..26666; firmware README Decision 20; components/bench_storage/bench_storage.c (SPI3, MISO GPIO21, not the VSPIQ IO_MUX pin GPIO19); IDF 5.5 esp_driver_sdspi/src/sdspi_host.c configure_spi_dev() sets no input_delay_ns
findings.evidence: IDF 5.5 spi_master.rst 'Timing considerations': limit = 80 / (floor(MISO delay/12.5) + 1). The GPIO matrix adds 25 ns (GPIO_LL_MATRIX_DELAY_NS = 25). IDF calculates with an input delay of 0, so it accepts 26.67 MHz. A card output delay of 12.5 ns or more lowers the limit to 20 MHz, and the SD default-speed output delay can be up to about 14 ns. That last value comes from memory of the SD Physical Layer spec and was not confirmed against a document.
findings.requirement: Full-duplex MISO setup time.
findings.consequence: The 20 MHz default is within the limit for a card delay below about 24 ns. The 26666 setting the Kconfig allows can give CRC errors or failed mounts. sdspi CRC and the CARD block would catch these, so nothing fails silently.
findings.fix: Cap the range at 20000 kHz, or state in the help text that 26666 works only with a card whose output delay is under 12 ns.

findings.title: VBUS_SENSE sits above the ESP32's specified ADC range at normal USB voltages
findings.refs: R29 100k / R30 150k -> VBUS_SENSE (GPIO36, ADC1_CH0); components/slab_board/slab_analog.c (ADC_ATTEN_DB_12); slab_analog.h SLAB_VBUS_PRESENT_MV 4300
findings.evidence: ESP32 datasheet, ADC characteristics: at atten 3 the effective range is 150-2450 mV (+-60 mV), and accuracy is worse above about 2450 mV. Pin voltages: VBUS 4.3 V -> 2.58 V, 5.0 V -> 3.00 V, 5.25 V -> 3.15 V, 5.5 V -> 3.30 V. The firmware README section 6 says only 'near the top of the ADC range'.
findings.requirement: ADC input within its calibrated range for the VSYS estimate that slab_bl_plan() uses.
findings.consequence: USB detection still works because the reading is monotonic. The VSYS estimate (VBUS - 0.35 V), and with it the backlight duty, can be off on USB. R17 stays protected because the 80 percent USB cap alone limits it to 0.8 x 0.273 W = 0.218 W.
findings.fix: For rev B, use R30 82k (5.5 V -> 2.48 V) or R29 150k with R30 100k (5.0 V -> 2.0 V), then update SLAB_VBUS_DIVIDER_X1000. No action needed for rev A.

findings.title: Player arms ext0 even when the side button is still low after 10 s, so a stuck or case-pressed SW1 causes a wake-and-reboot loop
findings.refs: slab-player/main/player_power.c player_power_sleep(): waits up to 10 s for SIDE_BTN to go high, then calls esp_sleep_enable_ext0_wakeup(SLAB_PIN_SIDE_BTN, 0) without a condition; compare slab-bringup go_to_sleep(), which skips ext0 in this case
findings.evidence: An ext0 level-low wake with GPIO38 already low wakes the chip at once. After each boot the player stays awake for CONFIG_SLAB_IDLE_SLEEP_MIN (10 min) before it tries again.
findings.requirement: Deep sleep must be reachable. SW1's actuator goes through the right case wall (README 'Mechanical interface'), so a tight case can hold it pressed.
findings.consequence: Never-ending reboot cycles and a battery that drains with no visible cause.
findings.fix: Do as the bring-up does: if the line is still low, skip ext0 (keep the touch wake) and show a notice.

findings.title: Touch wake needs about 0.5 to 0.8 s of contact with the sleep scan settings
findings.refs: components/slab_touch/mpr121.c mpr121_sleep() (SFI code 0 = 4 samples, ESI 64 ms; debounce 0x5B = 0x22 stays); Kconfig SLAB_SLEEP_TOUCH_ESI_MS 64
findings.evidence: MPR121 datasheet: touch status updates every ESI x SFI = 64 x 4 = 256 ms, and debounce lasts ESI x SFI x DT, which is 512 ms at DT = 2. Adding up to one update period of phase gives 0.5 to 0.77 s.
findings.requirement: The firmware README section 3 says 'a wheel touch wakes it'. The bring-up prompt asks the tester to hold for about 1 s.
findings.consequence: A quick tap does not wake the player. This is not a hardware fault.
findings.fix: Write 0x5B = 0x00 (DT 0) in mpr121_sleep() while the part is in stop mode; the next mpr121_start() restores 0x22. Alternatively, document 'touch and hold'.

checked: Every SLAB_PIN_* in slab_pins.h (20 pins) matches netlist.xml U1 net by pin function (scratch review-work/firmware-hw/pincheck.out); the U1 symbol pin numbers match the ESP32-PICO-MINI-02 datasheet v1.8 pin table (4 I36, 6 I38, 7 I39, 9 I34, 10 I35, 12 IO32, 13 IO33, 15 IO25, 16 IO26, 17 IO27, 18 IO14, 20 IO13, 21 IO15, 22 IO2, 24 IO4, 26 IO20, 29 IO5, 33 IO19, 34 IO22, 35 IO21)

GPIO20 (I2C_SCL) is a valid input/output GPIO on ESP32-PICO-V3-02 and in the pinned IDF 5.5 (gpio_num.h GPIO_NUM_20, SOC_GPIO_VALID_OUTPUT_GPIO_MASK). The in-package flash and PSRAM use IO6/IO11/IO9/IO10 (datasheet note), and the firmware uses none of them

I2C addresses: MPR121 ADDR (U6 pin 4) on /3V3 gives 0x5B (MPR121 DS ADDR table); DRV2605L is fixed at 0x5A with STATUS DEVICE_ID = 7 (DS Table 4); MAX17048 is at 0x36 (0x6C/0x6D 8-bit, DS); there is no conflict

MPR121 setup vs wiring: ECR 0x89 = CL 10 and ELE0-ELE8, which matches ELE0 (centre) and ELE1-8 on U6 pins 8-16 with ELE9-11 unconnected; AFE1 0x90 = FFI 18 and CDC 16 uA; AFE2 0x2C = CDT 0.5 us, SFI 6, ESI 16 ms; ACCR0 0x8B has FFI equal to AFE1, BVA 10, ARE and ACE; USL 0xC9, LSL 0x82 and TL 0xB5 are right for 3.3 V; soft reset is 0x63 to 0x80 and the AFE2 reset value 0x24 matches the DS register map; thresholds are at 0x41+2i; the frame parse covers 0x00-0x26 (OVCF bit 15, ACFF/ARFF bits 15/14 of OOR); the sleep AFE2 encoding of 64 ms is ESI 110; register writes happen only in stop mode

Wheel geometry: the firmware sector_deg {0,90,45,0,-45,-90,-135,180,135} matches design.py SECTOR_ANGLES and the verify.py measured centroids (89.74 ... 134.74 deg). The design.py to_device transform (mirror X, flip the y-down screen axis) is correct for viewing L4 from the front. Clockwise counts positive (cw = -d), and the zones are HOME top, NEXT right, PLAY bottom, PREVIOUS left

MAX17048 registers and scaling vs the Maxim DS register table: VCELL 0x02 at 78.125 uV/cell (raw*5/64 mV), SOC 0x04 at 1/256 %, VERSION 0x08 = 0x001_, HIBRT 0x0A default 0x8030 and 0xFFFF to force hibernate, CRATE 0x16 at 0.208 %/h signed

DRV2605L: MODE 0x40 = standby (reset default), N_ERM_LRA is 0x1A bit 7, ERM_OPEN_LOOP is 0x1D bit 5, LIBRARY 0x03, GO 0x0C; EN is tied high through R12 and IN/TRIG is grounded, as the driver comment says
Polarity PERIPH_EN_N: low = Q4 (AO3401A, source /3V3) on; slab_periph_on drives 0, off drives 1, and deep sleep RTC-holds 1
Polarity LCD_BL: GPIO4 high = Q5 (AO3400A low-side on LCD_LEDK) on; R16 100k pull-down and the GPIO4 reset pull-down keep it off at boot; LEDC idles at 0 and 1000 permille holds it high
Polarity BUZZER: GPIO2 high = Q6 on; D2 cathode on BZ_P and anode on BZ_N is the correct flyback; 4 kHz at 50 percent matches the MLT-5020 4000+-200 Hz, 1/2-duty rating

Polarity side button: SW1 COM goes to GND through NO1/NO2 and R26 100k pulls up to /3V3, so the input is active low; the firmware uses == 0 and ext0 level 0; GPIO38 has no internal pulls, and the firmware enables none

Card detect: the DM3AT detection switch is normally open (C114218 DS), CD_B (pin 9) is on GND and CD_A (pin 11) goes to GPIO15 with R25 100k to /3V3, so the line is low with a card in; the bring-up uses == 0; the pull-up is on the always-on 3V3, so detection works with Q4 off
TOUCH_IRQ: MPR121 IRQ is an open-collector, active-low output (DS pin table) with R11 10k to /3V3; the firmware uses a NEGEDGE ISR, ext1 ALL_LOW, and a stuck-low check before sleep

ADC: GPIO35 = ADC1_CH7, GPIO36 = ADC1_CH0, GPIO25 = ADC2_CH8 (PICO datasheet pin table); 12 dB attenuation; ratios 2000 (R27/R28 1M/1M) and 1667 (R29/R30 100k/150k) match the netlist values; VBAT 4.2 V gives 2.1 V, inside the 150-2450 mV range; both player channels are on ADC1, so they work while Bluetooth runs

SPI screen: SPI2 half duplex, write only, spics -1, mode 0. IDF 5.5 spi_hal_cal_clock_conf refuses only full duplex that needs dummy cycles, so 40 MHz on the GPIO-matrix MOSI (GPIO27) is accepted and is at the documented 40 MHz GPIO-matrix ceiling. DMA buffers are internal (MALLOC_CAP_DMA|INTERNAL) and the PSRAM framebuffer is copied into them

SPI card: SPI3 at 20 MHz full duplex is under IDF's GPIO-matrix limit of 26.67 MHz (input delay 0) and of 20 MHz for a card delay up to about 24 ns; sdspi uses CRC, so errors are detected; the ESP32's two SPI DMA channels serve both buses

Back-power order: slab_periph_on and slab_periph_off set the backlight low, then the lines low (MISO and TE as inputs), then switch EN. spi_bus_free() calls gpio_reset_pin(), which enables pull-ups (IDF 5.5 gpio.c), but only while the rail is still on, and slab_periph_off then drives the lines low with pulls disabled before GPIO13 goes high. The player and bring-up call orders are correct, and bench_storage_mount refuses to run with the rail off

Deep sleep: GPIO13, GPIO4 and GPIO2 are RTC outputs held at 1/0/0. RTC lines are isolated and held (rtc_gpio_isolate disables the pulls in the RTC registers). The digital pads 5/19/21 are held low with gpio_hold_en plus gpio_deep_sleep_hold_en, and IDF's esp_sleep_isolate_digital_gpio isolates the other digital pads. The stack-in-internal-RAM assert is satisfied (display task stack from xTaskCreate, SPIRAM_ALLOW_STACK_EXTERNAL_MEMORY off). ext0 keeps RTC_PERIPH on, and IDF holds the ext1 pad if it is off. slab_board_init releases the holds before reconfiguring

Strapping pins after boot: GPIO2 is low at boot (R20 100k plus internal WPD) and used afterwards as an LEDC output; GPIO12 is unconnected (internal WPD keeps the 3.3 V flash setting); GPIO15 is a plain input after boot, and its card-in boot-log effect is already documented; GPIO5 is pulled up at reset with nothing external opposing it (SDIO timing strap only); GPIO0 has R6 10k
Package identity check: EFUSE_RD_CHIP_VER_PKG_ESP32PICOV302 = 6, read as 4 bits by esp_efuse_get_pkg_ver (IDF 5.5); RTC_CLK_SRC_INT_RC is set, so GPIO32/33 are free for LCD_RST/LCD_DC
LEDC: backlight on timer0/ch0 and buzzer on timer1/ch1 do not conflict; 40 kHz x 10 bits = 41 MHz is under the 80 MHz APB clock
ESP32 errata GPIO-3.11 (80 ns pull-down on GPIO36/39) does not matter here: GPIO36 is ADC only and GPIO39 (TE) is unused, and neither is an interrupt
Bring-up detection, I2C: the scan requires all three addresses, so it catches a missing part or a dead bus

Bring-up detection, BATTERY: compares the divider with the gauge within 150 mV, so it catches wrong R27/R28 or a bad U5; ESP32 ADC error at 12 dB is +-60 mV at the pin (+-120 mV at VBAT), which is tight but workable
Bring-up detection, PERIPH: measuring 3V3_PERIPH through R22 on ADC2 with GPIO25 high-Z catches Q4 stuck on (off >= 400 mV after the R22 drain) or not switching (on <= 2800 mV)
Bring-up detection, SCREEN: init can never fail on a missing panel because the driver is write-only, so the PASS rests on the human confirmation
Bring-up detection, CARD: checks the CD switch level and runs a 4 MB raw read with error and speed checks

Bring-up detection, WHEEL: catches an open electrode (9/9 seen, peak 2x threshold) and a reversed wheel ('turn missing'); it would not catch two adjacent electrodes swapped, but verify.py checks that mapping statically
Bring-up detection, WAKE_BTN and WAKE_TCH: the ext0 and ext1 wakes are checked with stuck-line guards and a timer fallback
not_checked: Did not build either firmware project or run firmware/mark-8/tests/verify.py: verify.py writes verification.json into the project, and this review may not write there. The README's 'builds, host tests pass' claim is taken as stated
The ST7365P controller datasheet was not available, only the DLC module sheet. The timing limits in FW-HW-3 come from the module sheet
The SD card output delay (about 14 ns, default speed) in FW-HW-4 comes from memory of the SD Physical Layer spec and was not confirmed against a document

The ESP32 datasheet gives only a typical internal pull-down (45 kOhm), no min/max. FW-HW-1 holds across 30-80 kOhm. Which resets besides power-on, EN and download mode (for example esp_restart or panic) put GPIO13 back into its pull-down state depends on whether those resets clear the RTC pad registers; not verified
Actual deep-sleep current, the MPR121 slow-scan current, and the touch noise with the L3 crossings: these need hardware
The ESP32 ADC calibration scheme actually burned in eFuse on these modules (two-point or Vref), which sets the accuracy of the BATTERY and PERIPH thresholds
The shared Mark-6 player code (audio, Bluetooth, UI) beyond its storage and pin use, and the enclosure label orientation (verify.py claims to check it)
Q4 turn-on inrush into the 20 uF behind it and its effect on 3V3; this belongs to the power review

verdicts.reasoning:
I checked this against the primary sources.

The design: netlist.xml puts PERIPH_EN_N on U1 pin 20 (IO13) and on R14 pin 1. PERIPH_GATE joins Q4 pin 1 (G), R13 pin 2, R14 pin 2 and C18 pin 1. R13 pin 1, C18 pin 2 and Q4 pin 2 (S) are on /3V3. The BOM gives R13 100k (C25741), R14 10k (C25744) and C18 100 nF.

The datasheets: ESP32 TRM v5.9, Table 6.10-1, gives GPIO13/MTCK reset value 2, which the table legend defines as "IE=1, WPD=1". The ESP32 datasheet v5.3 IO_MUX table gives MTCK "After Reset: oe=0, ie=1, wpd". The same datasheet gives RPD 45 kOhm typ (no min or max) and a pull strength of about 75 uA. That puts the gate at about 1.17 V, so Vgs is about -2.1 V. AO3401A (C15127): VGS(th) is -0.5/-0.9/-1.3 V and RDS(on) is under 85 mOhm at -2.5 V, so Q4 is on. The firmware matches the reviewer's description. slab_board_init() returns ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE without touching IO13 when the identity check fails. In the normal case it drives IO13 high only after app start, and slab-player main.c turns the rail back on a few calls later. The bench_storage __wrap_sdmmc_card_init CMD0 wrapper exists because "a card left powered across an ESP32 reset". That agrees with Q4 staying on through software resets.

One sub-claim is wrong. The finding says the rail is "probably" on "while EN is held low". The ESP32 datasheet column "At Reset" (status during reset) gives MTCK "oe=0, ie=0", with no pull. So while EN is low, R13 does hold Q4 off. The README sentence is true during reset and false from reset release until slab_board_init(). That window covers the ROM, the bootloader, the PSRAM test, the whole of download mode and flashing, and every software or brown-out reset.

No damage results. The peripherals have power, so the IO lines cannot back-power them. Deep sleep is unaffected, because slab_board_prepare_deep_sleep() RTC-holds IO13 high. The SD spec (Physical Layer Simplified v3.01, section 6.4: a power cycle needs VDD below 0.5 V for at least 1 ms) confirms that the short off period in slab_board_init() is not a card power cycle. Nothing fails, so the severity is minor.

Also checked and correct: GPIO32 (LCD_RST) has reset value 0 (no pull), so RESX floats during boot. GPIO14 (LCD_SCK) and GPIO5 (SD_SCK) have reset pull-ups (value 3 and the datasheet wpu), which matches the reviewer's side note for fixes (a) and (b). I recomputed the reviewer's figures in calcs.txt and they agree.
verdicts.fix: For rev A, choose (c): correct the README Power bullet to "R13 holds Q4 off while EN is low. After reset release, GPIO13's internal 45k pull-down turns Q4 on until slab_board_init() drives GPIO13 high". Also fix the firmware comments. If Dave wants Q4 off during boot on these boards, the BOM swap in (a) works: R13 4.7k, R14 1k, C18 1 uF, all 0402 basic parts. Vgs at reset is then -0.31 to -0.43 V, which is close to the -0.5 V minimum threshold when the board is hot. R13 2.2k with R14 1k gives more margin (Vgs -0.15 to -0.22 V at reset, -2.27 V when driven low) and costs 1 mA while the rail is on. For rev B, use (b): move PERIPH_EN_N to a pad with reset value 0 (GPIO25/26/27/32/33), for example by swapping it with LCD_RST on GPIO32.

verdicts.reasoning:
I traced slab-bringup/main/bringup.c lines 113-127. With SIDE_BTN held low:

- The first loop in wait_press() gives up after 3 s of "let go first".
- In the main loop, button_down() is true, and still true after 30 ms. It sets t0 and waits until the 10000 ms cap.
- It then returns about 10030, which is greater than 0.

test_button_and_screen() line 483 then records BU_BUTTON PASS "pressed for 10030 ms". The SCREEN prompt (line 489, wait_press(15000)) returns about 10030 the same way, so line 490 records PASS "picture confirmed". test_buzzer() line 500 gates on BUTTON PASS, so the BUZZER prompt (line 501) passes too, and so does HAPTIC (line 506) when CONFIG_SLAB_MOTOR_FITTED is set. Only go_to_sleep(1) (lines 620-623) sees the button still low, skips ext0 and lets the timer record WAKE_BTN FAIL.

The hardware supports the trigger cases. Netlist: SIDE_BTN joins U1 pin 6 (I38), SW1 pin 2, R26 pin 2 (R26 pin 1 to /3V3, 100k) and C23 pin 1 (C23 pin 2 to GND). ESP32 TRM Table 6.10-1 note "I": input-only pins have no internal pull-up or pull-down, so an open R26 leaves the line floating.

This is a bring-up firmware fault that sends the diagnosis the wrong way. It is not a hardware fault, and firmware can fix it, so the severity is minor.
verdicts.fix: In wait_press(), require the line to be high (released) for about 100 ms before it arms. Return -1 if the line never releases within the timeout. Treat a press that reaches the 10 s cap as a failure (return -2), and have BUTTON report FAIL "held more than 10 s: SW1, C23 or R26". Then SCREEN, BUZZER and HAPTIC skip, as they already do when BUTTON is not PASS.

verdicts.reasoning:
I read the DLC-T2.7DDS#1 spec v1.0, page 7, "Serial Interface Characteristics (4-line SPI)". The write timing is TSCYCW min 66 ns, with TSHW and TSLW min 15 ns each.

- 40 MHz: a 25 ns cycle and 12.5 ns high and low, so both limits are violated.
- 26.67 MHz: 37.5 ns. 20 MHz: 50 ns. 16 MHz (80/5): 62.5 ns. All three violate the cycle time.
- 80/6 = 13.33 MHz: 75 ns. This is the highest APB-divided rate that meets the sheet.

The Kconfig SLAB_LCD_SPI_HZ help text suggests 26666666 or 20000000 as fallbacks. The firmware README line 123 tells the user to lower the clock to 26666666 for noise. Neither suggestion is within the sheet. The Kconfig help itself quotes "66 ns ... (15 MHz)", so the author knew the limit, but the fallbacks given do not meet it.

On the range: IDF 5.5 spi_master.rst line 448 says GPIO-matrix signals go "only up to 40 MHz". The Timing Considerations section of the same document says a write-only device with SPI_DEVICE_NO_DUMMY "can be 80 MHz, even if the GPIO matrix is used". st7365p.c line 180 sets only SPI_DEVICE_HALFDUPLEX, and spi_hal_cal_clock_conf() does not refuse half-duplex. So a setting above 40 MHz is accepted. The panel limit makes it moot either way.

The README already lists 40 MHz as a known risk. What this finding adds (the fallbacks are out of spec) is correct. At 13.33 MHz a full frame takes about 123 ms, so dirty-band updates matter more.
verdicts.fix: Add 13333333 as the in-spec fallback in the Kconfig help and in the README troubleshooting row. Cap the range at 40000000. No hardware change is needed.

verdicts.reasoning:
I checked the IDF side in the source.

- hal/esp32 gpio_ll.h sets GPIO_LL_MATRIX_DELAY_NS to 25.
- spi_hal_iram.c spi_hal_cal_timing() computes delay_apb_n = (1 + input_delay + 25) x 80 MHz. It refuses full duplex only when dummy cycles would be needed.
- sdspi_host.c configure_spi_dev() sets no input_delay_ns.
- bench_storage.c puts MISO on GPIO21 (not VSPIQ GPIO19), so the bus goes through the GPIO matrix, and it passes CONFIG_SLAB_SD_SPI_KHZ to host.max_freq_khz.

With input delay 0, IDF accepts 26.67 MHz. The spi_master.rst table labels that row "Ideal Device". The formula 80/(floor(delay/12.5)+1) drops the limit to 20 MHz once the card's output delay is about 11.5 ns or more.

The card value is the weak link. I downloaded the SD Physical Layer Simplified Specification v3.01 into review-datasheets/sd-spec/. Its section 6.6 (3.3 V bus timing) is blank in the simplified edition, so I could not confirm tODLY from a primary document. A secondary copy of the default-speed table gives tODLY max 14 ns, which matches the reviewer's memory. Confidence is therefore medium.

The consequence is small. The default of 20000 kHz is within the limit, and CRC errors at 26666 would show up as CARD FAIL or mount errors. Nothing would fail silently.
verdicts.fix: Cap the SLAB_SD_SPI_KHZ range at 20000. Or keep 26666, and change the help text and README Decision 20 to say that IDF accepts it only because input_delay_ns is 0, and that it works only with a card whose output delay is under about 11 ns. Optionally, set the slot's input delay if the sdspi API exposes it. To settle the card value, read the full SD Physical Layer spec section 6.6, or put a scope on SD_SCK and DAT0 on the first board.

verdicts.reasoning:
I checked the hardware, the datasheet and the firmware.

Netlist: R29 pin 1 is on VBUS. VBUS_SENSE joins R29 pin 2, R30 pin 1 and U1 pin 4 (I36). R30 pin 2 is on GND. The BOM gives R29 100k and R30 150k, a ratio of 0.6. So VBUS 4.3 / 5.0 / 5.25 V gives 2.58 / 3.00 / 3.15 V at the pin.

ESP32 datasheet v5.3, Table 4-4: at atten 3 the effective range is 150-2450 mV (+-60 mV). The notes say accuracy is worse above about 2450 mV (raw 3000). slab_analog.c uses ADC_ATTEN_DB_12 with line-fitting calibration. Normal USB voltages are therefore outside the specified range.

USB detection (4300 mV threshold) still works, because the reading is monotonic up to saturation. I re-checked the R17 safety argument with the firmware constants (SLAB_BL_R_MOHM 11500, P_MAX 231 mW, USB cap 800 permille, brightness range up to 150 percent). The reviewer's "0.218 W" uses VSYS 4.7 V. At VBUS 5.25 V, VSYS is about 4.9 V, the current is 183 mA and the full-duty R17 power is 0.334 W. An ADC that clips low makes the firmware underestimate VSYS, which raises the duty. Even so, the worst case at the 150 percent config maximum is about 0.24 to 0.25 W, at the 0.25 W rating. At the default 80 percent it is about 0.11 W. The finding's conclusion holds, with less margin than it states. The pin voltage stays at or below 3.3 V, so it is within the pad's limits.
verdicts.fix: No change for rev A. For rev B, use R30 82k (5.5 V gives 2.48 V) or R29 150k with R30 100k (5.0 V gives 2.0 V), and update SLAB_VBUS_DIVIDER_X1000. Optionally lower the Kconfig SLAB_BL_BRIGHTNESS_PCT maximum, or base the R17 cap on a VSYS of at least VBUS_max - 0.35 V when on USB.

verdicts.reasoning:
In slab-player/main/player_power.c player_power_sleep(), the code waits up to 10 s for GPIO38 to go high, delays 50 ms, and then calls esp_sleep_enable_ext0_wakeup(SLAB_PIN_SIDE_BTN, 0) with no condition. ext0 is a level wake, so the chip wakes at once if the pin is still low. Compare bringup.c lines 620-623, which skip ext0 in this case.

I checked whether the loop is faster than the reviewer says. slab_controls.c side_button() (lines 65-66) ignores a press that is still down at boot until it is released. So a stuck button does not cause an immediate 1.5 s long-press sleep. The cycle comes from the idle timer, CONFIG_SLAB_IDLE_SLEEP_MIN default 10 min, exactly as the reviewer says.

A case that holds SW1 pressed, or a shorted SW1 or C23, would leave the player awake about 10 minutes of every cycle. This is a firmware edge case and firmware can fix it.
verdicts.fix: Match the bring-up. If SIDE_BTN is still low after the wait, do not arm ext0. Keep the ext1 touch wake (and a timer wake if touch wake is off), and show "side button stuck" before sleeping. Optionally, record a stuck flag in RTC memory so the next boot does not retry sleep in a loop.

verdicts.reasoning:
I checked mpr121.c mpr121_sleep(). It writes AFE2 = mpr121_afe2_value(0, esi_ms): SFI code 0 (4 samples), and for 64 ms the loop gives ESI code 6 (64 ms). It leaves 0x5B as mpr121_regs.c set it, PUT(MPR121_REG_DEBOUNCE, 0x22), so DT = 2.

MPR121 datasheet (C91322): status updates every ESI x SFI (section 5.x status registers), and section 5.7 (Debounce Register 0x5B) says the status change is delayed by "ESI x SFI x DT". That gives 64 x 4 = 256 ms per update and a 512 ms debounce delay, plus up to one update period of phase: about 0.5 to 0.77 s of contact before TOUCH_IRQ falls. A tap shorter than that does not wake the player.

The bring-up prompt already says "hold about 1 s". The player README (line 167) says only "a wheel touch wakes it".
verdicts.fix: Document "touch and hold the wheel about 1 s to wake" in the player README and UI. Alternatively, write 0x5B = 0x00 (DT 0) in mpr121_sleep() while the part is stopped. mpr121_start() restores 0x22. That roughly halves the wake time, but with no debounce in sleep, noise glitches can cause false wakes (each one is a full boot). Measure the false-wake rate before adopting it.

findings.title: JLC Standard PCBA will add edge rails to this board, but every edge has parts 0 to 0.53 mm from it and J1 and SW1 overhang it; no rail plan and no fiducials
findings.refs: jlcpcb/ORDER.md rows 'Delivery format: Single PCB' and 'Tooling holes: Added by JLC ... JLC adds rails or uses fixtures'; harmony-mark8-slab.kicad_pcb has no fiducials (0 matches) and no tooling holes; part bodies from mechanical-interface.json against the outline x +-27.2, y -10.0 to -49.6
findings.evidence: Board is 54.4 x 39.6 mm. Distance of part bodies to the nearest edge (device coords, from mechanical-interface.json 'parts'): J1 -0.80 (overhangs the bottom edge), SW1 -0.26 (overhangs the right edge), U1 0.00 (right), R1 0.45 and C1 0.48 (bottom), U7 0.50 (left), J3 0.51 (bottom), J4 0.53 (top), LED1 0.79, C15 0.80 (left), SW2 1.10 (top), U3 and U4 1.15 (left), C7 1.40 (left). 17 parts are within 2.5 mm of an edge and every one of the four edges has at least one. JLC assembly terms (jlcpcb.com/help/article/terms-and-conditions-of-jlcpcb-assembly-service): 'Tooling holes, Edge rails and Fiducials are required for PCB assembly orders'; 'for board dimension smaller than 70mm x 70mm or missed edge rail on standard PCBA service, JLCPCB will select a suitable production method for edge rail, for instance, mouse bite method'; 'The distance between the body of the components and the edge of the board must be equal or greater than 2.5mm.' JLC capabilities page lists edge rails as 'Necessary' for Standard PCBA. The layout reviewer listed edge-rail handling as not checked; nobody checked it.
findings.requirement: JLC Standard PCBA needs rails, tooling holes and fiducials, and wants 2.5 mm from part bodies to any edge that carries a rail.
findings.consequence: JLC must pick rail edges itself. The bottom (J1, J3) and right (SW1, U1) edges cannot take a rail, so rails go on the top and left edges, where J4 (0.53 mm), U7 (0.50 mm), C15 (0.80 mm) and C7 (1.40 mm) sit at the break line. Snapping off mouse bites flexes a 0.8 mm board right at those joints, which is the classic way to crack an MLCC (C15 is on VSYS and C7 on VBUS: a cracked one can short a supply) or lift a J4 pad. Mouse-bite stubs left on the edge eat the 0.5 mm side clearance in the case and the 0.2 mm boss notch clearance. A DFM hold or extra rail charge is also possible.
findings.fix: Before paying, choose the rail edges yourself: ask JLC (order remark, or in the 'Confirm production file' step) for rails on the top and left edges only, with mouse bites, and the tooling holes and fiducials on the rails. Snap the rails off by cutting the bites with flush cutters, not by bending, and file the stubs flush. For rev B, keep MLCCs and J4 2.5 mm from the rail edges, or add your own rails and fiducials.

findings.title: The player turns 3V3_PERIPH back on a few milliseconds after turning it off, so the microSD card never gets the SD-spec power cycle and can sit in a partial brown-out
findings.refs: firmware/mark-8/slab-player/main/main.c app_main (slab_board_init at the top, slab_board_periph_power(true) after NVS, I2C and DRV2605L init); components/slab_board/slab_board.c slab_board_init (Q4 off); slab_power_seq.c slab_periph_on (no off-time check); 3V3_PERIPH loads C19/C21 10 uF, C20/C22 100 nF, R22 10k to SD_CS
findings.evidence: After any reset (EN, esp_restart in player_power.c line 135, panic, brownout), GPIO13's reset pull-down holds Q4 on through the ROM and bootloader (FW-HW-1). slab_board_init then sets GPIO13 high (Q4 off) and app_main turns Q4 on again after nvs_flash_init, slab_cal_load, slab_i2c_init and the DRV2605L calls, roughly 10 to 100 ms later. 3V3_PERIPH has no bleed resistor. The only fixed discharge path is R22 10k into SD_CS driven low (about 0.33 mA). With about 20 uF on the rail the time constant is about 0.2 s, and reaching 0.5 V from 3.3 V takes about 0.38 s plus whatever the card and screen draw. The bring-up already knows this: test_periph waits sleep_ms(800) 'to drain the rail through R22' before it measures. The player has no such wait. SD Physical Layer Simplified Spec v3.01 section 6.4.1.2: power-on or power cycle needs VDD 'below 0.5V' for 'at least 1ms'; section 6.4.2 says the same for power-down.
findings.requirement: SD Physical Layer spec 6.4.1.2 and 6.4.2: VDD below 0.5 V for at least 1 ms before power is applied again.
findings.consequence: After a crash or forced restart during a card transfer, the card sees a dip to somewhere between 0.5 and 3 V instead of a reset. Most cards recover with CMD0, but a card left busy or in an undefined state can fail to mount until the device sleeps long enough or the battery is unplugged. The player then starts its recovery UI with no library. The same applies to a very quick sleep-and-wake.
findings.fix: Firmware only: in slab_periph_on, if the rail was on within the last second, wait until it has drained (about 0.5 to 1 s with SD_CS low, or measure it the way test_periph does) before setting GPIO13 low. Rev B: add a bleed resistor (for example 1k to 2.2k from 3V3_PERIPH to GND is too much current, so prefer a small N-FET discharge switched by PERIPH_EN_N) or keep the existing R22 path and the firmware wait.

findings.title: 21 passives have their GND pad fully merged into the L1 pour with a direct via while the other pad sits on a thin track; this is the classic tombstoning set-up
findings.refs: harmony-mark8-slab.kicad_pcb zone L1_GND (F.Cu, connect_pads yes = solid); README 'GND fan-out' (every GND pad also gets its own via to L2); scratch review-work/completeness/tomb.py
findings.evidence: The L1, L2 and L3 GND zones all use solid pad connection (zone 'connect_pads yes'; layout reviewer also noted 'zone pad connection FULL'). Parsing the filled L1_GND polygons shows 21 of 60 two-pad passives with the GND pad perimeter 56 to 100 percent inside the pour: 0402 C2, C4 (ESP_EN), C6, C10, C11, C12, C15, C16, C17, C23, C24, C25, R1, R9, R28; 0603 C5, C7, R7, R30; 0805 C1, C9. Their other pads connect to tracks of 0.15 to 0.4 mm. On a 4-layer board with solid inner GND planes the pour side heats more slowly in reflow.
findings.requirement: IPC-7351 and common assembly-house guidance: use thermal relief on small passive pads that connect to large copper, so both ends of a chip part reflow together.
findings.consequence: A higher chance that a 0402 stands on end (tombstones) or skews during reflow. JLC's AOI and repair step usually catches this, so the likely effect is a repaired joint or, at worst, one open decoupling or EN capacitor found at bring-up.
findings.fix: No action for this order beyond checking the 0402 parts under a loupe at bring-up (C4 on ESP_EN and C11 at the RT9080 output first). For rev B, set the L1 GND zone to thermal relief for SMD pads (keep solid for the U1, U2 and U5 exposed pads) or set the pad connection per footprint for 0402 parts.

findings.title: VBUS has no surge part rated below the CH9102F 6.0 V absolute maximum, and the attach capacitance is above the USB 2.0 10 uF limit
findings.refs: Net VBUS: J1 A4B9/B4A9, C1 10 uF 25 V 0805 at (7.85, -48.5), C7 4.7 uF, C25 100 nF, U8 pin 5, U2 pins 7/8 (VDD5, VBUS), U3 pin 4, D1 to VSYS (C9 22 uF, C10, C15, C16); DRV2605L U7 on VSYS
findings.evidence: CH9102F datasheet (C2858418) section 6.1: VDD5 absolute maximum 6.0 V, VBUS pin 6.5 V; section 6.2 operating VDD5 4.0 to 5.5 V. The only clamp on VBUS is the USBLC6-2SC6 rail diode: VBR minimum 6 V at 1 mA (C7519 p.3), so it starts conducting only at or above the CH9102F limit. MCP73831 VDD absolute maximum 7.0 V; RT9080 VIN 6.5 V (C841192 'Absolute Maximum Ratings'); DRV2605L VDD 5.5 V behind D1. Hot-plug estimate with a short low-resistance cable: L about 0.7 uH, loop R about 0.1 to 0.15 ohm, effective C at 5 V about 23 uF (C1 about 7 uF, C7 about 2.5 uF, C9 about 12 uF through D1) gives damping 0.3 to 0.43 and a first peak of about 6.1 to 6.9 V for some microseconds. Attach capacitance is about 15 uF directly on VBUS plus about 24 uF through D1, against the 10 uF that USB 2.0 section 7.2.4.1 allows without inrush limiting. The power reviewer listed hot-plug overshoot as 'judged low risk, not simulated'; this note gives the numbers.
findings.requirement: CH9102F VDD5 must stay at or below 6.0 V (abs max); USB 2.0 7.2.4.1 limits device attach capacitance to 10 uF.
findings.consequence: Probably nothing on the first boards: the same CH9102F-on-VBUS scheme ships on the Feather ESP32 V2. A stiff cable and a stiff source could stress the CH9102F (and the DRV2605L through D1) by a few hundred millivolts for microseconds. The large attach capacitance can make some hubs or host ports drop briefly when the player is plugged in.
findings.fix: No change for rev A. For rev B consider a 5 V TVS (for example SMF5.0A, standoff 5.0 V) at J1, or a small damping resistor or polymer capacitor in place of part of C1. Measure the VBUS plug-in waveform with a scope on the first board using the shortest cable you own.

findings.title: No ESD protection on the microSD lines, which go straight to ESP32 GPIO5, 19, 21 and 25 at the open bottom edge
findings.refs: J3 DM3AT pads 1-8, nets SD_DAT2, SD_CS (GPIO25), SD_MOSI (GPIO19), SD_SCK (GPIO5, a strapping pin), SD_MISO (GPIO21), SD_DAT1; J3 card slot at the bottom wall opening
findings.evidence: Only USB D+, D- and VBUS have protection (U8). The card lines have only 10k pull-ups (R21-R24) and no series resistors or TVS. The connectors reviewer listed 'ESD on the external connectors other than USB' as not checked.
findings.requirement: IEC 61000-4-2 practice for user-accessible connectors; the ESP32 pins are rated only for component-level ESD (HBM about 2 kV).
findings.consequence: A charged user inserting a card can discharge into the card contacts, and from there into the ESP32 pins. The contacts are recessed and the card body is plastic, so the risk is low, and many hobby designs omit this. Noted so it is a known choice.
findings.fix: No action for rev A. Touch a grounded object (or the USB-C shell) before inserting a card. For rev B, consider 22 to 33 ohm series resistors on the card lines near J3 (also helps the 82 mm SD_SCK edge rate, finding L6) or a low-capacitance TVS array.

checked: Programming and recovery path: a bricked board can still be flashed. USB path: CH9102F U2 is powered from VBUS only, independent of the ESP32 firmware, and Q1 drives EN and IO0 in hardware, so esptool auto-reset works even if the firmware hangs or sleeps. Fallback path: TP5 U0TXD, TP6 U0RXD, TP4 GND and TP1 3V3 plus SW2 BOOT and SW3 RESET allow flashing with an external 3.3 V UART if U2 or J1 fails. GPIO2 stays low (R20) and GPIO12 is unconnected, so download mode is reachable.
Firmware does not lock the chip: slab-player and slab-bringup sdkconfig.defaults set 8 MB DIO flash and enable neither secure boot nor flash encryption, so reflashing cannot be blocked by eFuses.

slab_board_init identity check: CONFIG_SLAB_EXPECTED_MAC defaults to empty (slab_identity.c returns true for an empty string), so a new board is not refused; only package, 8 MB flash and 2 MB PSRAM are required.

Back-power order at every 3V3_PERIPH switch (slab_power_seq.c): backlight off, all screen and card lines low or input, then GPIO13; bring-up test_periph waits 800 ms for the R22 drain before measuring (the player does not, see CC-2).

SD Physical Layer Simplified Spec v3.01 power rules read from the downloaded copy (scratchpad review-datasheets/sd-spec): 6.4.1.2 power cycle below 0.5 V for at least 1 ms, 6.4.1.3 ramp 0.1 to 35 ms, 6.4.2 lines driven to 0 at power-down. The firmware meets the line-state rule.

JLC assembly rules fetched from jlcpcb.com help pages (terms and conditions of the assembly service, tooling-hole article, process-edge article): rails, tooling holes and fiducials are required; JLC adds them for boards under 70 x 70 mm; 2.5 mm part-to-edge rule. Board edge distances for all 82 placed parts computed from mechanical-interface.json (17 within 2.5 mm, see CC-1).
Gerber set has no fiducials and no tooling holes (grep of the .kicad_pcb, NPTH list from the layout reviewer); ORDER.md delegates both to JLC.
Zone pad connection style for all 15 zones (all 'connect_pads yes', solid) and the 21 passives with a GND pad merged into the filled L1 pour, computed with shapely from the filled polygons (CC-3).

USB ESD part placement: U8 sits about 7 mm from J1 and is in line on D+ and D- (J1 A6/B6 to U8 pin 4 to pin 3 to U2 pin 3; A7/B7 to pin 6 to pin 1 to U2 pin 4), so the protection is between the connector and the CH9102F.

VBUS rating chain: CH9102F VDD5 abs max 6.0 V and operating 4.0 to 5.5 V (datasheet 6.1, 6.2), RT9080 VIN abs max 6.5 V, USBLC6 VBR minimum 6 V, MCP73831 7.0 V; VBUS and VSYS capacitor lists from the board (CC-4).

EN reset network placement: C4 1 uF sits 4.9 mm from U1 pin 8 and R5 3.6 mm; the ESP_EN net is 50 mm long (40 mm on L3) to reach Q1 and SW3, which is acceptable with 1 uF on the pin and EN only sampled as a level.

Pull-up audit of every open-drain or floating input on the board: EN R5, IO0 R6, TOUCH_IRQ R11, SIDE_BTN R26, SD_CD R25, I2C R31/R32, SD DAT0-DAT3 R21-R24, DRV2605L EN R12, Q4 gate R13, Q5/Q6 gate pull-downs R16/R20, CH9102F RST internal; LCD_TE is a push-pull output; the only missing one is SD CMD, already reported as CONN-2.

Strapping pins with Q4 on during reset (FW-HW-1): none of the lines that the switched rail pulls up (R21 GPIO21, R22 GPIO25, card DAT3 internal pull-up) is a strapping pin, and the card CLK input on GPIO5 is high impedance, so the early rail does not change the boot mode.

Reflow suitability of the mechanical parts: SKRTLAE010 reflow profile with a 260 C peak (C110293 'Condition for Reflow'); DM3AT rated for reflow (C114218 'Resistance to soldering heat'); MLT-5020 solderability test at 255 C (C94598).
not_checked: What JLC actually does with this board's edges: which edges get rails, V-cut or mouse bites, and whether the rails are removed before shipping. Only the DFM result or a support ticket shows this; CC-1 is based on JLC's published terms.
A scope measurement or SPICE run of the USB plug-in overshoot (CC-4); the figures are a second-order RLC estimate with assumed cable values and typical DC-bias derating.
Real 3V3_PERIPH decay time after Q4 turns off: depends on the screen's and card's idle current, which no datasheet in the folder gives. The 0.2 s time constant uses only R22 and the board capacitors.
Whether JLC's AOI and repair step catches tombstoned 0402 parts on this order (CC-3); JLC does not publish its defect rates.
Battery temperature during charging: the MCP73831 has no thermistor input and the pack choice (protected 404050) is outside the board; not treated as a defect.
CH9102F host driver behaviour on Dave's Mac (it is expected to enumerate as a CDC-ACM device); needs the real board.

The ESP32 module's metal shield and internal 40/80 MHz flash and PSRAM traffic sit behind the ELE2 to ELE4 area of the wheel (U1 x 10.6 to 16.6 is inside the r 16.6 disc). Its effect on touch noise needs a built board; the layout reviewer's L3 covers the in-pad vias only.

verdicts.reasoning: Checked against primary sources. (1) harmony-mark8-slab.kicad_pcb has 0 fiducial footprints, and bom.csv and cpl.csv have no fiducial or tooling entries. (2) jlcpcb/ORDER.md has 'Delivery format: Single PCB' and 'Tooling holes: Added by JLC ... JLC adds rails or uses fixtures'. It does not say which edges or how close parts may be, so this is not a documented exception with reasoning. (3) I computed body-to-edge distances from mechanical-interface.json 'parts' against the outline (x +-27.2, y -10.0 to -49.6, bottom corners notched) and got the same numbers: J1 -0.80 (bottom), SW1 -0.26 (right), U1 0.00 (right), R1 0.45 and C1 0.48 (bottom), U7 0.50 (left), J3 0.51 (bottom), J4 0.53 (top), LED1 0.79 (bottom), C15 0.80 (left), SW2 1.10 (top), U3 and U4 1.15 (left), C7 1.40 (left). Every edge has a part within about 1.1 mm. (4) I fetched JLC's PCBA terms. They say: 'Tooling holes, Edge rails and Fiducials are required for PCB assembly orders'; 'for board dimension smaller than 70mm x 70mm or missed edge rail on standard PCBA service, JLCPCB will select a suitable production method for edge rail, for instance, mouse bite method'; and 'The distance between the body of the components and the edge of the board must be equal or greater than 2.5mm.' So JLC will add rails on edges it chooses, and on every candidate edge the parts break the 2.5 mm rule. Two refinements. First, JLC usually joins rails across a routed slot of about 1.6 to 2 mm, so a 0.8 mm overhang (J1) does not by itself rule out a rail on that edge. JLC may pick the two long edges (top and bottom) rather than top and left as the finding assumes. Second, flush-cut mouse bites put little stress on the board, so a cracked MLCC is possible but unlikely. The realistic costs are a DFM hold or engineer question, an extra charge, or bite stubs that need filing to fit the 0.5 mm case clearance. Minor is the right severity.
verdicts.fix: Before paying, add an order remark: 'Please add edge rails with mouse bites on the top (y -10, J4 side) and left edges, or contact me before choosing. Place tooling holes and fiducials on the rails. Parts overhang the bottom (USB-C, 0.8 mm) and right (side switch, 0.26 mm) edges. Leave at least 2 mm of routed slot and no bites next to J1, J3, SW1 and U1.' After delivery, cut the bites with flush cutters (do not snap them) and file the stubs flush before fitting the case. For rev B, add your own 5 mm rails with three fiducials and tooling holes, and keep MLCCs and J4 2.5 mm from the rail edges.

verdicts.reasoning: Hardware: design.py line 210 has Q4 AO3401A with source on 3V3 and drain on 3V3_PERIPH.
